About CABINET VISION Help

The CABINET VISION Help System was created in order to make your experience with CABINET
VISION more enjoyable and productive. We welcome your feedback so please let us know if you
find this information useful by sending an e-mail to us at tech@cabinetvision.com.
The format of this Help System should closely follow the layout of CABINET VISION itself. Also,
you may press the F1 key on your keyboard while using CABINET VISION to see Help on the
area you are using.
In order to get the most from using the CABINET VISION Help System, it is important to first know
some terms of communication that will be used throughout the Help System.
First, any time that you are to navigate to a specific area of the ribbonbar to perform a certain
function, the sequence will appear as follows:
Main | Help | Help Topics...
This tells you that you should be on the Main Tab, then click on Help, and finally, click on Help
Topics... in order to get to the specified location.

Secondly, it is important to understand the terminology used in describing movements and clicks
of the mouse. See the "Using a Mouse in CABINET VISION" topic for more information on using your
Mouse in CABINET VISION.
On a mouse with the typical configuration, the left button is used as a Select tool. The right button
is used as an alternate select tool. Some mice have a third button or a wheel.
With this typical configuration, if you see the word "click" used in this Help System, that means to
click one time with the left mouse button on the object specified. A "double-click" means to click
two times in relatively rapid succession on the item or object specified. A "right-click" means to

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
click one time with the right mouse button on the object specified. Also, you will be asked to
"drag" objects with the mouse at certain times. This means that you will hold the mouse over the

How It All Comes Together

The core of CABINET VISION is setup in levels. The levels of CABINET VISION are in yellow
below:

When starting a Job, CABINET VISION copies the System Files into the Job Level and they
become part of the Job file. Changes made at any level of a Job will only affect that level and will
have no effect on System Level settings, unless you wish them to. Changes made in one Job will
not affect any other Job. Changes made in one Room will have no affect on any other Room.
Changes made to one Assembly will have no affect on any other Assembly. Changes made to one

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Part will have no affect on any other Part. And finally changes made to one Operation will have no
affect on any other Operation.
When CABINET VISION looks for instructions on building your Assembly it starts at the lowest
level and works its way up. When CABINET VISION finds the instruction(s) it is looking for it stops
and does not look any higher. If changes are made to an Assembly and then changes are made at
the Room Level all Assemblies in the Room will use the Room level changes except the
Assembly that had changes made at the Assembly Level.
Example: If the Doors for one Assembly were changed, at the Assembly Level, and then the
Doors for the Room were changed, at the Room Level, to a different Door Style, all Assemblies in
the Room would use the Room Level Door changes, except for the Assembly that had its Door
Style changed at the Assembly Level.

The System Level

Click on the areas in the image below for more information on the specific area

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
© 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The key to successfully using CABINET VISION is proper setup of the System level properties.
System level properties control the way Assemblies are constructed and the Materials and
Hardware those Assemblies utilize. To setup CABINET VISION, the first place to start is setting up
your Parts and Materials.

The Hierarchy of CABINET VISION

A topic that is related to the Hierarchy of CABINET VISION is the concept of Global and Local
when referencing the reach of information within your system. These concepts are important
enough that they are mentioned in many places as they apply to a particular subject.

Applying these concepts to the hierarchy of CABINET VISION might be explained using a map of
the United States. We have a map of the entire country, which has 48 contiguous states. Those
states have multiple counties composed of multiple cities. Those cities probably have
subdivisions, etc. That Country, State, County, etc. organization would be the hierarchy of the
country. Now, if a change is made to a Global law, say a law covering the entire United States, it
applies to all the lesser divisions below it, even the lowest subdivisions.

Let's assume King County, in California passes a law outlawing raising cattle. That would be a
local law, and it would have no reach to a neighboring county, another state, etc. However it would
effect the cities within it. If you look at the United States as the Global portion of CABINET
VISION, and a State as the Job portion of CABINET VISION, and the entering of data in your
databases as the equivalent to the laws in the above example, then the Global, or Local reach
within the hierarchy. A Setup modification made to your databases, (construction, schedules, etc)
would have maximum reach over all future Jobs. Those changes would not be required of existing
Jobs. However, if they were such great changes that the existing Jobs would benefit from them,
then those changes can be IMPORTED into CABINET VISION. If on the other hand, something
less than a State, say a County in our example, then we would need to do so without effecting
other neighboring counties. A county here would be like a Room in CABINET VISION. The ability
to freely change Rooms to be different from other Rooms, in Material and Construction is
necessary for those instances when you have an oak kitchen, with a cherry dining room, with a
plastic laminate laundry room, and melamine garage cabinets in the same Job. By organizing
each of these portions of the project into the appropriate Room, you have guaranteed that the
Material, the Construction, the hardware, the Counter Tops, etc are unique and particular to that
area.

Shows the orientation of the drawing. CABINET VISION drawings are superimposed on an
invisible grid, or coordinate system. Coordinate systems are based on X, Y, and (for 3D) Z

drawing orientation, this Axis Indicator is displayed in the lower-left corner of the drawing area.

· Click to specify locations

· Click to cancel an event

   control the Zoom Factor and Scroll Direction.

· Double click to Zoom All

· Drag to Pan view

A Scroll Wheel Mouse is typically a two-button mouse with a small wheel between the buttons.
The left and right buttons behave the same as they do on a standard mouse. You can rotate the
wheel by discrete values. You can use the wheel to zoom and pan in your drawing without using
any CABINET VISION tools.

The following table lists the mouse actions supported with a Scroll Wheel Mouse in CABINET
VISION.

To...                    Do this...
Zoom In or Out           Rotate the wheel forward to Zoom In, backward to Zoom Out.
Zoom All                 Double-Click the Scroll Wheel button
Pan                      Drag the Scroll Wheel button

Object Snapping

CABINET VISION provides a special kind of cursor snap in addition to the typical grid snap. This
allows the cursor to automatically snap to different hot-points on or adjacent to an object; for
example, end-points, mid-points, center-points, and intersections. These locations are commonly
referenced when creating or editing geometry. For most functions, the cursor will also snap to the
origin of the object.

       For example, you may want to create a line that is connected to the end of an arc. Start
       creating the line by locating the endpoint of the arc. When located, a round hot-point marker
       appears on the arc endpoint.

                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Click the hot-point marker to start the line there. The start of the line snaps precisely to the
       end of the arc, connecting these objects end-to-end.
You can choose what types of positions and conditions will automatically be located by enabling or
disabling options in Preferences | Tools.

General Snapping Shortcut Keys

Ignores snap to Grid and Points, and leaves the Smart-Lines angle snap on.

Activates the "full grid snap" mode, forcing snap to the Grid over a position just aligned with a
Point.

Completely ignores snap, including Smart-Lines.

             +
Using the CAD Dimension Tool, allows the automatic dimensioning of a CAD object when clicking on
it.

Dynamic Snapping

CABINET VISION also has the ability to Snap Dynamically (also known as Assumptive Snapping).

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
When you are in line with a Snap Point on another Object within the Drawing space CABINET
VISION will project that position to your location. When this projection along with the associated
hot-point marker is displayed you can be assured that the Object will be placed in-line with that
Objects Snap Point.

       For Example you would like to draw two line Parallel to each other. After drawing the first line
       simply move your cursor in-line with the first lines Start Point and you will see a Snap Line
       projection assuring you they are in-line.

Hot-point Markers

When the cursor moves over a valid snap location, the located position displays with a hot-point
marker and a special cursor appears to identify the type of location.
Note: The system will not display a hot-point marker for a particular location type if it is disabled in
Preferences | Tools.
The list below identifies these special cursors:

       Cursor is snapping to one of the extremities (End Point) of an object.
       Cursor is snapping to the middle position (Mid Point) of an object.
       Cursor is snapping to the center of an arc or circle.
       Cursor is snapping to the intersection of two objects.
       Cursor has one coordinate aligned with any of the snap points.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Editing CAD line is extending along the original angle.
       Editing CAD line is snapping to one of the smart line angles.
       Editing CAD line has a locked angle.
       Cursor is snapping to any of the points in the editing shape.
       Cursor is snapping to the grid.
       Cursor is snapping to a Snap Mark.
       Cursor is snapping to the origin (0,0 position) in the view.

Users

In the Users Tab, there is a list of the Users that have been created. When a User is selected in
the list on the left, the Rights for that User will be displayed on the right. Scroll down the list of
Rights and set the level of access that you wish for that User to have for each area listed.
For example, the field labeled S2M CENTER will give you the choice to allow that user access to
the S2M CENTER or not allow that user access. The choices for that field are simply 'Yes' or 'No'.
However, there are sub-areas under the S2M CENTER such as Machine Catalog and Tool
Catalog where you can set that User's access to 'None', 'View', or 'Edit'. Setting a User's access to
'View' will allow them to see that area without the ability to make changes. 'Edit' will allow the User
to make changes.

               It is recommended to have the default user of CABINET VISION user
         name match the Windows login name. Doing so will cause the user that is
         logged into the computer to have his/her user name automatically be selected

Update Version

The progress window shown below will appear during the Update Version process.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The Update Version Utility performs several functions:
       Create Backups - The Update Version Utility first creates a full set of database backups
       which means that you will have a restore point in case there is a need to revert to saved
       database files for some reason.
       Cleanup Databases - This portion of the Update Version Process will take the database
       files and remove any errors that are found.
       Compact Databases - This portion of the Update Version Process removes empty space in
       the CABINET VISION Database files.
       Update Databases - This portion of the Update Version Process will make any changes
       necessary to bring the CABINET VISION Databases in line with changes that have been
       made during the development of new versions and builds of CABINET VISION.
       Register Files - This portion of the Update Version Process re-registers system files used
       by CABINET VISION.

Set As System Defaults

                              Use this function to store the current settings as default values. For
example, if you are entering the values for the Heights and Depths of the different Cabinet
Classes, and you want every Job to have these new values input automatically, click the Set As
System Defaults button when you finish entering the numbers. This will allow the values entered
to appear each time a new Job is started so that you don't have to re-enter them in every Job. The
values may still be modified thereafter.

              System Default settings are stored in the Windows Registry.

              In Job Properties once you Save a Job Template then the Set As System Defaults is no
       longer necessary and will not be displayed.

during backup and AutoSave generation but are deleted once the system has completed the
process. It is unlikely, but possible, that you could restore a Job from a TMP file.

Measurement Units Tab

The Measurement Units tab allows access to the area where your standard display unit of
measure and its precision are set. Keep in mind that CABINET VISION stores everything as a
double integer in the Imperial (Inches) unit of measure. What you are selecting is how CABINET
VISION displays this information not how it is stored.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
A double Integer consists of 15 unit places, meaning a measurement entered as 56mm is actually
stored as 2.20472440944881" by CABINET VISION. The measurement entered by you at 56mm
would display as follows:

Units as Millimeters

Precision as 1 = 56
Precision as 1.5 = 56.0
Precision as 1.1 = 56.0
Precision as 1.01 = 56.00
Precision as 1.001 = 56.000

Units as Inches

Precision as 1 = 2
Precision as 1.1 = 2.2
Precision as 1.01 = 2.20
Precision as 1.001 = 2.205
Precision as 1.0001 = 2.2047
Precision as 1.00001 = 2.20472
Precision as 1.000001 = 2.204724

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Precision as 1/8 = 2 1/4
Precision as 1/16 = 2 3/16
Precision as 1/32 = 2 7/32
Precision as 1/64 = 2 13/64

                      The important thing to remember is CABINET VISION sees this number (56mm),
               no matter how you have the display units set, as 2.20472440944881".
       The "Trim trailing decimal zeros" option, when enabled, will remove any trailing zeros
       when in decimal Millimeter or Inch mode.
       The "Allow unit-switch button on Status Bar" options turns on/off the Unit-switch button in
       the Status Bar Menu.
       You can also set the Angle Precision here from 0 to 3 Decimal places.

General Tab

Following are the options on the General tab:

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
© 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
                                   :Core
CABINET VISION DESIGN

Set the size of the Undo/Redo stack. This allows you to decide how many actions that you can
undo if you make a mistake. The purpose of limiting the number is to keep the system from using
too much RAM and slowing down other processes. If this number is set too high, there may be a
noticeable reduction in system resources (your system could slow down). Setting this Undo/Redo
stack to around 5 is recommended.

Set Auto-Save time in minutes. This setting allows you to decide how often the system will
perform an automatic save of the job that you are working on. If the program crashes for some
reason while you are in a job, an autosave file may be used to restore most of your work. Click
here for more information on restoring an autosave file. As with Undo/Redo, the Auto-Save
settings may slow your system if not correctly entered. For example: if you set the Auto-Save
time to 1 minute, the program will attempt to save your job every minute. While this seems to
create a very safe setup, it will actually slow your system during the save process and this could
actually cause crashing with some very large jobs. We recommend setting the Auto-Save time to
at least 10 minutes with 20 being optimum.

Architecture of the Auto-Save Utility

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 The auto-save feature is enabled by a value greater than zero being entered under File |
   System | Autosave.

 When a job file has been opened -OR- a new job file has been started, the timer starts.

 When the timer reaches the auto-save time limit, an .asv file by the same name as the .cvj
   file will be created in the same directory that stores the .cvj file. Then, the timer resets to
   zero.

 If the .cvj file was NEVER saved by the user, but the auto-save time limit is reached, then the
   .asv file will be given the name, 'Untitled.asv'

 When the user saves a .cvj file, the existing .asv file is deleted from the Jobs directory and
   the saved .cvj file is considered the most current copy. Then, the timer resets to zero.

 If nothing in the job changes since the last save (manual or auto), the .asv file will not be
   updated when the time limit is reached, but the timer still resets to zero.

 IF a crash or any other unexpected exit from CABINET VISION occurs, THEN...when a user
   re-opens CABINET VISION, the program searches for an .asv file in the Jobs directory. If an
   .asv file is found in the Jobs directory, the user will be prompted to restore the job from the
   .asv file.

    · If the user chooses NOT to restore the job from the .asv file, the result is the same as if
       the user closed the job and did NOT choose to save changes. In this case, any changes
       made since the last manual save will be lost.

    · If the user chooses to restore the job from the .asv file, the job will be restored according
       to the last time the .asv file was create, which would mean that some changes could still
       be lost (i.e., any changes to the job between the last time the .asv file was created and
       the crash).

    · If the auto-save time limit was NEVER reached before the crash occurred, the user will
       not be prompted to restore the job from the .asv file because an .asv file was NEVER
       created.

 Autosave file types:

    asv - Autosave for CVJ Job file

    ass - Autosave for Seperate Drawing Scenes

    asr - Autosave for CVR Render file

    asz - Autosave for zipped media files

    abv - Backup of Autosave for CVJ Job file

                                                              © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
        abs - Backup of Autosave for Seperate Drawing Scenes
        abr - Backup of Autosave for CVR Render file
        abz - Backup of Autosave for zipped media files

              See the Job Recovery topic to see how to manually recover an .asv file.

Architecture of the Back-Up Utility

A .bak file is created upon saving an 'active' .cvj file that has previously been saved. The
intended design is to backup the previous copy of the .cvj file (created during the last save)
BEFORE overwriting it with the modifications made in the current session. Note that the
action of saving the .cvj file itself is intended to save the modifications made in the current
session.

Below is an example of how it works...

1. Create a new job

2. Place ONE cabinet on a wall

3. Save the job file

Result: No .bak file is created because this process simply creates a NEW .cvj file.
There is not a previous copy of the .cvj from which to create a .bak file.

4. Place a SECOND cabinet on the wall

                                © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
5.  Save the job file

    Result: A .bak file is created from the last saved copy of the .cvj file that contained
    ONE cabinet (i.e., backup previous). New .cvj file contains TWO cabinets (i.e. save
    modifications).

6. Place a THIRD cabinet on the wall

7.  Save the job file

    Result: A .bak file is created from the last saved copy of the .cvj file that contained
    TWO cabinets (i.e., backup previous). New .cvj file contains THREE cabinets (i.e.
    save modifications).

              See the Job Recovery topic to see how to manually recover an .bak file.

menu, similar to below.

Suspend UCS while Sectioning Assemblies - This feature allows you to suspend UCS's while
in the Section Editor. Depending upon what a UCS is doing it can slow down the Section Editor,
this option is designed to supend UCS functionality until moving to a different view and/or level.

 Use Pair Doors - Pair Doors are two equal Doors in a common opening. In Face Frame
   construction, there will be no Mid Stile. In Frameless, there will be no Partition. Pair Doors must

drawn Line or Wall.

       A Snap Angle of 45 and a high Tolerance (Sliding the bar all the way to the right) will snap
       Walls and CAD lines only in 45 degree increments.

       A Snap Angle of 45 and a low Tolerance (Sliding the bar all the way to the left) will basically
       disable the Snap feature. This will basically allow you to free-hand line and wall drawing.

Snap Lines. In this section you can control the Color and Type (Dashed or Solid) of line that
Dynamic Snapping will use.

Snapping Options. In this section you can control the Snap Hot-Keys as well as which Hot-Points
are on for Dynamic Snapping.

       Grid Snap - Snaps what you are currently placing to Grid points.

       Point Snap - Snaps what you are currently placing to Snap points

       Snap To Corner - This function is designed to facilitate placing a Cabinet diagonally across
       a 90 degree corner. While placing your Cabinet in the Corner use the assigned short-cut key

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       to Snap the Cabinet diagonally in the corner as demonstrated in the image below.

       Pan - The Pan function allows you to set a new View center. When activated the Pan feature
       will center your current view to the location of the cursor on the screen.
       Refresh - The Refresh function instructs CABINET VISION to redraw the current View.

       From Corner - When using this and performing a Zoom Window you specify the corners of
       your Zoom area diagonally.
       From Center - When using this and performing a Zoom Window you start from the Center of
       the View. This is the way CABINET VISION has normally performed a Zoom Window.
       Factor - This slider sets the Zoom Factor for Scroll Wheel Zooming. The lower (left) the
       setting the smaller the Factor.
       Reverse Scroll Wheel Zoom Direction - An option allowing you to reverse the Zoom In/
       Zoom Out direction on your Mouse Scroll Wheel.

Managing Job Files

This section will focus primarily on how to manage Job files and understand Job Status in the
Customer view.

To manage Job files in xCRM, a Job must be associated with a Customer.
When a Job file was previously saved in CABINET VISION prior to adding the xCRM option, you
will first need to highlight a customer in the top half of the Customer view. Next, right-click in the
bottom half of the Customer view and select "Import Job". You can then browse for your .CVJ file
and select "Open" to import it under the selected Customer.
To create a new Job in xCRM, you can select "New" in the File menu item or right-click in the
bottom half of the Customer view and select "New Job". Again, Job files are associated with a
Customer, so be sure to highlight a customer in the top half of the Customer view before creating
a new Job.
The default "Job Filename" will repeat the Customer Name, followed by an underscore and a
number. The number is automatically sequential, depending upon the number of Job files already
associated with this Customer Name. You can either click on OK to accept the automatic Job
name, or type in a different name for your Job. Additionally, you may add a comment in the "Job
Comment" field.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
              The Job status upon returning to the xCRM Opening Screen, until your Job file has
       been opened and saved, will indicate, "Job file not created yet".
To open a Job, right-click on the Job in the bottom half of the Customer view and select "Open".
After making selections in the "Job Properties" window, click on OK to enter Layout Level. To
return to the xCRM Opening Screen from the Job, select "Close" from the Solid Button menu.

              xCRM allows you to save multiple versions of a Job file. Until the "Save Version"
       option is used in the xCRM Opening Screen, the Job status will indicate, "New Job (no
       versions saved)".
To save a version of a Job, right-click on the Job in the bottom half of the Customer view and
select "Save Version". (Note: if this option is grayed out, either the Job file has not been created
yet OR has not been checked out by you. A Job file must be opened or checked out before a
version can be saved.)
You will then be prompted to write a comment for this version of the Job. This is one of the most
critical tools in xCRM. Your Job Version comments will help you identify differences in multiple
versions of the same Job. For example, if you have the "rare" customer that frequently changes
his/her mind, having an "initial version" will help you start over without actually having to start over.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
There are two toggle boxes in this window. Each of these choices has a significant effect on the
status of the Job file. By toggling ON "Keep Checked-out to you after saving" the Job status will
read, "Checked out to ". By toggling ON "Undo Check-out (Don't Save Version)" the Job status
will read, "Checked-in". Additionally, "Undo Check-out" will NOT save a version of the Job and
any change made by you will be lost. Note: The first time you save a version of a particular Job,
"Undo Check-out" will not be available to you.

              The Job status upon returning to the xCRM Opening Screen, will either read,
       "Checked-in" or "Checked-out to ". Also, a version number is indicated in the "Version"
       column.
To view ALL versions of your Job file, right-click on the Job and select "Properties". Highlight
which version you would like to check out and use the "Check-out Selected Version" button. If you
want to copy a version for another Job that is similar, use the "Copy Version as New Job" button.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
When a version of a Job file is checked out, other users are prevented from checking out the
same or different versions of the Job file until you check it back in.
When a version of a Job file has been copied as a new Job, the default "Job Filename" will
automatically repeat the Job Name, followed by an underscore and the original Job number.
Since this is a copy of another Job file, an additional underscore, followed by another number
identifies the "copy" number. You can either click on OK to accept the automatic Job name, or
type in a different name for your Job. Additionally, you may add a comment in the "Job Comment"
field.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Main Tab
Click the options below for more information

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The Part Manager is relatively straight forward in design and usage. It is primarily responsible for
holding information on Parts that you need within CABINET VISION. It is relatively complete as it
stands, containing the majority of Parts that most shops will use. It is configurable to a degree as it
allows you to set Labor values, CNC restrictions, or even Finishes to Parts. There are several
Tabs available depending on which Part Group you have active.

Part Tab

Name

The Name is an abbreviated code assigned by CABINET VISION to the Part. Although you can
change the Description, you can never change the Name once it is entered. The character limit for
the Name is 15.

Description

The Description of the Part can be changed by changing the text here. The Description of the Part
here is the "Name" displayed throughout CABINET VISION including all output such as Cut Lists.
The character limit for the Part Description is 100.

              This will change the "name" of the Part everywhere it is used.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Labor Setup

The Labor Setup column allows for a "minute" value to be entered concerning the time you will
allow to manufacture the selected Part. The "Labor Setup" value will only occur within the Job
once for the part (Setup Value).

Labor Each

The Labor Each column allows for a "minute" value to be entered concerning the time you will
allow to manufacture the selected Part. The "Labor Each" values occur for each Part within the
Job.

Price

The Price column allows you to establish Pricing for your selected Part. You can type a fixed Price
or select one of the pre-defined calculation methods. You can also utilize math to create your own
custom price utilizing (addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*), and/or division (/). The formula
will be validated by moving to another field. If the formula entered is invalid you will receive a
warning message and the invalid formula text will turn red. Following are the available pre-defined
calculations:
· <Cubic IN> - The Cubic Inch value of the Part.
· <Cubic M> - The Cubic Meters of the Part.
· <Face SqIN> - The Square Inches of the Face of the Part.
· <Face SqM> - The Square Meters of the Face of the Part.
· <Length IN> - The Length, in Inches, of the Part.
· <Length MM> - The Length, in Millimeters, of the Part.
· <Matrix Price> - This option will use the active Price Matrix that is selected in the Matrix

   column within the Price calculation formula you enter. See the Price Matrix topic for more
   information.
· <Thick IN> - The Thickness, in Inches, of the Part.
· <Thick MM> - The Thickness, in Millimeters, of the Part.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
· <Width IN> - The Width, in Inches, of the Part.
· <Width MM> - The Width, in Millimeters, of the Part.

Matrix

The Matrix column allows you to select the Matrix Price to utilize for this Part. See the Price Matrix
topic form more information.

CNC Tab
Optimize

The Optimize column is a toggle. Assuming you have the Optimizer or Nesting, you can toggle
Parts on or off as to Optimizing/Nesting.

Ignore Grain

The Ignore Grain column is a toggle. Assuming you have the Optimizer or Nesting, you can toggle
Parts on or off as to whether honoring Grain rules for the Part is required.

CNC

The CNC column is a toggle. If you have CNC capabilities, you can choose which Parts are
outputted to CNC by toggling them off or on.

Finishes Tab
Exterior Face Finish, Exterior Back Finish, Exterior Edge Finish, and Exterior
End Finish

These columns determine whether the Part uses the Exterior (enabled) or Interior (disabled)
Finish for the Parts Face, Back, Edge, and/or End. The choices are Enabled (match Exterior
Finish in the Job/Room/Assembly) or Disabled (match Interior Finish in the Job/Room/Assembly).

Textures Tab
Exterior Face Texture, Exterior Back Texture, Exterior Edge Texture, and
Exterior End Texture

These columns determine whether the Part uses the Exterior (enabled) or Interior (disabled)

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Texture for the Parts Face, Back, Edge and/or End. The choices are Enabled (match Exterior
Texture in the Job/Room/Assembly) or Disabled (match Interior Texture in the Job/Room/
Assembly).

Part Matrix Pricing allows you to establish standard Part sizes along with fixed Prices or Pricing

The Interface

The Toolbar

The following tools are available in the Size - Price Matrix.
                                            Matrix Selector - Allows you to select an existing Price Matrix to

       edit.
           New - Creates a new Price Matrix.
            Copy - Will Copy the selected Price Matrix

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
            Rename - Will Rename the selected Price Matrix.
            Delete - Will Delete the selected Price Matrix.
            Modify Prices - Allows you to Increase or Decrease the Prices in the active Price Matrix
       a specific Percentage.

            Unit of Measure Selection - Allows you to select the Unit of Measure to work with.

The Matrix Area

Shows the currently selected Matrix. Lengths are shown vertically and Widths horizontally.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Global Pricing Area

There are four options in the Global Pricing Area. This area allows you to establish Global Pricing
for the selected Price Matrix. There are two options here:
 Default Price Formula - The Price or Pricing Formula entered here will be used for any Cells

   left blank within the selected Price Matrix.
 No-Match Price Formula - The Price or Pricing Formula entered here will be used for the

   selected Price Matrix if a Size Match is not found.
 Exact Width Match - This option, if selected, instructs Solid that the Width must be an exact

   match to use the Price for the Size.
    If this is not selected for Width then instead of an exact match it will use >= for the match.

      The low number in the Width is what is keyed off of. So a 0 to 12 Width will capture from 0"
      up to 11.999". The next Width grid from 12 to 14 will capture 12" up to 13.999" and so on.
 Exact Length Match - This option, if selected, instructs Solid that the Length must be an exact
   match to use the Price for the Size.
    If this is not selected for Length then instead of an exact match it will use >= for the match.
      The low number in the Length is what is keyed off of. So a 0 to 24 Length will capture from 0"
      up to 23.999". The next Length grid from 24 to 36 will capture 24" up to 35.999" and so on.

An Example

The best way to explain how Matrix Pricing functions is by example. This example will cover
setting up a Price Matrix for Fixed Shelves with the following Prices.
Create a Size/Price Matrix Named "Fixed Shelves Locked Width-Length".

Next, you will need to setup the Sizes for your Size/Price Matrix. Fixed Shelves are offered in
widths from 12" to 24" in 2 inch increments. Lengths are offered from 24" to 96" in 12 inch
increments. So in this example the manufacturer has these Fixed Shelves pre-cut and ready to
ship and these sizes each have a set Price. Any other sizes are custom and will use a special
calculation to cover the cost custom cutting the special sizes. Step one would be to create a Size
Matrix to cover Fixed Shelves. To cover the sizes in the example simply enter the required Widths
in the Column Headers and the required Lengths in the Row Headers as in the illustration below.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
You will also notice two options in the lower left (highlighted above) of the Part Size - Price Matrix
area. In this example the Prices are for exact Part Sizes so these two options (Exact Width Match
and Exact Length Match) should be selected.

Each cell in the Price Matrix on the right is now active and ready for us to enter our Prices.

You have a few options here:

1. You can enter a fixed Price in the Cells.

2. You can enter a Price formula amount in the Cells.

     You can type a fixed Price or select one of the pre-defined calculation methods. You can also
       utilize math to create your own custom price utilizing (addition (+), subtraction (-),
       multiplication (*), and/or division (/). The formula will be validated by moving to another field.
       If the formula entered is invalid you will receive a warning message and the invalid formula
       text will turn red. Following are the available pre-defined calculations:

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
        Volume
            - The Cubic Inch value of the Part.
            - The Cubic Meters of the Part.

        Face Area
            - The Square Inches of the Face of the Part.
            - The Square Meters of the Face of the Part.

        Length
            - The Length, in Inches, of the Part.
            - The Length, in Millimeters, of the Part.

        Thickness
            - The Thickness, in Inches, of the Part.
            - The Thickness, in Millimeters, of the Part.

        Width
            - The Width, in Inches, of the Part.
            - The Width, in Millimeters, of the Part.

3. You can leave any Cell you need to blank.
     If you leave a Cell blank then the blank Cell will utilize the Price or Formula that is entered in
       the Default Formula field at the bottom.

You can use any combination of the 3 options above within the Matrix. This means, each Size cell
can be any one of the 3 options above.
In the example there are Fixed Widths and Lengths along with Fixed Prices for each combination
so our Price Matrix will look like below with each Cell containing a fixed Price.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Because the Widths and Lengths are fixed we have covered all of the Pricing for our Standard
Parts. Next we need to cover the Pricing when there is no Size match. This will be our calculation
for Custom Fixed Shelf Sizes. This formula needs to be entered in the "No Match Formula" field.
In this case we are going to use *1. This is the Square Inches of the Part multiplied by 1.

The Material Manager is simply a list of all Materials that could possibly be used in a CABINET
VISION Job. This list can be separated into groups and sub-groups that you define so that you can
find specific items more quickly.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 ALL Materials must be listed in the Material Manager BEFORE they will be available inside a
   Job.

 There is no limit to the number of Materials that may be added to the Material Manager. Your
   only limitation is the size of your computer's hard drive.

 Make sure that every sheet good or board good that you enter has a valid THICKNESS. The
   Thickness is the most important characteristic of a Material.

                      Do not use any characters in the Material name except letters, numbers and a /
               character in fractions. The use of quotation marks (") and the pound symbol (#) can
               cause errors in the S2M Center as well as other areas of Solid.

Drawer Guide
      Drawer Guide

               Unit of Issue - Previously covered.
               Type - The Type of Drawer Guide. There are three choices here:

               Length - The Length of the Drawer Guide.
               Height - The Height of the Drawer Guide. Only available for the "System" Type.
               Side Clearance - This is the value establishes the clearance at the sides of the drawer
               box for the Drawer Guide. This value, multiplied by 2 and then subtracted from the
               opening width, will set the Width of a Drawer Box that has this Drawer Guide. This is
               the area where Drawer Boxes receive the information on their Width. If you want more
               than a typical 1/2 inch, for a little play for instance, consider entering a value of 17/32.
               Top Clearance - This value, and the values entered in the Drawer Box/Roll Out Wizard
               begin to set the Height of your Drawer Box. You are asked to enter a minimum value
               here, and that minimum value will always apply to the selected Drawer Guide. This
               represents the distance between the top of the Drawer Box and the first thing it would

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       otherwise hit, or, the gap between it and another Drawer if there is no Cabinet member
       in between.
       Bottom Clearance - Similar to the minimum top clearance, this defines the distance
       between the bottom of the Drawer Box side, (or the Drawer bottom, the lower of the
       two), and the first thing it would hit. If there is no Cabinet member in the way, it would
       reference the gap.

Mount Holes

       Diameter - The Diameter of the Mount Holes.
       Depth - The Depth of the Mount Holes.
       Top Reference - When set to Yes establishes that the Mount Holes are referenced
       from the top of the Guide.
       Screw Center to Ref. - Sets the dimension from the Reference (established with Top
       Reference) to the center of the Mount Holes.
       Position 1 - The Position of the first hole from the Front of the Drawer Box. When
       defining a "Model" for your Drawer Guide the first hole should be placed at the Graphic
       Reference Point. This value will shift the Graphic when used in an Assembly by this
       value. This value typically represents the distance from the front of your Case to the
       First Bore Hole. Sets the Model Reference Point placement.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Position 2 - The Position of the second hole from the Front of the Drawer Box.
       Position 3 - The Position of the third hole from the Front of the Drawer Box.
       Position 4 - The Position of the fourth hole from the Front of the Drawer Box.
       Position 5 - The Position of the fifth hole from the Front of the Drawer Box.
       Position 6 - The Position of the sixth hole from the Front of the Drawer Box.

Front Mount Holes

       Horizontal Offset - The Horizontal Offset distance from the Drawer Box Side to the
       center of the Front Mount Holes.
       Vertical Offset - The Vertical Offset distance from the Reference, specified in Top
       Reference, to the center of the Front Mount Holes.
       Diameter - The Diameter of the Front Mount Holes.
       Depth - The Depth of the Front Mount Holes.
       Spacing - The Spacing (if more than one in Quantity) of the Front Mount Holes.
       Quantity - The Quantity of the Front Mount Holes.

       Diameter - The Diameter of the Back Mount Holes.
       Depth - The Depth of the Back Mount Holes.
       Spacing - The Spacing (if more than one in Quantity) of the Back Mount Holes.

Alias
   Alias

This option will add an Alias for your selected Material. Aliases are Material which get most of their
Properties from the Parent Material with a few Properties that are unique (differentiators). This
allows you to do things like create Panel Stock which would be the same with the exception of
their Name, Sheet Size, and Cost. Most Material Types have special Properties used as
differentiators.
Simply type the unique Name and Description for your Alias.

The Alias will be available as a sub-item to its parent Material.

Certain fields will be available for editing (differentiators) while other will be locked indicating they
are derived from the parent Material.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

   Kit

Composite
      Composite

This option allows you to set the structure of your Composite Material. A Composite Material is a
sheet Material consisting of several layers of sheet goods.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
              The Composite Material Manager is only available for the Composite Material type.

Select your sheet good from the pane on the right and then click the left button to add it to the list
of Materials that make up the Composite in the left pane. There is a Filter option at the top to
assist in finding a specific Material.
You can control the order the sheets are layered by using the Up and Down buttons and remove a
sheet from the Composite by clicking the Right button.
The following fields can be edited once a sheet good is added to the Composite:
Face Up - Specifies if the sheet good is Face Up (Enabled) or Face Down (Disabled).
Oversize - An Oversize amount for the sheet good when used in this Composite.
See the Composite Material Type topic for more information.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

Creating a Model

              When modifying or creating a Model for a Drawer Guide it is important to note that you
       define the Left Guide and the system automatically creates a right guide and it's operations
       (placed on the Primary Work Plane) as a mirror of what you have defined for the left Guide.
In the following example we are going to create an Entry Knob Model which includes an Inside
Door Knob and Outside Door Knob and a Strike Plate. To start create a new Miscellaneous Material
named "Entry Knob". Once in the Properties area with this new Material make sure to go to the
Miscellaneous Group and set the Model option to True.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Click Model in the ribbonbar then from the sidebar select the "Assembly" Object. This Object is
simply a sample part to help you orient your Graphic. This object is displayed in brown on screen.
For the following Tutorial go ahead and change the DZ (Thickness) of the sample Assembly
Object to 1.25".

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
From the sidebar select the "Primary Work Plane" Object. This is the default Work Plane and also
represents the insertion (Reference Point) of the Model. Think of this as the container for your
Model, everything will be referenced from this Object. The center of the Work Plane object is the
insertion (Reference Point). Change the X and Y of the "Primary Work Plane" to 4". The true
position of the "Primary Work Plane' will be set when the Model is placed within a Job whether
automatically, manually, or via UCS.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
1. Set the View Mode to Front.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
2. With the "Primary Work Plane" object selected in the sidebar click the Add Work Plane
    option in the ribbonbar.

                      Additional Work Planes will search for matching surfaces and transfer their
               operations (such as shaped routes). This search is only within the Part that the primary
               surface touches..

3. Set the "Front WP" X and Y to 0.

4. Click the Add Hardware  option in the ribbonbar.

5. Simply browse to the 3D Model you wish to import making sure to set the appropriate file type
    (highlighted below) then click Open.

      The models used in this tutorial are available on the DVD at \Support\Sample
Models\.

                           © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
6. The next screen offers several modification options you can perform prior to importing the 3D
    Model. See the topics on Importing DXF or Importing SketchUp Models for more information on the
    modification options on this screen. Click OK to import your model.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
              See the DXF Import topic for information for the formatting requirements of 3D DXF files.
7. Once imported I am going to change the following Properties for the Inside Knob:

    1. Name = IKNOB
    2. Description = Inside Knob
    3. Finish = Chrome
    4. Finish Type = Metal - Matte
    5. X = -1.25 (This will center my knob horizontally on the Plane)
    6. Y = -1.25 (This will center my knob vertically on the Plane)

      more information on the CAM Editor options.

                 Operations.

     1. Name = OKNOB
     2. Description = Outside Knob
     3. Finish = Chrome
     4. Finish Type = Metal - Matte
     5. X = -1.25 (This will center my knob horizontally on the Plane)
     6. Y = -1.25 (This will center my knob vertically on the Plane)

      View Mode to the Left.

     4. Finish Type = Metal - Matte

      Parameters

Opens the Parameter Editor allowing you to add a Parameter to the currently selected Material.
See the Parameters topic for more information on the Parameter Editor interface.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
              To query these Parameters via UCS you will need to use _M:ParameterName on the
       Object using the Material. The Parameter will not be visible in the Object Tree.
When editing Parameters for a Connector Material you have an additional tool in the toolbar.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
When a Connector primary operation creates a secondary operation, the primary operation
notifies the Connector a secondary operation has been created. The Connector in response then
runs a UCS that has been created for it here. This will allow you to create a UCS to adjust the Z
Position of operations after all the internal processing has taken place so the Connector
Operations can be adjusted to different thickness Secondary parts.
There is an example within the UCS editor when you click the New tool. See the User Created
Standards topic for more information on the UCS interface.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Notice you have the ability to create multiple UCS's here. To actually have a specific Connector
UCS run you would use a normal UCS within CABINET VISION to call it. You would assign the
normal UCS to the Primary Operation within the Connector and set _MACRO = n. n being the
Order number for the UCS in the Connector UCS Editor.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Select your Vendor from the pane on the right and then click the left button to add it to the list of

from the right pane to the left.
The following fields can be edited once a Vendor is added to the Material:
SKU - The identifier used by the Vendor for the selected Material.
Cost - What you pay the Vendor for the selected Material.
Markup - The Markup you apply when using the Material from this Vendor.

Current Default Vendor

If you are assigning multiple Vendors to a Material make sure to select which Vendor is your

Material Types
Banding
Banding

This topic covers all the Properties for the Banding Material Type.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Material Group

 ID - Returns internal ID number for the selected Material. Not available for editing.
 Name - The name of the Material, this name can be anything as long as it helps you to identify

   the Material correctly.

                      Do not use " marks in the Name of the Material as it causes errors in the
               optimization of a Job. For example, 1/2" Melamine would not be an appropriate name
               for a Material; use 1/2in Melamine to be safe.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 Description - The Description of the Material.

 Type - Returns the Material Type for the selected Material. Not available for editing.

 Unit of Issue - Allows you to set the Unit in which you buy the Material. There are nine options
   here:

    BD FT - Per Board Foot

    BD M - Per Board Meter

    Cubic FT - Per Cubic Foot

    Cubic M - Per Cubic Meter

    Each - Per each

    Pair - Per pair (Useful for Drawer Guides or other Hardware sold in Pairs)

    Per FT - Per Foot

    Per M - Per Meter

    Sheet - Per Sheet

    SQ FT - Per Square Foot

    SQ M - Per Square Meter.

 Default Vendor - If you have assigned Vendors to the selected Material you will be able to
   choose between those Vendors or None. If you choose a Vendor the Default Cost, Default
   Markup, and Default Tax Rate will come from the selected Vendor and those fields will be
   disabled. If you choose None as the Vendor then you can enter your own values. None is the
   only option if no Vendors are attached to the Material.

 Default Cost - Allows you to set the Cost you pay for the selected Material. If the Default Cost
   comes from an assigned Vendor this field will be disabled.

 Sell Price -      - Allows you to set the Sell price you charge your Customer for the selected
   Material.

 Default Markup -  - Allows you to set the Markup percent you charge your Customer for

the selected Material. The Cost Markup entered here would most often be used to cover

transportation costs or overhead associated with the Materials themselves. You will have the

opportunity to enter additional Markups in the Bid Center as well. If the Default Markup comes

from an assigned Vendor this field will be disabled.

                   © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 Sales Tax - Allows you to set whether you pay Tax on the selected Material. If the Sales Tax
   comes from an assigned Vendor this field will be disabled.

 Default Tax Rate -  - Allows you to set the Tax percent you pay for the selected Material.

The Sales Tax Rate entered here is what you pay when you purchase your Materials. The

Sales Tax (if any) that you charge your Customer is entered in the Bid Center.

 Waste - Allows you to set the Waste percent for the selected Material.

 Estimate - Allows you to control whether the selected Material is sent to the Bid Center and
   calculated with the % of Material Cost Bid Method.

 Load Model - Allows you to control whether the Model is loaded into a Job. Models can be
   large and can cause Jobs to perform slowly this allows you to overcome this with specific
   Materials. This option only displays on Materials that support Models.

 S2M Material - When enabled makes the Material available in the S2M CENTER Material
   catalog.See the S2M CENTER Help system for more information.

                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Banding Group

 Length Trim - Allows you to set a extra amount of Banding length to compensate for wasted
   Length on an edgebander for feeding and end trimming.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 Thickness - Allows you to set the Thickness of the selected Banding Material. The Thickness is
   the most important property of a Material because the construction of your Cabinets will depend
   on the Material Thickness in order to give you a correct cut list.
                     The Width of banding is determined by the Part it is attached to's Thickness. The
               overall width of the Banding is not considered, instead, you may wish to enter banding
               that is 13/16 or 7/8 wide by referencing that fact in the Material Name.
                     It is permissible to define Solid Stock as banding in the event you need solid
               wood edges on your Cabinets, Doors, or Drawer faces. If you do so, do not confuse
               the Thickness with the Width, the Width will default to the net finished Thickness of the
               Part it is attached to.

                                                                    © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Layer Group

The Layer Group Header identifies which Layer you are controlling.
 Finish - The Finish assigned to the Layer. A fixed Finish applied to the Layer will show as a color

   swatch. If the Finish is derived from the Job/Room/Assembly/Part Finish the word Automatic will
   be in this field. By selecting a Finish you are locking that Finish (Color) to the selected Material.
 Finish Type - The Finish Type assigned to the Layer.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 Texture - The Texture assigned to the Layer. If the Material does not have a Texture (pattern) to it
   then select the Blank Texture for it.

                      CNC Users take note: Texture selection on your Panel Stock determines
               whether the Material is one Sided or Two Sided. If the same or no Texture is assigned
               to both the Face and Back you are, when sending Parts utilizing the Material to the
               S2M CENTER, stating that the Material is Two Sided. This will allow the S2M CENTER
               to flip Parts over if the Part has more operations on one side versus the other.
               At the same time if the Textures differ from Face to back you are instructing the S2M
               CENTER that it can not flip the Parts on that Material over. Also, the S2M CENTER will
               determine which side of that Material needs to be face up on the Nest by an Operation
               count and the operator will be instructed to face that Texture (by name) Up on the
               Machine.

Board Stock

This topic covers all the Properties for the Board Stock Material Type.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Material Group

Previously covered in the Banding Material Type topic.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Board Group

 Thickness - Establishes the Boards finished Thickness. The Thickness is the most important
   property of a Material because the construction of your Cabinets will depend on the Material
   Thickness in order to give you a correct cut list.

 Rough Thickness - Establishes the Boards Rough Thickness for proper Board Foot/Meter
   calculations. This field only comes into play if BD FT or BD M is selected for the Unit of Issue.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
      Other than selecting a different Unit (BD FT or BD M in place of a Sheet Size) the
logic is the same in completing these two areas. You may choose to enter Board Stock
as dimensional lumber and define the Thickness in the Thickness box. An example,
4/4 Oak for the Name and 3/4 for it's Thickness. This would appear on your Cut List as:
The 4/4 references the Board Stock's name. This is a matter of taste as the 4/4
reference has no effect on the Material Thickness. To control the purchased (Rough)
thickness to get accurate Board Stock Material Requirements enter the thickness in
the Rough Thickness field. Additionally, you may need thicker stock for manufacturing
other items. Keep in mind that the Name you provide for your Material is the name that
will appear on the Cut List, and in the Material Schedule area when accessing the
Material from the Material Manager.

                                              © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
CNC Group

The CNC Properties section allows you to set up the CNC properties for the current Material. For
example, the "Minimize Face Chipping" and "Minimize Back Chipping" check boxes will be
used by the S2M CENTER's Automatic Tool Selection Logic.
 Optimize - If the Material that you are setting up is sheet stock, you should set up the

   Optimization rules so that Solid and/or the S2M CENTER will know how to treat the Material in
   the Optimizer/Nester. This option lets you select whether or not to send this Material to the
   Optimizer/Nester when it is used in a Job. Although this Property is available for Board Stock it

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
   would be unusual to send Board Stock Parts to the Optimizer/Nester.
 Grain Dependent - This option will let you determine whether Parts may be rotated across the

   Sheet/Board in the Optimizer/Nester. It is a good idea to set up these rules for any new sheet
   stock Material even if you do not currently have the Optimizer option for Solid/S2M Center. If
   you upgrade to Optimization/Nesting in the future, it will already be set up.
 Drop Width - A value representing the Minimum Width to be considered an Offcut rather than
   scrap.
 Drop Length - A value representing the Minimum Length to be considered an Offcut rather
   than scrap.
 Feed Rate Percent - A value representing the Percent of optimum Tool Feed Rate to use with
   this Material.
 Spindle Speed Percent - A value representing the percentage of optimum Tool Spindle Speed
   (RPM's).
 Minimize Face Chip - If this option is enabled, the S2M CENTER automatic tool selection logic
   will try to select a down-shear bit. If both this option and "Minimize Back Chipping" are enabled
   then the S2M CENTER automatic tool selection logic will try to select a compression bit.
 Minimize Back Chip - If this option is enabled, the S2M CENTER will try to select an up-shear
   bit for that Material. If both this option and "Minimize Face Chipping" are enabled then the S2M
   CENTER automatic tool selection logic will try to select a compression bit.
 Climb Cut - Establishes if this Material should be cut with Climb Cut.
 Maximum Depth Per Pass - Establishes the depth per pass a tool can make when cutting this
   Material. The smaller of the two amounts (material versus tool) will be used for the path

Drawer Guides
Drawer Guides

This topic covers all the Properties for the Drawer Guide Material Type. The properties that
accompany each Drawer Guide play an important part in helping determine your Drawer Box size.
However, this is only part of the process of Drawer Box sizing.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Material Group

Previously covered in the Banding Material Type topic.
              Cost - If you are entering "Cost" information, be aware that the price you enter is for

       "each" Drawer Guide, not each pair. Therefore, enter 1/2 of the cost of the "pair" of Drawer
       Guides.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Guide Group

 Type - Type defines the style of Drawer Guide as either Side Mount, Bottom Mount, Top Mount
   or System.
                      With Cabinet Vision the "Mount" indicates how the Guide attaches to the
               Assembly not how it attaches to the Drawer. Example a typical Blum Tandem Drawer
               Guide in Cabinet Vision is considered a Side Mount because it Mounts to the side of a
               typical Cabinet.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 Height - The Height of the Drawer Guide.
 Length - The Length of the Drawer Guide.
 Extension - This value sets the graphic limit of how far the Drawer Box opens when you use

   the "Open Drawer" feature.

 Screw Center Reference to Top - This option, if enabled, will set the reference for your
   mounting bores from the top of the Drawer Box. If not enabled the Reference will be from the
   Drawer Box Bottom. Sets the Graphic Reference Point placement.

                                                     or
 Screw Center To Box Reference - This value sets your Mounting Bore position from the

   Reference selected above. Sets the Graphic Reference Point placement.
              This value helps determine your Drawer Box Height if you Bore All Line Bore Holes and

       align your Drawer Guides to System Boring.
 Back Notch Length - Allows you to specify the Back Notch Length.

                                                                    © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 Back Notch Height - Allows you to specify the Back Notch Height.
 Back Notch Offset - Allows you to specify the Horizontal position of the Back Notch.

                                                                    © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
© 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Clearance Group

 Side Clearance - This is the "thickness" of the Drawer Guide. This value, multiplied by 2 and
   then subtracted from the opening width, will set the Width of a Drawer Box that has this Drawer
   Guide. This is the area where Drawer Boxes receive the information on their Width. If you want
   more than a typical 1/2 inch, for a little play for instance, consider entering a value of 17/32.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 Minimum Below Box - Similar to Minimum Above Box (below), this defines the distance
   between the bottom of the Drawer Box side, (or the Drawer bottom, the lower of the two), and
   the first thing it would hit. If there is no Cabinet member in the way, it would reference the gap.

   Method begin to set the Height of your Drawer Box. You are asked to enter a minimum value

Finish Type
   Finish Type

Toolbar

The toolbar has the following options:
                                     Finish Type Selector - Allows you to select an existing Finish Type to

edit.
    New - Allows you to create a New Finish Type.
     Copy - Copies the currently selected Finish Type.
     Delete - Deletes the currently selected Finish Type.

The following options can be used to control the Finish Types properties:

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Name - The Name of the current Finish.

Description - The Description of the current Finish.

ID - The Finish Type's database ID.

Shader - There are seven Shaders you can choose from. These simulate the real-world
reflectance of the stated Material Types.

 Glass
 Gloss Metal
 Gloss Plastic
 Metal
 Mirror
 Plastic
 Wood

Ambient - Sets the base color, should typically be set at 50%. Defines an Ambient Lights affect on
the Material. This is typically set to a high value for complex surfaces to help shade or define folds
and creases on the Materials surface.

Diffuse - Values higher than 50% are shinier while values lower than 50% are more matte.
Defines how light reflected from the Material strikes other objects in the surrounding area,
illuminating them. The Diffuse Factor describes light reflected from surfaces which are not shiny or
specular. In real life terms what this means is that light is reflected off non-shiny surfaces such as
the ground, walls, or fabric, to reach areas not directly in view of a light source.

Specular - The Specular Factor is distinct from the Diffuse Factor, where incoming light is
reflected in a broad range of directions. The most familiar example of the distinction between
Specular and Diffuse reflection would be glossy and matte paints. While both exhibit a
combination of Specular and Diffuse reflection, matte paints have a higher proportion of Diffuse
reflection and glossy paints have a greater proportion of Specular reflection. Very highly polished
surfaces, such as high quality mirrors, can exhibit almost complete Specular reflection.

Shininess - This setting sets the smoothness of the surface. Shininess references the Materials
ability to reflect. The more towards the right you set the slider the more the Material will reflect.

               Shininess in and of itself will not control Reflection specifically. The roughness of the
       Finish plays a role in "how" something reflects. A mirror is perfectly smooth and with it
       reflection is reflection. First you establish a surface is reflective by selecting the Mirror Type
       then you must tweak the other Finish Properties in order to fully define how the finish reacts
       to lighting.

Transparency - Transparency references the ability of the Material to allow the Texture below it to
show through. Wood grain shows through a transparent color to give a wood tone finish when set
correctly. If the slider bar is moved to the full transparent side (the right side), the Finish will
appear as a tint. This may be useful for glass type Finishes, but is too transparent for stain type

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Finishes.

Preview

The Preview area (highlighted above) allows you to preview the active Finish Type using different
Finishes, Textures, Light Types, and Brightness.

Texture
    Texture

A Texture is a pattern that will appear on your finished objects such as wood grain or any other
visible feature. Textures will generally show through the Finish color in a Room adding the element
of realism to your objects. Typically, Textures are black and white, and receive color from a Finish
at the Room Level, however, this is not always the case. A Texture can be a sample of Marble,
complete with the color and pattern that you choose to scan into Solid for use in your
presentations. You will have to experiment with scanning in order to find the size and type of
acceptable (scannable) images that do not distort when you shrink them to the size necessary to
appear on a scaled Solid rendering. A hint that may help is to search for books from hobbyists
who create miniature items. Examples might be doll house publications, model railroad

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
publications, etc. Typically, the textures you will find there are created at the scale they will be
rendered at, and do not need to be reduced, and do not suffer the distortion that often
accompanies the reduction process.

Toolbar

    Import Image - Allows you to Import an image as a new Texture. See The Bitmap Method
below for more information.

       You can use Windows    + Click and/or                              + Click to select and
import multiple image files.

         Make sure that the image file you are importing is located somewhere other than where
  you are importing it to.

Height across the surface it is being applied to.
The Bitmap Method
Here, a new Texture created using the Paint program that ships with Microsoft WindowsTM will be
imported for use as speaker cloth on Doors for a Job. The Texture was created in the favored 200
by 200 pixel size, and saved as a Bitmap file to the to my Windows Desktop folder as spk.bmp.

                   Make sure that the image file you are importing is located somewhere other than
where you are importing it to. In the above example the image file is on the Windows Desktop.
To add a Texture choose the Category where you want it located then click the New option in the
ribbonbar and select the Bitmap or JPG file from the Graphics sub-folder where you saved the file
you made. Files that you copy to your computer can be saved to the same folder as those you
make and imported in the same fashion.
Since this is a file that exists on my computer I will choose the "Load an image from a file" option
in the toolbar.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Browse to, and select you image file then click Open.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Go ahead and fill out all the Properties, when you are happy with the Properties click the Save
option in the toolbar.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
                      The "Decal" check box, must be checked if you want the Texture to stand alone,
               I.E., not to be tinted by the Room Finish.

The "Tile" check box should be enabled if you want the pattern to repeat on your object. Without
checking this box, the Texture will appear one time, and may not cover all the surfaces you have
applied it to. Make sure to set the World Width and World Height at 12 each. After verifying the
appearance of your new Texture you can adjust these World dimensions to tweak the appearance
of the Texture when displayed.

To add this Texture to a Door as speaker cloth, create the speaker cloth as a "Miscellaneous"
Material in the Material Manager, and choose the new Texture for the face Texture. From the Door
Material Schedules, create a Schedule referencing the Material as one with speaker cloth (Birch/
Spker) and assign the speaker cloth to the "Flat Panel" category. You will see the following if
viewed in High Detail in a Job. Note how the speaker cloth is not tinted by the Cabinet color and
how the pattern repeats to fill each Door.

The ultimate secret to successful Texture creation and usage is to experiment with the resolution
and scale of the items you chose to use. You will quickly understand the relationship and how to
improve the image after viewing your Textures in a practice Job. Textures are not limited to
patterns, even company logos, initials, etc..., can be used.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
              Textures can also be added from within a Job in the 3D View when selecting Textures
       to use in your Room or Assembly.

      Properties
Material schedules are created so that you can tie Parts from the Part Manager to Materials that you
have created in the Material Manager, inside a Job.
A Material Schedule is simply a template of the list of Materials assigned to specific Parts. For
example, you might want to create a Material Schedule for an Oak Cabinet. To do so, you would
go to the Assembly Parts Material Schedules and create a new one. You would probably want to
call the Material Schedule something like "Oak Cabinets." Next, you would go through the
Schedule and assign the proper Material to each Assembly Part. Then, any time that you wanted
to create a Job that included Cabinets made of oak, all that you would have to do is select the Oak
Material Schedule in the Materials Property window, and then draw the Job. In other words, once a
Material Schedule has been created, it can be used in any subsequent Jobs that require the same
Materials. This should help to save time that would otherwise be used in assigning Materials for
Assembly Parts in every Job.
