Steps to Creating a New Material Schedule for Assembly Parts

You will notice that when you expand a branch (by clicking the + symbol beside a branch, you will
expand that branch to see the underlying levels), there are names of specific Assembly Parts. For
each Assembly Part, you need to select a Material that will be used in this Schedule.

First, click the New option in the Ribbonbar.

In the sidebar type in a Name for the new Material Schedule. The name should reflect the
Materials that you will be selecting for this Schedule so that you can identify the Schedule by the
name alone. The Description field is simply for any additional details that you wish to include.

Next, you should go down the Part List and make sure to assign Materials to every Part. In this
example, we will first click the + symbol to expand the Banding line.

When the Banding line is expanded, you will see a list of the types of banding that are available to
you. See the Banding topic for information on creating additional Banding Material.

To choose a Material for Exterior Banding, click on the words Exterior Banding and then browse to
and select a Material from the Material List. At this point you can either drag and drop the desired

Material onto the Part or you can click the assign  button to assign a Material to a selected
Part.

Then, repeat the process for Interior Banding and any additional Banding types that you have

© 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
created.
Next, click the + symbol next to Case and then the + symbol next to Interior so that you can
select Materials for the internal case Parts of the Assembly.

You should notice that there is a Material selected for Assembly, for Case and for Interior.
However, there is no single Cabinet Part called "Assembly," or "Case," or "Interior." Actually, these
are Parent lines for all of the Parts that appear underneath. Any Parts that appear in the list which

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
have a red check mark beside them have been changed to something other than the Material that
is selected for the parent. The benefit of having a Part that matches the parent's Material is that
changing the parent Material will also change the "child." Therefore, you can make a single
change to the parent line and subsequently change all of the "children" under it without going
through the tedious process of changing each Part's Material. The only changes that you would
have to then make individually would be any Parts that do not match the parent. If you want a Part
to follow the parent's Material, simply right-click on that Part and click Materials | Match Parent.
Finally, you should repeat the process for every Part that is listed in the Material Schedule until
they are all assigned a proper Material.

              There are many Parts in the Schedule that you may never use in a Job. For example, if
       you build Frameless Cabinets, the Face Frame Parts will have Materials assigned but will
       not appear in a Job unless your Construction Method calls for them. For these types of
       Parts, you should choose the Material that you would use if you ever did put that Part into a
       Job.

                      There is only one way to "turn off" Laminate or Banding for a particular Job, and
               that is to choose the Material named None for Laminate and Banding. The None
               material is a Material that has no Thickness and no Cost. CABINET VISION will see
               that Material applied to the Laminate or Banding and will leave those items out of the
               Job.
Your Material Schedules are very flexible. When you are in a particular Job that is similar to the
normal Schedule with some minor changes, you can modify the Schedule inside that Job and it
will not reach beyond that Job. For more details, click here.
You are not limited in the number of Material Schedules that you may create. However, it is
recommended that you create them as you need them rather than trying to anticipate your needs
when you start setting up CABINET VISION.

Buy Out - Enable this option you Buy-Out the Door rather than building it yourself. This will tie in
to your Reports and Bids.

Cost/Door - This option will simply add the entered amount as a flat rate per Door. This value will
only be added in a Rate Table that uses the Bid Method "Use Door Catalog Pricing."

Cost/SqFt (SqM) - This option will multiply the entered amount by the total area of the Door. This

this Material Schedule. Note that total door cost is Door + Mat + Profile (Inside Edge + Outside
Edge + Raised Panel + Custom Route). This value is only for the Material cost so if the Material
"Add Per Door" and the Material "Add Per SqFt" is less than "Min Cost" it will use Min Cost for the
Material cost. In other words... the Door Cost and Profile Costs will be added to this Minimum
Cost.

Part to your Door.

       another without. Remember to name the Schedules in a way that lets you know that Banding
       is turned on. For example, you may want to have a Schedule called Birch and one called
       Birch Band. This will allow you to know by name that one Material Schedule is for a Birch
       Door that has banding turned on.

be used on Doors that you want to Banding simple enable the option.

Multi-Length Drawer Guide Schedules

Drawer Guide Length is based off of the Drawer Box Depth. The first step in the process is to
verify that Drawer Box Depths are being calculated correctly. Once you have verified that the Depths
of the Drawer Boxes are correct then focus on the Drawer Guide Lengths.

Steps to set up a Multi-Length Schedule

First, make sure that the parent (the line that is labeled Drawer Guide) is set to either the "no
guide for this size" Material or the shortest guide that you would use in this Material Schedule.
Next, right click the Drawer Guide Category and select Variable Sizing | Add Size.
You will then be prompted to enter the minimum Depth Drawer Box that the new Guide will be
used on. In the example above, the first depth is 10. When you click OK, you will have a line under
Drawer Guide that says ">= 10." This means that any Drawer Box that is less than 10" deep will
use the parent guide and any Drawer Box that is 12" deep or greater will use the >= 12 guide (12"
guide).

Then, continue adding new Drawer Box Depths until you have complete coverage for your needs.

Multi-Height Drawer Guide Schedules
Steps to set up a Multi-Height Schedule

First, make sure you have created your Lengths (above). Each Drawer Guide Height needs to
correspond to a Length.
Next, right click the Length breakout you want to add a Height to and select Variable Sizing | Add
Size.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Next, enter a Height this Guide is available for. If you enable the "Add this height for each length
of this part" option, this New Guide Height will be added to every Guide Length in the Schedule
you are in.

Then, continue adding new Drawer Box Heights until you have complete coverage for your needs.

Frame Stile and Rail Widths
The value entered in these field represents the portion of the Stile or Rail as it exists without
any Inside Profile on it. The dimension of the Inside Profile, optionally depending on the 'Extend
Part' Property for the Inside Edge Profile, is in addition to the Stile or Rail width. If there is no
Inside Profile, then the value set as the default width for the Stile or Rail is the net width of the
Stile or Rail.
If you highlight a Stile or Rail in the Section area of the Door Manager, you will see the Stile or
Rail width, and an "Extra Width". Remember, the overall width of the Stile or Rail is the default
value, PLUS the Profile for the Inside Edge, if any.
You will note that in the graphic above that the Left Stile, Right Stile, Top Rail, and Bottom Rail
all preset to 2 1/8". In the graphic below the Left Stile of a Door is highlighted. If this Door were
being produced, the finished width of the Left Stile would be 2 ½". You will notice that the width
of the Stile says "Width" + "Extra" these two measurements must add up to the overall width of
the finished Stile. Since this Door is using a 3/8" Inside Edge Profile, setting the Width to 2 1/8"
(2 ½ - 3/8 = 2 1/8) under "Default Rail & Stile Widths" will automatically fill in the "Width" portion
of the "Width" + "Extra" with the 2 1/8" needed.

                                                               © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
You will note that the Mid Rail and the Mid Stile in this scenario should be set to 1 ¾". This is
because to achieve a 2 ½" finished size you have to take into account the 3/8" Inside Edge
Profile on both sides of the Mid Stiles and Rails.
2 x 3/8 IEP = ¾
2 ½ - ¾ = 1 ¾
Frame - Miter

           Associations

Doors that should change Construction style based on pre-determined size requirements or
conditions require Associations.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
In the above illustration we have established minimum and maximum sizes for the Square Raised
Panel Door.

For example I have a square raised panel Door and I would normally not make this Door any less
in width or length than 8 inches. Because the Top Rail is 2 inches, the Bottom Rail is 2 inches, my
raised panel detail is 1 ¼ inches all around, and I would want a flat area on the panels of no less
than 1 ½ inches wide. This all adds up to 8 inches if I make the Door any less than 8 inches in
height it gets dangerous to run the panel on my shaper.

When the Square Raised Panel Door is used and the Width or Length of the Door is 8" or less
then the Solid Wood Door Style is used.

When the Width is greater than 8" but 24" or less then the Square Raised Panel is used.

When the Width is greater than 24" but 42" or less then the Vertical Split Raised Panel is used.

When the Length is greater than 8" but 32" or less then the Square Raised Panel is used.

When the Length is greater than 32" but 64" or less then the Square Raised Panel is used.

And anything greater than 42" wide and 64" long will be a Slab (plywood).

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
So using Associations I have set a size limit of 8 inches for the length and the width. When I am in
a Job and the Door becomes 8 inches or less in length or width, CABINET VISION will
automatically replace the Square Raised Panel Door with the Solid Wood Door. I have also set a
size limit of 32 inches for the length. When I am in a job and the Door becomes 32 inches or taller
CABINET VISION will automatically replace the Door with a Vertical Split Raised Panel Door.
In situations where the left and right Doors should mirror each other, use the Mirrored Right Style
option to assign an alternate Right Door Style to use. Simply create both the Left and Right
versions of the Door. Then select the left Door and assign the right Door here. When you choose
the left Door as your default Door in a Job, the Mirrored Right Style Door will thereafter be used
when right hinging is called for.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Material Filter

"Cherry", "Maple", "Oak", and "Paint Grade" Material Schedules for use with this Door.

      Profile Filter

Profile Filters are not required but are a good option if you want to limit what Profiles are available
for the current Door Style. Simply add any of the Available Profiles on the left to the list on the
right. When you start a new Job, you will select the Door at the Job Properties tab and it should
give you the opportunity at that time to select the profiles that will be used in that particular Job
from the Profiles that you have made available for that Door.
Simply select the Profile Type to see the list of that type.
There are four different types of profiles.

   Inside Edge - The Inside Edge is used when you have a frame around the Door and the frame is
assembled with cope & stick construction. Inside Edges are important because they can,
depending on the Extended Property, affect the size of your Door parts.

   Outside Edge - The Outside Edge is a shape you will cut around the outside of the Door. Outside

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Edges do not affect the size of your Door parts.
   Raised Panel - The Raised Panel is the shape you will cut along the outside of the Door panel.

Usually done around the edges of a Raised Panel. Panel details do not affect your Door parts
sizes.

   Route - The Route is the shape of the cutter you would use if you where going to route a design
into the face of the Door using a Door jig.
The Profile Cost associated with the selected Profile is also displayed and can be edited from
here.

      3D View

  In the 3D View you will see a graphic representation of the Door that is similar to the graphic
  representation that will appear in a Job. This view may be rotated, zoomed, and rendered as if it
  were in a Job. Also, the Door may be exploded or bent to give you a more detailed view. Following
  are the sidebar options when in 3D View.

 1. Sample Material - Material - Use this option to specify the Material to view this Door in this 3D
      View.

 2. Sample Profiles - Outside - Use this option to specify the Outside Edge Profile on this Door in
      this 3D View. This option will apply only to those Edges defined as Outside in the Door's
      Properties.

 3. Sample Profiles - Inside - Use this option to specify the Inside Edge Profile on this Door in
      this 3D View.

 4. Sample Profiles - Panel - Use this option to specify the Panel Edge Profile on this Door in this
      3D View.

 5. Sample Profiles - Route - Use this option to specify the Route to assign to a Route Path on
      this Door in this 3D View.

 6. Sample Profiles - Fingerpull - Use this option to specify the Finger Pull Profile on this Door in
      this 3D View.This option will apply only to those Edges defined as Finger Pull in the Door's

        Section

  The Section View is is where your Door will be designed by adding Stiles and Rails if required, as
  well as modifying their size, shape, and joinery.

  The idea behind the Door Section Editor is that you would add Stiles and Rails, if that were the

                                                                        © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
type of Door you are working on. And then you would click on each Part (Stiles, Rails, Panel) one
at a time and make sure that they are the size you would cut them if you were going to make this
sample size Door. CABINET VISION will then use these sample Part sizes to give you the correct
cut-list for whatever size Doors your Job requires.

                      When entering the sample Part sizes you should enter finished Part sizes not
               rough cut Part sizes. The exception being, that some parts have an "Extra box, so you
               can add in an extra amount to the Part.
If you are buying your Doors you don't need to worry about the Parts being the correct size. Just
make the Door look like the Door you want.

Panel Type

The first step in the Door Section Editor would be to click in the middle of the Door and select the
"Type" of panel for your Door. In the screen below I have selected "Raised Panel" as the type of
panel for this Door.

You can also right click in the middle of the Door to select the panel type.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
By selecting "Raised Panel" as my panel type, I have performed two functions. First I have told
CABINET VISION I want this Panel to be a Raised Panel "Type" Panel. And second I have told
CABINET VISION that I want to make this Panel out of whatever Material I selected for "Raised
Panel" when I filled out my Door Material Schedules.

There are seven panel types to choose from

· None - Most commonly used if your Door has no Panel and consists only of Stiles and Rails.

· Raised - most commonly used for solid lumber.

· Flat - most commonly used for thin plywood or thin panel stock.

· Glass - most commonly used for glass.

· H Slats - most commonly used for tambour Doors with the slats going left and right. If you never
   use this type of panel you could assign it as cloth or some other Material that you do use.

· V Slats - most commonly used for tambour door with the slats going up and down. If you never
   use this type of panel you could assign it as cloth or some other Material that you do use.

· Slab - most commonly used for thick plywood or thick panel stock.

With the panel highlighted by clicking on it, the Door Properties in the sidebar display the width
and height of the panel. Additionally, you may change the amount of inset the Panel has. Panel
Inset is that portion of the panel which fits into the Stile and Rail. The values you enter here is the
overall inset.

Horizontal Grain

This option is only available when the panel is highlighted. The default value is vertical grain.
Selecting Yes in this box will change the panel to horizontal grain.

Panel Height/Width Locking

If your Door has more than one panel and you select one of them, there will be two sidebar
properties named Lock Width and Lock Height. These properties allow you to lock the width
and/or height of a panel so that when you are in a Job the locked panel will remain the same size
when the Door grows or shrinks in width or height.

Once you have checked the part sizes for the sample Door. The next step is to click on the
"Profile" tab and select the Profiles you wish to use with this Door.

Stiles & Rails

The second step is to add any necessary Mid-Stiles and/or Mid-Rails. To do this simply select the
Panel and use the Split options in the ribbonbar.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The order in which you add the parts determines their joinery. If you add the Rails before the
Stiles, the Rails will run long.
If you choose, you can miter the Stiles and Rails by clicking off of the Door and onto the screen
enabling the Miter Corner Property in the sidebar.

3. Horizontal Split - Will split the selected panel with Mid Rails creating the number of specified

    Sections/Panels.
4. Vertical Multi Split - Will split the selected panel with Mid Stiles creating the number of

    specified Sections/Panels.
5. Delete - Allows the deletion of the selected Stile/Rail.

What is an Intelli-Joint?

An Intelli-Joint applies operations to separate Parts that come together. When the two Parts come
together in a specified manner (the Parts must either touch or be at an exact specified distance
from each other in order to trigger the Intelli-Joint to be applied), you may have the Intelli-Joint
place operations on either of the two Parts or both of them.

Intelli-Joint Ribbonbar

Following are the options available in the ribbonbar.

             Return

       Will Return you to the System Level.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
     New
Option to Name and create a New Intelli-Joint.

      Copy
Option to Copy the selected Intelli-Joint.

       Delete
Option to delete the selected Intelli-Joint

        Rename
Option to rename the selected Intelli-Joint.

       Mirror
Option to Mirror the selected Intelli-Joint. Mirroring the Intelli-Joint creates a copy of that joint
and changes the face of operations in the new joint to the mirror opposite of the original
operation. For example, if you mirror an Intelli-Joint vertically and there is an operation that
is performed on the top face, the mirrored operation in the new joint will appear on the
bottom face. Horizontal mirroring changes the new operation from left to right (and vice
versa). You also have the ability to mirror both horizontally and vertically at the same time.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
      Intelli-Joint Selector

       Option to select which of the existing Intelli-Joints you would like to edit.
               Preview

       Opens the Intelli-Joint Viewer allowing you to simulate your Intelli-Joint on objects.
An Intelli-Joint is considered, by CABINET VISION, as a Part. This means that an Intelli-Joint has
the standard nine parameters that all Parts in CABINET VISION have. At the right of this interface,
there are 3 dynamic views of the current Intelli-Joint, see a detail of those views below:

In the box on the top of the above picture, you can see the "normal" face of the Intelli-Joint. The
Intelli-Joint appears in green with operations in blue and red. The origin point for the Intelli-Joint is
at the bottom left corner of the green rectangle representing it. Notice that operations may be
placed outside of the boundaries of the Intelli-Joint.
The middle box in the picture above shows the view of the Intelli-Joint as if you were looking down

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
the length of the Intelli-Joint with the origin point on the closer end. To assist in your understanding
of the perspective, the operations are the same color in all views. Therefore, the red hole in the
picture at the top is the same as the red hole in the middle picture and the red hole in the bottom
picture.
The bottom box is a perspective view of the Intelli-Joint.
You may zoom in or out of any of the three views. To zoom in, simply click in that view window. To
zoom out, right click in the window.
The next area (pictured below) is the Operations Area where you can input the values for the
Operations that you will be adding to the Intelli-Joint.

available here:

            New Operation

       This option may be used to add a user defined Parameter to the selected Operation.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
   To add a Parameter:
1. Click the Add button.
2. Name the Parameter in the Name field.
3. Choose either a value to set the Parameter to or you can choose to set the value through an

    equation.
   In the following example, I have added a Parameter named MyParameter with a value of 99
   onto an Operation in an Intelli-Joint.

                                                               © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       This MyParameter = 99 parameter will now show up in the Object Tree under the Operation
       added by the Intelli-Joint.

A useful X= Parameter example:

Take a Bore you are adding and click X= and add a Parameter to it called _FUDI and give it a
value of 100 and that Operation will force the side of the Part it is on up in the nest on two sided
Material.

At the far end of the toolbar is the ID for the Intelli-Joint which is useful when writing UCS's
applying Intelli-Joints.

Operations List

This is the area where Operations that are included/added to the Intelli-Joint are displayed and
modified. There are eleven columns (Properties) you can control here.

       Operation - This is a name for the Operation. This Name will display in the Operations area
       of the Part Editor.

       Primary - This controls where the Operation goes. It can be placed on either the Primary or
       the Secondary Part.

       Type - This option allows you to control the Operation Type (Bore or Dado).

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Face - The operation is not limited to being on the face of the Part that actually touches the
other Part (the normal face). The operation can be on the Left, Right, Top, or Bottom Face.
Pos X - The X position of the Operation if the Intelli-Joint is viewed in the normal orientation
(the top view of the Intelli-Joint at the right of the Intelli-Joint Catalog window). Click the
button and the field and you can then type a hard Value, a Variable, a Formula, or a
combination of the three.

               There are nine pre-configured Variables you can use to help build formulas, they
               are:
      DX - This represents the Width of the Intelli-Joint.
      DY - This represents the Length of the Intelli-Joint.
      DZ - This represents the Thickness of the Intelli-Joint.
      _MP:DX - This represents the Width of the Part the Intelli-Joint is attached to.
      _MP:DY - This represents the Length of the Part the Intelli-Joint is attached to.
      _MP:DZ - This represents the Thickness of the Part the Intelli-Joint is attached to.
      _SP:DX - This represents the Width of the Part the Intelli-Joint is contacting.
      _SP:DY - This represents the Length of the Part the Intelli-Joint is contacting.
      _SP:DZ - This represents the Thickness of the Part the Intelli-Joint is contacting.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Pos Y - The Y position of the Operation if the Intelli-Joint is viewed in the normal orientation.
       Depth - The Depth of the Operation.
       Space Length - If the Operation is a Dado, this is the Length of the Dado. If the Operation is
       a Hole, this is the space between Holes (for multiple Holes).
       Diam. Width - This is the Diameter if the Operation is a Hole and is the Width if the
       Operation is a Dado.
       Quantity - This is the number of Holes if the Operation is a Hole. If the Operation is a Dado
       a Quantity of 0 indicates no dado which could be useful as a result from a formula
       calculation, any number 1 or higher for a Dado is considered 1.
       Tool - This is used to specify a certain Tool to cut out the operation. Selecting this field will
       display a Tool selector in the Operations Tool Bar. If Auto is selected, normal Automatic Tool
       Selection Logic is followed. Also, if the selected Tool won't work for some reason, the
       Automatic Tool Selection Logic will be followed.

Techniques for Creating Molding Shapes

The easiest method of adding a Molding Shape is to import it into the Molding Manager. Editing is
similar, and uses the same editing tools common to Solid to create the final shape.

      Importing A DXF file to Define A Molding

       In the following example, a DXF file such as the one shown, will be imported into Molding
       Shape for use as a Light Rail.

1. Take your new Molding to the Shape Editor .

2. Click Select All  then click Delete          .

3. Click Insert DXF .
4. Click the browse button to browse to the location of your DXF file.

                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
5. Once you have Opened your DXF file from the Browse dialog click Import.

                                                               © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
6. Click OK to Import the DXF into the Shape Editor.
7. Pick its location in the Shape Editor. It doesn't really matter where you place it.
8. Once placed select the Reference option and pick the point which you want to be the

    Reference point on the Molding. See the Shape Editor topic for more information on the
    Reference option.

                                                               © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       9. Click Return to Save the shape of your new Molding.

                      Keep in mind you have full CAD editing capability here so you can Flip,
               Mirror, Rotate, Scale, Stretch, and modify the imported shape in any way prior to
               saving it.

Importing an Image file to Define A Molding

When Importing an Image file you bring in an Image that will allow you to get the general
shape of the Molding by tracing it utilizing the Shape Editor Tools. There are two additional
Tools available when a Bitmap is imported that allow you to Scale and/or Align the Bitmap to
facilitate proper tracing. Once you have the Bitmap sized as you need simply use the CAD
tools to trace the image to get the final shape you desire.

Molding Sets

The Molding Shape Editor, when dealing with a Molding Set, allows you to add Moldings to
the Set as well as control the added Molding's positions within the Molding Set.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
              Make sure you have "Snap To Points" turned on as it will make placement of the
       Moldings within the Molding Set more accurate.
Once you click the Insert option you will be able to select your Category and Molding from
the sidebar and drag it into the Shape Editor. Unlike when shaping a Molding you can not
control the position of the Reference point but instead must build your Molding Set around
the Reference Point. That is the placement point for the Molding when laying it out in your
Job. You can drag as many existing Moldings into your Molding Set as you like.

When selecting a specific Molding within the Molding Set you will have the following
Property options in the sidebar:

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

    Name - Displays the Name of the selected Molding.
    Origin X - Controls the X Position of the selected Molding.
    Origin Y - Controls the Y Position of the selected Molding.
    Width - Displays the Width of the selected Molding.
    Height - Displays the Height of the selected Molding.
    Angle - Controls the rotation angle for the selected Molding.
    Mirror - Will Mirror the selected Molding.

The Assembly Manager is the utility that you will use to "teach" CABINET VISION the manner in
which you build your Assemblies. The following Assembly Types can be configured here:
· Assembly - Includes both Cabinets and Closets
· Drawer - Roll Out - Includes both Drawers and Roll Outs
· Counter Top - Counter Tops
The answers that you give to the questions in this area will create a set of rules that your

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Assemblies will follow when they are constructed. If you have a situation where you need a
specific Job, Room, or even an Assembly to follow a different set of rules, there are several ways
that you can make changes to each of those levels. Therefore, the set of rules that you create in
the Assembly Manager should reflect the "normal" manner in which Assemblies of this type are
built.

                      You are not limited to a certain number of different Construction Methods,
               therefore, you may create as many different Construction Methods as you may need to
               cover all the types of construction that you use.

Assembly
Assembly

In the above view of the Assembly Manager, you see an Assembly Construction Method named
"Face Frame" that uses a Face Frame Style of Construction.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The Construction Style you select for your Construction Method is very important. This selection
determines the Parts available for your Construction Method as well as options within each Part
that are specific and necessary for the Style of Construction you need to configure. There are 5
possible Case Construction Styles:

       Face Frame -

       A face frame in cabinet making is the frame fixed to the front of a cabinet carcass which
       obscures the edges of the carcass and provides the fixing point for doors and other external
       hardware. A face frame provides strength to the front of a cabinet and is also considered a
       visual feature of particular styles of furniture. In CABINET VISION selecting the Face Frame
       Style turns on the Face Frame Branch and its Parts in the Construction Method. Door Sizing
       for this Construction Style is controlled by the Hinge Overlays in the Material Manager.

       Frameless -

       Frameless construction in cabinetmaking refers to the construction of cabinets using flat
       panels of engineered wood, usually particle board, plywood or medium-density fiberboard,
       rather than the traditional frame and panel construction. Frameless cabinets typically make
       use of edge banding to conceal the edge of the carcass. This is most commonly seen in
       European modular-style kitchens. In CABINET VISION selecting the Frameless Style turns
       off the Face Frame Branch and removes the Machining options from the Construction
       Method. Door Sizing for this Construction Style is controlled by the Reveals within the Exterior
       Case Branch.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       32 Millimeter -
       Is the same as the Frameless Construction Style visually. In CABINET VISION selecting the
       32mm Style turns off the Face Frame Branch and turns on the Machining options from the
       Construction Method. Door Sizing for this Construction Style is controlled by the Reveals
       within the Exterior Case Branch.

       Frame Overlay -
       Is the same as the Face Frame Construction Style with the exception that Doors are sized
       by the Reveals rather than the Overlays. This allows you to give the look of European
       Cabinetry (Frameless/32mm) with the added strength of the Face Frame. In CABINET
       VISION selecting the Frame Overlay Style turns on the Face Frame Branch and its Parts in
       the Construction Method. Door Sizing for this Construction Style is controlled by the Reveals
       within the Exterior Case Branch.

       Closet 32mm -
       Is similar to the 32mm Style with the exception of the addition of Parts in the Construction
       Method specific to Closets. Door Sizing for this Construction Style is controlled by the Reveals
       within the Exterior Case Branch.
Typically, you would want to name your Construction Method something that indicates its
contents, for example: If you only have one Face Frame Construction Method, then the name
"Face Frame" would suffice. However, if you have several Face Frame methods, then your names
should be more descriptive like "Face Frame No Back," or "Face Frame Dado Back." Since Style
determines Door Sizing this is a very important selection.

How to Create a New Construction Method

There are several ways to begin a new Construction Method. You could start with one of the
Construction Methods that are pre-set in CABINET VISION and make modifications to them. You
could copy one of the existing Construction Methods and then make changes to the copy so that it
meets your requirements. Finally, you could create a brand new Construction Method by clicking
on the Create a New Construction Method button (or by clicking on the Construction menu at the
top of the Assembly Manager window and then clicking Create New Method). For the purposes of
this example, we will create a brand new Construction Method because the options will be the
same.
1. Click the Create New Construction Method option in the ribbonbar.
2. In the pop up window, give the Construction Method a name and select the Construction Style
that should apply to this Construction Method. You should also select the Connection Machining to
use for the options in the Connections area. Connection Machining is configured through the
Connection Manager.

3. When you click OK, you will see the following window. Notice that the name of the Construction
Method is "My 32mm Construction" and the Construction Style is 32 Millimeter.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
4. Next, you should begin to run through the Assembly Manager and answer the questions in
each section. Start by clicking on the + symbol next to Interior Case and then double clicking
Adjustable Shelf. Double clicking on a branch (such as Adjustable Shelf) runs the Part Wizard for
that branch. You can also run the Part Wizard for a branch by clicking the branch to select it and
then clicking the Modify option in the ribbonbar. You will then see the following window:

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The Assembly Manager consists mainly of options that you may choose between. In our example,
the first option that you must configure concerns Adjustable Shelf banding.

              You will find that the illustrations can be very helpful tools when answering the
       Assembly Manager questions. The illustrations will change according to the choices that you
       make and they should give you an idea of what will happen in the Construction Method if
       certain choices are made. However, you should not be worried if the pictures don't match
       your Construction 100%. Simply choose the options that most closely resemble your
       Construction Method.

      Break Outs

         When answering questions in the Assembly Manager, you will notice that you are
         configuring the "Default" which applies to all Cabinet Classes. You might however
         for some reason need to Break Out the question if a different Class object needs
         a different configuration.

Example of the use of a Break Out:

       A classic example of the need to add a break out is when the Top type is different between
       Base Cabinets and Upper and Tall Cabinets. In this example, we use Stretchers in Base
       Cabinets and a full Top in the Upper and Tall Cabinets.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
In order to define a different configuration for other Class objects simply click the + Tab next
to Default then select the Class you need to define a different Configuration for.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       In this case i have selected Upper and Tall in order to specify full Tops for them.

5. Then, simply go through the rest of the questions by answering them and then clicking Next.
When you answer the final question in the branch, you will need to click the Finish button.
6. When you finish the questions for the first branch, move on to the next one and answer the
questions there.
7. Complete the rest of the Branches for this Construction Method adding break outs for any
situations that require it.
8. Test your Construction Method in a Job. The easiest way to begin testing a Construction
Method is to create a Job with a single Cabinet. Start out with a single Base Cabinet in the Job
making sure that the overall size of the Cabinet is one that you can easily work out a cut list for
comparison. Also make sure that you are using a valid Material Schedule for this Job and that
each part of the Cabinet is made out of the correct Material.

                      Part thickness, which has a huge influence on the cut list, is controlled by the
               Material Schedules and NOT the Construction Method. Check each Part of this test
               Cabinet and make sure that it is sized correctly. For any Parts that are incorrect, try to
               look at the orthographic views to determine where the problem lies.
Next, put a second Base Cabinet next to the first one. Each Cabinet should now have an
Unfinished End and other properties that go along with a Cabinet next to another Cabinet.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Follow the same procedure for Upper Cabinets, Tall Cabinets, Vanity, and finally Corner Cabinets.

Fixed Shelf
Fixed Shelf Branch

A Fixed Shelf is yet another horizontal part that is permanently mounted within a Cabinet. A Fixed
Shelf is sometimes called a Horizontal Partition. There is no option to adjust the setback of the
Fixed Shelf front, as it is flush with either the back of the Face Frame or the Case, depending on
the Construction Style. Typically, a Fixed Shelf divides a Tall Cabinet. Face Frame Cabinets
typically have Mid Rails in front of Fixed Shelves, while Frameless Cabinets split Doors or Doors
and Drawers at the Fixed Shelf.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

Finished End
Finished End

There are a few things to consider when answering the questions in the Construction Method for
Finished Ends. When choosing the type of Finished End, click each option and look at the graphic.
You will see that several of the End Types have a structure behind them. This structure is the Sub
End. There is also an option for "skins" for Finished Ends. It is important to understand what Skins
are not. They are never plastic laminate, nor are they sheet veneer. This is because both of those
items are handled in the Material Schedules as Horizontal and Vertical Laminate. Additionally, you
may find that you have chosen Standard or another Finished End Type only to find several
questions following regarding Applied Doors and/or Applied Panels.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
                      Remember, when this occurs, answer the questions with the "What if" approach.
               CABINET VISION is aware that you have selected a different default End Type, yet, it
               remains possible to change a particular Cabinet within CABINET VISION to have an
               Applied Door or Applied Panel, and in that event, the information would be necessary.

      Finished End Conditions

               Standard and Panelized Ends

               These end types will follow the Construction Method settings for Finished Ends

               Applied End and Applied Doors

               These types of Finished Ends consist of two parts - a Sub End and a Finished End (or
               a DOR for an Applied Door). The Sub End part will follow the Construction Method
               settings for a Sub End, while the Finished End (or DOR) part will follow the
               Construction Method settings for a Finished End.
               The internal Parts (Top, Stretchers, Deck, Nailers, etc.) will respond to Sub End
               standards where applicable.
               It is important to note that if the Sub Ends have a specified inside scribe amount, this
               could cause the Applied Part (the Finished End or DOR) to extend beyond the outside
               of the Cabinet.
               The Front Toe, Side Toe, and Back Toe will respond to Finished End
               Construction Method settings.

               Skinned and Laminated Ends

               These types of Finished Ends are also made up of two Parts: an Unfinished End and a
               Skin (SLF/SRF) or Laminate (LAMV). These types of Ends are considered to be a
               single part by the Construction Method and are treated as Finished Ends.
               All internal Parts (Top, Stretchers, Deck, Nailers, etc.) will respond to the Finished End
               Construction Method.
The following diagrams show the options available in the Finished End Branch. Click a specific
option in the diagram for more information or continue through this topic for information on all the
options.

Reveals

32mm Construction Styles. In standard Face Frame Construction the Hinge Overlay controls the Door
Sizes except for the Gap for Pair Doors which is controlled here with the Vertical Reveal
(Standard #350). Also, if building Face Frame Cabinets with Inset Doors the Doors size is
controlled using this Reveals Branch, the Reveals here are used to set the Inset Gaps.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

1/8 of an inch, or combinations thereof are used, so that face reveals read 1/8 of an inch on
adjoining Cabinets.

are using 2 sided Materials for the Top of a Cabinet. You can select whether the "good side" faces in

Assemblies.

Line Boring
Line Boring

This option sets Line Boring options, it sets the dimensions, type, and position conditions.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Line Boring is typically used for Adjustable Shelf, and Hardware Mounting (Hinges, Drawer Guides,
Wire Baskets, and Hanging Section).

One additional consideration regarding Hardware location. If you choose to use (32mm) System
Holes for location of your Hardware, the information you have setup in the appropriate area may
be effected. I.E., if you choose to mount Drawer Guides in system holes, your Drawer Boxes will be
sized accordingly. Additionally, you may choose to use the option to split Drawer Faces and Doors
on system holes if you choose to mount on system holes.

Drawer Box - Roll Out
Drawer Box - Roll Out

       or

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
In the above view of the Assembly Manager, you see a Drawer Box Construction Method named
"5 Piece Drawer" that uses a Five Piece Drawer Box Style of Construction.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The Construction Style you select for your Construction Method is very important. This selection
determines the Parts available for your Construction Method as well as options within each Part
that are specific and necessary for the Style of Construction you need to configure. There are 5
possible Construction Styles.

 Five Piece Drawer - This Drawer Box will include 2 Sides, a Back, a Sub-Front, and a Bottom.

 Four Piece Drawer - This Drawer Box will include 2 Sides, a Back, and a Bottom. Select this
   option if your Drawer Front is the actual front of your Drawer Box.

 Roll Out - This Roll Out will include 2 Sides, a Back, a Roll Out Front, and a Bottom.

 System Drawer - This Drawer Box will include a Back, Bottom, and Drawer System Guides.

 System Roll Out - This Roll Out will include a Back, Bottom, Roll Out Front and Drawer System
   Guides.

Typically, you would want to name your Construction Method something that indicates its
contents, for example: If you only have one Five Piece Drawer Construction Method, then the
name "5 Piece Drawer" would suffice. However, if you have several Five Piece methods, then your
names should be more descriptive like "5 Piece Dovetail," or "5 Piece Miter."

How To Create a New Construction Method

There are several ways to begin a new Construction Method. You could start with one of the

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Construction Methods that are pre-set in CABINET VISION and make modifications to them. You
could copy one of the existing Construction Methods and then make changes to the copy so that it
meets your requirements. Finally, you could create a brand new Construction Method by clicking
on the Create a New Construction Method option . For the purposes of this example, we will
create a brand new Construction Method because the options will be the same.
1. Click the Create New Construction Method option in the ribbonbar.
2. In the pop up window, give the Construction Method a name and select the Construction Style
that should apply to this Construction Method. You should also select the Connection Machining to
use for the options in the Connections area. Connection Machining is configured through the
Connection Manager.

3. When you click OK, you will see the following window. Notice that the name of the Construction
Method is "My Five Piece" and the Construction Style is "Five Piece Drawer Box".

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
4. Next, you should begin to run through the Drawer Box Construction Method and answer the
questions for each Part. Start by double clicking General. Double clicking on a Part (such as
General) runs the Part Wizard for that Part. You can also run the Part Wizard for a part by clicking
the branch to select it and then clicking the Modify option in the ribbonbar. You will then see the
following window:

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The Drawer Box Construction Method consists mainly of options that you may choose between. In
our example, the first option that you must choose between is concerning the Cost of the Drawer
Box.

              You will find that the pictures are very helpful tools when answering the Drawer Box
       questions. The pictures will change according to the choices that you make and they should
       give you an idea of what will happen in the Construction Method if certain choices are made.
       However, you should not be worried if the pictures don't match your Construction 100%.
       Simply choose the options that most closely resemble your Construction Method.

5. Then, simply go through the rest of the questions by answering them and then clicking Next.
When you answer the final question in the branch, you can click the Finish button.

6. When you finish the questions for the first Part, move on to the next one and answer the
questions there.

7. Complete the Drawer Box Construction Method.

8. Test your Construction Method in a Job. The easiest way to begin testing a Construction
Method is to create a Job with a single Cabinet. Making sure that the overall size of the Drawer
Box is one that you can easily work out a cut list for comparison. Also make sure that you are
using a valid Drawer Box Material Schedule for this Job and that each part of the Drawer Box is
made out of the correct Material.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
                      Part thickness, which has a huge influence on the cut list, is controlled by the
               Material Schedules and NOT the Drawer Box Construction Method. Check each Part of
               this test Drawer Box and make sure that it is sized correctly. For any Parts that are
               incorrect, try to look at the orthographic views to determine where the problem lies.

      Drawer Box Cost (Standard #137)

       The price in this box will be added to the Bid for each box (Drawer or Roll Out) that has been
       included in the Job. This will be added to the Bid under any Line Item where the Bid Method
       "Use Drawer Catalog Pricing" or "Use Roll Out Catalog Pricing" is selected.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Drawer Box Labor (Standard #93)

The time (in minutes) in this box will be added to the Labor Estimate.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Height Specifications (Standard #1)

You have two choices for how the Box Height is calculated.
· To Fit Using Guide Clearance - This option will look at the Drawer Guide in use on the

   Box and calculate the Height based on the Opening Height where the Drawer is placed
   minus the Top and Bottom Clearance set on the Drawer Guide in the Material Catalog.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
· Standard Heights - This option will allow you to establish a series of Standard Heights.
   When this option is selected the next screen will be Standard Heights (#2).

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Standard Heights (Standard #2)

This area allows you to list all the possible Standard Heights for the Box. The Heights must
be entered from Largest to Smallest. There is no limit to how many Standard Heights you
can define. CABINET VISION will choose from that list and build the largest Drawer Box that
will fit the opening minus the value set by Top and Bottom Clearance for the Drawer Guide in
use. If it happens that the smallest Standard Height is still too large, being that it is the last
available size on the list, CABINET VISION will default to the actual required size for the
Drawer Box Height. See the Drawer Box sizing topic for more information.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Depth Clearance (Standard #5)

This option allows you to specify the "Minimum Distance Required Between the Drawer Box/
Roll Out Back and the Face of the Assembly Unfinished Back"

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
      Depth Specification (Standard #6)

       You have two choices for how the Box Depth is calculated.
· To Fit Using Depth Clearance - This option will look at the value previously established in

   "Standard Heights (#2)" and subtract that value from the actual Opening Depth where the
   Drawer is being placed to come up with the exact Drawer Box Depth.

                                                                    © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
· Standard Depths - This option will allow you to establish a series of Standard Depths. When
   this option is selected the next screen will be Standard Depths (#7).

                                                                    © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Standard Depths (Standard #7)

This area allows you to list all the possible Standard Depths for the Box. The Depths must
be entered from Largest to Smallest. There is no limit to how many Standard Depths you
can define. CABINET VISION will choose from that list and build the largest Drawer Box that
will fit the opening minus the value set in "Depth Clearance (#5)". If it happens that the
smallest Standard Depth is still too large, being that it is the last available size on the list,
CABINET VISION will default to the actual required size for the Drawer Box Depth. See the
Drawer Box sizing topic for more information.

There are five options for the Top Recess on Splash Edge:
 No Change - This would be flush as demonstrated in the image for the selection in the Wizard.
 Recess Top - The Splash is against the Wall and you specify the distance the Top and Build Up

   is away from the Wall. See sample image for selection in the Wizard.
 Pre-Scribe Edge - The Splash is against the Wall and you specify the distance the Top and

   Build Up is away from the Wall. You will next be prompted for the Span which will be cut fully
   through the Top Surface. See sample image for selection in the Wizard.
 Prep Edge For Scribe - The Splash is against the Wall and you specify the distance the Top
   and Build Up is away from the Wall. You will next be prompted for the Span which will be cut to
   Depth based on an additional prompt for the Top scribe Thickness. See sample image for
   selection in the Wizard.
 Recess Build Up - The Splash and Top is against the Wall and you specify the distance the
   Build Up is away from the Wall. See sample image for selection in the Wizard.

Licensing - Getting Started
You can only install the License after CABINET VISION has been installed on your PC.
When first starting CABINET VISION without an active License you will be presented with the
License Setup Wizard.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Choose License Type

Step 1 - Select from the available Licensing methods. The method must match the Licence
Delivery Note which was emailed to you.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Step 2 - Click the "Install" button.
Step 3 - Enter the Servercode from the License Delivery Note which was emailed to you. You
should have received your Servercode via an email from Vero Software Limited
orders@verosoftware.com that contains your Servercode (see image below). If you did not receive this
email then you will need to contact your CABINET VISION Software Representative to have it
emailed to you.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Step 3 - Click the Install button.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
When performing a CV Network Installation Sentinel RMS License Server will be installed on your
Server automatically.
You can install the licenses on the license server from a CLS that is installed on either the server
or a client PC (with Administrator Mode enabled).
1. From the CV Splash Screen Utilities tab open the License Manager.
2. On the Server menu, click Search Network to list the Sentinel RMS server(s). Select the

    server you wish to connect to and click Change Active Server. Confirm that you wish to
    change the active server, and close the dialog.
3. Select your chosen server in the list and click the Install License button.
4. In the dialog that opens, you have the option to request your license file over the Internet or
    Browse to a file that you have already downloaded or received by email.
 To request a license file over the Internet
1. Type in or copy-and-paste your Servercode.
2. Click Request License File to request a license file from the CV server over the Internet. Click
    Next.
3. In the license activation dialog, check the details are correctly displayed and click Next.
4. In the confirmation dialog, click Finish to install the new license file.
To install a file that has been sent to you
1. Type in or copy-and-paste your Servercode.
2. Click Use License File.
3. Browse for and select the license file (the license file will be named

       .one, .clss or .clsn, i.e. 1234-4567-1234-4567-1234-4567.one for example).
4. Click Next.
5. In the confirmation dialog, click Finish to complete the installation. Your licenses are now

    installed and ready to use.
Note that network licenses cannot be revoked using the License Manager.
This completes the Server and license installation.
Once a license server has been set up, follow this procedure on the client PCs:

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
1. Install the Workstation following the Network Install for a Workstation section Install Help
    document.

2. From the CV Splash Screen Utilities tab open the License Manager.
3. On the Server menu, click Search Network to list the Sentinel RMS server(s).
4. Select the server that you wish to connect to and click Change Active Server.
5. Confirm that you wish to change the active server, and close the dialog.

Selecting Licenses

Click on a module license and click < or < to select it.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 You can now run the software using the functionality covered by the selected licenses (seen
   on the left in the list above.)

 Please note these licenses are only effectively 'pre-selected' for your PC. To run the
   software, the licenses must be available on the server at run time.

                                                              © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
You can setup License Profiles to make this more 'automated'. Please see the License Profiles topic
for more information.
License Profiles allow you to save multiple profiles containing groups of Licenses which can then
be selected when starting up the application.

1. In the dialog, enable Use License Profiles.
2. Enter a Profiles Location. Use the Browse button to select a directory, if required.
3. Click Ask For Profile On Startup to ensure that a profile is selected when starting an

    application.
4. Select the Current Profile to be used from the drop-down list.
5. Select Save to save an new or existing profile or Save As to make a copy of the current profile.
6. Click Delete to remove the selected profile.
Some licensing functions (installing, updating, revoking and commuting network licenses) can only
be accessed in Administrator Mode.
By default, Administrator Mode is enabled when the software is installed on the PC, allowing client
PCs access to administrator functions. To prevent users from accessing those functions, you need
to disable Administrator Mode and password protect it.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 Setting a Password for Administrator Mode

 1. From the CV Splash Screen Utilities tab open the License Manager.
 2. On the Tools menu in the License Manager, click Administrator Mode to disable it.
 3. Click Administrator Mode again to display the Administrator Mode Password dialog.
 4. Click Change Password.
 5. In the Change Password dialog, type in the current password. By default, the password is left

      blank.
 6. Enter and confirm a new password.
 7. Uncheck Allow license commuting if you want to prevent users from commuting and returning

      network licenses on a client PC.
 8. Click Change.
 9. In the Administrator Mode Password dialog, type in the new Password and click OK.

       The password has now been set. Note that Administrator Mode is still enabled.
10. On the Tools menu, click Administrator Mode to disable it. The user cannot now install/update

      the network license file, or commute licenses (if you have unchecked the option - see step 6
      above).
  Administrator Mode cannot be enabled again without typing in the password.

 Enabling/disabling Administrator Mode

  The Administrator Mode option is a 'toggle' switch; click to switch between ON and OFF.
  If Administrator Mode has been disabled and you click the option, the Administrator Mode
  Password dialog is displayed. Type in the password to enable Administrator Mode. By default,
  the password is left blank.
  There are several things which might require you to Update your Network License:
 1. When you renew your annual maintenance if your software is tied to annual maintenance.
 2. You purchase additional software modules.
 3. You are on a monthly short term or long term payment plan.
  If you are setting up network licensing for the first time, please refer to the Server Setup topic.

                                                                        © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Preparation

1. Ensure any unexpired commuted licenses are checked in (returned).
2. If you are using a keyed network license, ensure that the key is attached to the server.

Installing the license file

You can install the licenses on the license server from a CLS that is installed on either the server
or a client PC (with Administrator Mode enabled).
1. From the CV Splash Screen Utilities tab open the License Manager.

       If the license server is already the active server, go directly to step 3.
2. Select the server you wish to connect to and click Change Active Server. Confirm that you wish

    to change the active server, and close the dialog.
3. Select the license server in the list and click the Install License button.
4. In the dialog that opens, you have the option to request your license file over the Internet or

    browse to a file that you have already downloaded or received by email.
To request a license file over the Internet
1. Click Request License File to request a license file from the CV server over the Internet.
2. In the license activation dialog, check the details are correctly displayed and click Next.
3. In the confirmation dialog, click Finish to install the new license file.
To install a file that has been sent to you
1. Click Use License File.
2. Browse for and select the license file (the license file will be named .one, .clss or .clsn, i.e.

    1234-4567-1234-4567-1234-4567.one for example).
3. Click Next.
4. In the confirmation dialog, click Finish to complete the installation.
5. The last dialog that is displayed includes an option to Remove Existing Licenses. This option

    will remove the old license file completely from the server before installing the new license file.
    It is recommended that you check this option when installing a license update.
Your updated licenses are now installed and ready to use.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
A commuted license can be used to work on your PC when you are not connected to the network
for a period of time. You cannot use a commuted license on a PC that already has a standalone
license.
If you wish to commute licenses to a PC that is not or has never been connected to the network,
please refer to the Commuting Network Licenses Remotely topic.

Commuting Licenses

1. From the CV Splash Screen Utilities tab open the License Manager.
2. Ensure the server you want to commute a license from is highlighted.
3. Right-click on the server and select Commute Configured Licenses. If you have Optional

    licenses configured you will be asked if you want to commute them.
     The Commute License dialog is displayed, showing the licenses to be commuted. Until

       commuted, their status is shown as 'Pending'. Note that you will see an additional license
       (Commute License) in the list; this is automatically added by the system.
     Note that you can select individual licenses for commuting from the Server Details list.
4. Type in the number of days you wish to commute the licenses for. The maximum number you
    can commute licenses for is 30 days.
5. Click Commute to commute the licenses, followed by OK and Close.
     You are now asked if you want to change to using the commuted licenses. If you say No you
       will need to change to the Commuter license when you are ready. To do this, select
       Commuter in the server list and click Change Active Server.
Once a license has been commuted it will not be available to anybody else until the commute time
is up or the license is returned manually to the server.
For further information please refer to the License Manager help.
There are some more advanced Licensing options utilizing the License Manager. Documentation
on those procedures are available in the License Manager Help system.

Libraries Tab

The Libraries tab is a place to use to add Libraries of functions for UCS:JSC (JavaScript UCSs) to
utilize.

In a traditional UCS (UCS:M), code is often duplicated in each UCS:M which can cause code bloat
and difficulty in ensuring propagating any modifications to the code made it to each instance of the

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
replicated code. With the added power and flexibility of JavaScript, it is even more likely there will
be a use for commonly used functions. To fulfill this need, in a UCS:JS, Libraries (Libs) can be
used to create groups of functions that can be shared between scripts without the need for
duplication.
A library will typically contain functions with related purpose, for example a math or geometry
library. In code the libraries are implemented as a JavaScript class with static methods
(functions).
class ClassName {

   method_1() { ... }
   method_2() { ... }
   method_3() { ... }
}
The name given to the JS Lib in CV will be used as the class name using the format
_libraryname. (the library name in lower case, preceded by an underscore).
Example:
A library can be created in CV called "Math"

In the code, methods for area and volume could be defined.
area(width, length)
{

   return width * length;
}
volume(width, length, depth)
{

   return width * length * depth;
}

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
In a UCS, the library can be used as follows
var width = _this.GetParameterValue('DX');
var length = _this.GetParameterValue('DY');
var depth = _this.GetParameterValue('DZ');
_this.SetParameter('MYAREA', _math.area(width, length));
_this.SetParameter('MYVOLUME', _math.volume(width, length, depth));

Public Variables

The Public Variables area in the sidebar will list any Public Variables that have been defined in the
selected UCS:M. See the Public Variables topic for more information.
Public Variables can not be defined within UCS:JS so must be manually added here. When a
UCS:JS is selected you will see the Add Public Variable icon become available. Simply define
your Public Variable here.

   New - User Created Standards Wizard

Add (link) A Part
Add (link) A Part

The Add (link) A Part UCS type is very powerful. Let's say for example you would like to add four
Shelf Clips to your Adjustable Shelves. Follow along with this Topic to find out How.
Click on the New option in the User Created Standards window.

General Tab

The General Tab is where you enter the Name and select the Type of UCS you would like to

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
create.

1. Enter a Name for the UCS. (Add 4 Shelf Clips to Each Adj Shelf)
2. For Type select Add.
3. From the list to the right select Part for the category then the Shelf Clip Part.

    · If the Shelf Clip is not in the list you must create it. Go to the Parts Manager and add it to the
       Pulls Part Group. Once added, add a Material named Shelf Pin at 1/8" thick in the Material
       Manager. Next select this Material for the Shelf Pin Part which should now be listed in your
       Pulls Material Schedule.

4. We will leave Macro Type as UCS which is the native macro language for CABINET VISION. If
    you are familiar with JavaScript and would like to use that language then you can select
    JavaScript from the list and the Wizard will construct the macro in JavaScript (UCSJS).

5. Click Next to go to the next step in the Add (Link) A Part UCS Wizard.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Link To Tab

The Link To Tab is where you select which Part you would like to Link your new Part/Operation to.

5. Select Part from the "Link To Each" section. This option is telling CABINET VISION to link
    these Shelf Pins to a certain Part.

6. Select the Adjustable Shelf from the list.
7. Click Next to go to the next step in the Add (Link) A Part UCS Wizard.

  The Conditions For Adjustable Shelf Tab allows you to filter out based on certain Adjustable Shelf
  Properties.

This Pre-Build option, when active, determines if the selected UCS is applied before or after the
Assembly is built. Select this option when using a UCS to change Assembly Construction
Parameters.

              Do not use this option if the UCS Adds, Modifies, or Deletes Parts.

Why This Tool is Available

During the Assembly build process, CABINET VISION builds the Assembly according to the
parameters generated by the Construction Method first. Then, it applies the UCS's second. In a
case where the UCS modifies the value on an Construction Method generated parameter, the
parameter was modified (in the Object Tree), but the result was not shown in the way the
Assembly was built because it was already built before the UCS modified the value. This required
the user to do a Room rebuild to cause the first step of the Assembly build process to recognize
the new value on the Construction Method generated parameter. By toggling ON 'Pre-Build', the
value of the parameter is modified PRIOR to building the Assembly.

Intended Use of This Tool

Note that this tool is intended ONLY for parameters that affect the way the Assembly Generator
builds Parts. For example, a UCS that modifies the DX, DY, DZ, AX, AY, AZ, X, Y, or Z parameters
of a Part would NOT use this toggle because these types of parameters will change the size,
position, and angle of a Part as soon as the parameter is modified. However, a UCS that modifies
or adds parameters such as BKTYPE, ESHAPL, ESHAPR, ETL, or ETR would require the
Assembly to be rebuilt AFTER these parameters are modified. The best way to understand this is
to think about what the parameter modifies. BKTYPE changes the back type, so the Assembly
would need to be rebuilt according to the Construction Method questions for Unfinished or
Finished back, depending upon what the BKTYPE parameter indicates the back type should be.
ESHAPL and ESHAPR changes the End to go to the floor, so the Assembly would need to be

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
rebuilt with an End that goes to the floor so that the Toe Parts that no longer belong, are removed.
ETL and ETR changes the End type, which requires the Assembly to be rebuilt according to the
Construction Method questions for the various types of Ends and/or other parameters (Finished,
Unfinished, Applied, Applied Door, Clipped, Radius, Angled).

How to Determine Whether to Use This Tool on a Particular UCS

The best way to determine whether the 'Pre-Build' toggle would be necessary on a particular UCS
is to try the UCS with 'Pre-Build' toggled OFF and evaluate results, as follows:
 If the expected results occur without the toggle and without a Room rebuild, then the 'Pre-Build'

   toggle is not necessary.
 If the expected results do NOT occur without the toggle UNLESS the user does a Room rebuild,

   then the 'Pre-Build' toggle being ON will most likely prevent the user from having to do a room
   rebuild.
 If the expected results do NOT occur without the toggle EVEN IF the user does a Room rebuild,
   then the 'Pre-Build' toggle will not make a difference.
Examples of UCS's on which this feature would be used:
Here are some samples of UCS's where the 'Pre-Build' toggle being ON prevents the user from
having to do a Room rebuild:
Example #1:
;Deletes Finished Back on Cabinets @ Peninsula Walls
For Each Cab Assembly
If ::DZ < Imp(.5) Then ;Looks to see if parts belong to cabinet that is on a peninsula wall
  BKTYPE = 0
End If
Example #2:
;Links Finished Left End to Cabinet
For Each CAB Assembly
ESHAPL = 2
