           Parameters

The Parameters option allows you to establish your own Custom Parameters (Attributes or Notes)
or establish the default values of System Parameters (Attributes). You can use these Parameters
to trigger UCS's, Object Intelligence, or add Notes. There are six values set here.
Prompt - This field allows you to establish a user friendly prompt or name to simplify use by other
Solid users. The Prompt value will show up on the Attributes Tab at the Parameters Class (Job/
Room/Cabinet) or in the sidebar.
Job Level Attributes Tab

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Room Level Attributes Tab

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Cabinet Parameters Tab

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Job/Room Parameter Sidebar

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Cabinet Parameter Sidebar

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Parameter - This is the name of the Parameter. This is the Name displayed in the Object Tree and
also used by UCS's to check or set it's value. It is recommended that you prefix your Parameters
with U_ to help differentiate between System Parameters, of course this is only a recommendation
as you can name them whatever you like.
Value - This is the default Value for the Parameter. You can also define a choice list of Values for
selection here.

       The choice selection is handled through a choice list assigned to a parameter. The format of
       the list is a list designator "", followed by choices separated by the "|" symbol. Each choice
       consists of a prompt and a value separated by the "=" symbol. The first choice in the list is
       considered the default. For example, Opt 2=2|Opt 1=1|Opt 3=3 designates a list of 3 choices
       with option 2 being the default. When displayed, the list will be sorted so the order after the
       first choice is insignificant.
       Choice lists can be added to the System Parameters by typing adding a choice list for the
       value.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Choice lists can be added to the Catalog Parameters by typing adding a choice list for the
value.

       Choice lists are imported/exported in the ORD files.
       [Parameters]
       Attribute="Stock","_CATCH","int",2, " Choice 1=1|Choice 2=2|Choice 3=3"
Choice lists can be added via UCS by typing a choice list for the value.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       ;Add a choice list through a UCS
       For Each LF|RF Part
       If _UCSLST = null Then

               _UCSLST<int> = '<lst>Val 2=2 |Val 1=1|Val 3=3'
               _UCSLST<style> = 1
               _UCSLST<desc> = 'UCS'
       End If
Choice lists can be added manually through the Parameter Editor. The top item in the list will
be the default.

If an Attribute parameter has a choice list, the list will be offered in the sidebar in place of the
standard edit field.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       If an Note parameter has a choice list, the list will be offered in the Note tab in the object
       properties.

       If a System parameter choice list is modified, the list will be updated in Job objects when the
       "Update Job" utility is run.
Type - Allows you to specify the Values type. The choices are Measurement, Degrees, Integer,
Boolean (True/False), Decimal, or Text.
Class - This allows you to specify which Level the Parameter will be placed in. The choices are
Job, Room, Cabinets, Base Cabinet, Wall Cabinet, Tall Cabinet, Vanity, Closets, Closet Standard,
Closet Shelf (Horizontal), or Closet Panel (Vertical).
Style - This option allows you to specify whether the Parameter is defining an Attribute or a Note.
A Parameter defined as a Note will add a Notes tab to the Class level it is defined for. These
Notes can be called up and utilized in CAD Tables and CAD Text Lookups.

        Setup Package
The Setup Package utility is a means to transfer specific objects from one computer running
CABINET VISION to another.

Exporting a Setup Package

The Setup Package feature allows you to create a single file that can store and transfer multiple
custom items for import into another CABINET VISION user's or CABINET VISION Tech's system.
The beauty of the CABINET VISION Setup Package is that any unique identifiers are stored and
recreated on the other user's system. In the simplest terms it is plug and play. A good example of
where this comes in handy is setting up a Blum Metabox drawer system. Prior to the
implementation of the Setup Package Utility you would have to export each UCS and Intelli-Joint
as well as having to recreate each Drawer Guide Material and Drawer Guide Material Schedule.
Then link each of these items together in your UCS. Another method would have been to send a
Technician or CABINET VISION user your database files thus overwriting their databases. With

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
the Setup Package you simply select the UCS and the Setup Package Utility will scan the UCS
and pick out each Intelli-Joint, Material, Finish, Material Schedule, and etc... that is involved in
properly creating the Blum Metabox Drawer System.
The following list of items can be added to a package for transfer:

       Bid Reports - This includes both Custom Reports and Word Forms.
  Catalogs
   Connections
   Construction Methods
   Door Catalogs
   Doors - If you select a Door it will automatically import any items attached to that Door such as;
Profiles, Material Schedules, etc...
   Drawer Boxes - If you select a Drawer Box it will automatically import the Material Schedule
associated with it.
   Drawings - This includes your Title-blocks and Drawing Symbols
   Finish Types
   Finishes
   Intelli-Joints
   Labels (Label-IT Labels or Saw Graphic designs only)
   Machines
   Material Schedules - If you select a Material Schedule it will automatically import all Materials
associated with it.
   Materials - If you select a Material it will automatically import any Finishes and/or Textures
associated with it.
   Parameters
  Parts
   Profiles
   Rate Tables

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
   Reports

    Roll Outs - If you select a Roll Out it will automatically import the Material Schedule associated
with it.

   S2M Reports

    Textures

    Tools - If you select a Tool Set it will automatically import all Tools associated with that Tool
Set.

    Top Construction Methods

    User Created Standards - If you select a UCS it will automatically import any items called
within the UCS such as; Intelli-Joints, Materials, Finishes, Material Schedules, and etc...

           Vendors

This topic explains how to export a package and send it to Tech Support or another CABINET
VISION user.

1. From the System Level go to the Utilities Tab | Setup Package

2. Select the item or items you would like to include in the Package from the list on the left side of
    the screen. After highlighting an item you want to add to the package simply click the "Add
    Items To Package" button in the lower left corner. There is no limit to the number of items that
    can be added to a package.

      You can use Windows      + Click or                                  + Click to select multiple
items in the active Category.

                               © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
3. After selecting the items to add to the package click on the "Save Current Package" tool in the
    toolbar.
              In the graphic below we selected several Material Schedules, notice that it also picked
       up the corresponding Materials, Finishes, Finish Types, and Parts.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
4. The next screen that pops up is the Create License screen and gives you the ability to put
    contact information in the Package for distribution. Make sure to type in a License Description if
    one is not already available and fill out all other details.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
    If the Package includes an Object Catalog the Create License dialog will pop up. Depending
    upon whether it is a Custom or Modular Catalog you will have up to 3 options for the License
    Type.

    1. None - Normal Assembly Catalog

    2. Protected Assembly Catalog - Allows you to create a Protected (Read Only) Catalog. A
        Protected Catalog can not be edited in anyway. You also have the ability to Hide the Cutlist
        as well.

    3. Distributed Assembly Catalog - This function will turn the selected Assembly Catalog into
        a self-contained Catalog that does not require the end user to have the necessary Materials,
        Construction Methods, or other items to make the Catalog work. This is useful if the Catalog
        will be used by outside dealers or others who need access to the Catalog but should not be
        allowed to make changes to it. This function combines all the information needed for the
        Catalog into a single read only format file. This file can then be copied to a DVD, thumb-
        drive, etc... for distribution. There are two main advantages for using this procedure. First,
        the dealer is not able to make permanent changes to the Catalog, thus giving the
        manufacturer complete control over Catalog content. Second, the manufacturer does not
        have to be concerned with distributing and updating all the individual database files
        associated with a CV Catalog. Be aware that a distributable file cannot be updated, but
        must be replaced when a change is made to the Catalog.

5. Select a location to save the Package and type in a Name for the Package then select "Save".

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
6. You may now either close the Setup Package screen or, if you use Microsoft Outlook you can
    click on the "E-Mail Current Package" tool in the top toolbar. This will attach the Package to
    your e-mail and allow you to e-mail to Tech Support or to another CABINET VISION User.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
6. You may now close the Setup Package screen. You have successfully exported a Package
    from CABINET VISION.

                                              © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
             Overwriting Existing Items

               Following are the options that allow you to choose how to Overwrite items that already
               exist in your system.

               All Matches - Overwrite - Will overwrite all existing items in your database with the
               contents of the Package.
               All Matches - Use Existing - Will use all the existing items in your database rather
               than overwrite them with the Package contents.
               Child Matches - Overwrite - Will overwrite all existing children of items in the
               Package that match those in your database.
               Child Matches - Use Existing - Will use all the existing children in your database
               rather than overwrite them with the Package contents.
               Toggle Overwrite - Allows you to Overwrite existing items by selecting them
               individually. This will cause items in the Package to either overwrite the existing item or
               to use the existing item.
6. Click on OK for the Import Complete notice.

7. You may now close the Package screen you have successfully imported a Package into
    CABINET VISION.

       automatically when Core Data is selected.

Overview of Building a Job

Your first Job with CABINET VISION will be a rewarding experience. The amount of time it takes
will quickly decrease as you become more familiar with CABINET VISION and how to navigate
between the various screens and menus used to create your Job. When working with a computer
remember the GIGO acronym, which stands for "garbage in, garbage out". A better way of saying
the same thing is this, "Your end results will reflect the care and attention you paid to the details
while working in CABINET VISION".
This topic covers how to define a Job as to Material and the Construction Methods necessary to
meet the Job's requirements.
The concept of Local Changes and Global Changes as well as Importing and Exporting changes
are concepts that shed additional light on when and why changes may or may not occur.
Prior to starting your Job, it would be beneficial to familiarize yourself with the tools and features
available for use in creating the Job.
Step 1: Plan the Job
Who is the customer?
What kind of Job is it? a kitchen? a laundry area? an entertainment center? furniture? closet?
What are the dimensions of the Room(s)?
What types of Materials will be used? Does the customer want to see several different options?
What type of Construction Method will be used?
What Door Styles will be used? Does the customer want to see several options?
What kind of Hardware will be used? Door/Drawer Pulls? Hinges? Drawer Guides? Wire Baskets?
It may be helpful to design a specification sheet that gets filled out when the customer requests a
quote. This form should contain the information listed above as well as any additional information
that will be helpful in setting up the Job. At this stage, you should probably also draw a sketch of
the Room(s) and include all appropriate dimensions.
Step 2: Start the Job in CABINET VISION
From the opening screen, click on File | New

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The Job Properties window is the first thing that you will see when you begin a new Job. This is
one of the most important steps in creating a Job so be sure to use this window to set all of the
options that you want to use in this Job. If you forget to make a change in one of the Job
Properties tabs, you can make the change later from inside the Job but the changes must then be
made in the Room Properties and will only affect that Room (in other words, there will no longer
be one place to make changes for the entire Job).

                      Do not press enter or click OK when you need to change to additional tabs, or
               different data boxes. Doing so will result in your loosing the Job Properties screen, if
               you wish to navigate through the menu windows without using the mouse, you can:

     to move forward

AND

     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
+                                     to move backwards.

Step 3: Layout the Job in CABINET VISION

When you have finished entering the Job Properties, you will then click OK to move on to the
actual layout of the Job. At this stage, you will need to draw the Walls to match your diagram.

There are different schools of thought as to the best way to recreate the design. One way to draw
the Room would be to simply draw the shape of the Room first with no regard to getting the exact
wall length. Then, you can go back to the Walls and click on them to change the length in the
sidebar. Another way to draw the Walls would be to click at the starting point of the wall and then
move the mouse in the appropriate direction, then, letting go of the mouse, you can type in the

correct length of the Wall and press      to finish the Wall.

                      When drawing Walls, make sure that you draw them in the correct direction. For
               example, if you are drawing a square room with Objects on the inside, draw the Walls
               in a clockwise direction.

Step 4: Placing Objects

Next, you will want to place the Objects in the Room that you have drawn. In your first Job, you
will have a standard Cabinet/Closet Catalog that came with CABINET VISION. The Custom
Cabinets Catalog includes some Base, Vanity, Wall, and Tall Type Cabinets in simple
configurations. The Custom Closet Catalog includes Verticals as well as some common Assembly
configurations. For your first Jobs you will probably pull out Objects that are as similar as possible
to the finished Object that you want, and then make changes until they are correct. You may save
the Objects into your Catalog after making changes to them so that you will have Objects that you
can re-use in the future without making as many changes.

                      It is best to get the overall size of the Object correct before editing the layout of
               the inside of the Object.

To place an Object on the Wall, from the Floor Plan or the Elevation View, click on the Objects
button in the sidebar. Then, you will want to choose the Catalog that the Object will come out of,
most likely the Custom Cabinets or Custom Closets Catalog. Click on the valid Catalog. Next, click
on the Object Category that you want to place (for example, Base Cabinets). Finally, choose the
desired Object out of the list of that Category. In our example, we will choose the Std Base
Cabinet from the Custom Cabinets Catalog in the Base Cabinets Category. To get that Cabinet out
of the Catalog, there are two methods:

1. You can "drag" that Cabinet out of the Catalog by clicking on it and holding the left mouse
    button down as you pull the Cabinet out of the Catalog. When you get the Cabinet out of the
    Catalog and over the Layout area you can release the mouse button and you will see the
    Cabinet outline that resembles an envelope.

   © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
2. You can double click the desired Cabinet and then when you move out over the Layout area
    you will see the Cabinet outline that resembles an envelope.

Room Layout Strategy

Adopt a plan for the order of laying out the Room. Having a plan will help to prevent problems with
Objects that interfere with each other. Below is one possible layout strategy. This is not the only
way or even the best way, it is just an example, you may find that there is a better way for you.

Strategy: Place Objects in the same order as they are actually installed on the job-site.

1. Place corner Cabinets first. In CABINET VISION, corner Cabinets are actually specially shaped
    Cabinets. They sit in the corner by design but they are actually placed on the Wall to the right
    of the corner.

2. Add any Cabinets that have fixed positions. For example, any Cabinets that are centered on a
    window or wall outlet. Don't place the actual window in the drawing yet, use the clearance and
    position numbers to place the Cabinet in the correct location.

3. Add appliances that have fixed positions using the clearance and position numbers as in step
    2.

4. Add Cabinets that relate to appliances such as hoods and refrigerator Cabinets.

5. Add Cabinets that need a certain clearance such as Cabinets that are ___ inches from a
    window, etc.

6. Fill in remaining Cabinets. You may use Autofill to bring in the rest of the Cabinets or place
    Cabinets and stretch them to fill the spaces.

7. Add Counter Tops, Molding, Windows, Doors, and any other decorative items.

Step 5: Reporting

Go to the Report Center by clicking on the Report tab in the screen menu.

Use the Report Center to create cut lists, material lists, and other useful reports that you may
need for the preparation and manufacture of the job.

Step 6: Bidding

Use the Bid Center to create bidding schemes for different types of designs and creating "what if"
scenarios for customers.

Step 7: Printing

Generally, it is best to print from the Drawings area. The advantages of sending views to the

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
drawings page include the ability to scale the picture, add title blocks, add multiple views per
page, and use CAD tools to edit or add details.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
              Fill Mode

This mode of rendering causes the Assemblies to appear solid, with the selected Finish added to
them. They do not display wood grain or other enhancements (Textures) of the advanced rendering
features. This view is useful for viewing Parts and Assemblies when speed is more important than
rendering quality.

                 Texture Mode

This mode of rendering causes the Assemblies to appear solid, with the selected Finish and Textures
applied to them.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

Choosing an Active Window
You will notice that the color band on top of the window is highlighted when it is the active
window. If you wish to work in a window that is not the active window, you must first click in the
window to make it the active window. You will have access to the features normally found in that
window once it is active.
Maximizing a Particular Window

Layers are used to control what appears in the different views in CABINET VISION. Layers are
like transparent overlays on which you organize and group different kinds of drawing information.
The Objects you create have common properties including colors and line-types. An Object can
assume these properties from the Layer Schedule chosen. Using Layer Schedules and the
Objects on Layers makes it easier to manage the information in your drawings.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Layers DO NOT control what is actually in the Job, they ONLY control what you can see on the
screen. For example: If you turn off Counter Tops in your Floor Plan View Layer, the Counter Tops
are still actually there, they simply won't show up in the Floor Plan View of that Layer.
Below, you will see a series of images of the same layout with different options selected in the
Layer Schedule. The images below are all of exactly the same view in the same Job. No Objects
have been removed, only the Layers have been changed.
The first image shows Base Cabinets, Upper Cabinets, Walls, and Dimensions. Also, the Cabinets
are shown in detail (not simply Cabinet outlines).

The next Layer has much of the same information but the Cabinets are shown as outlines only.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The next Layer has the Dimensions removed but has added Labels (Object names) to the
Cabinets.

In the next Layer, we have turned off the Upper Cabinets. The Upper Cabinets are still in the Job
(we have NOT deleted any Cabinets), we have simply turned off the Upper Cabinets so that they
do not appear in the Floor Plan View.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
In the last picture, we have turned off everything except the Walls. Again, the Cabinets are still
there, they simply do not appear in the view because they have been turned off in Layers.
This is the section of CABINET VISION where you can create, edit, copy, rename, and remove

You have four main options you can modify on each Layer:
1. The first option is represented by a light bulb . This determines if the Layer is On or Off (On

    = Visible/Off = Invisible) in the Viewing area of CABINET VISION. If the light is lit ( Yellow)
    then the Layer is On, if the light is not lit ( grey) then the Layer is Off. Simply clicking on the
    Light Bulb will toggle the value.
2. The second option is represented by a pencil . This determines if the Layer is On or Off (On

       = Visible/Off = Invisible) in the Drawing area of CABINET VISION. If the pencil is Yellow
    then the Layer is ON, if the pencil is grey then the Layer is off. Simply clicking on the Pencil
    will toggle the value.
3. The third option is represented by a colored square . This determines the Color of the Layer.
    Simply clicking on the colored square will bring up the Color Selector dialog box, click on the
    new color and it will now be reflected in the Layer.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
4. The forth option is represented by a Line  . This determines the Line-Type for the Layer.

Simply clicking on the Line will bring up the Line Type Selector dialog box, click on the new

Line-Type and it will now be reflected in the Layer.

You can also control the Weight (Width) of the line here. There are sixteen weight options.

Notice in the image below that the Edit button is unavailable. When you select a Layer that can be
edited, the Edit button becomes available.

Dimensions

The physical appearance of Dimensions is controlled in the Dimension Styles Editor. Where and how
the Dimensions appear is controlled here. Following are the main options:
1. Style - This option allows you to select which Dimension Style to use for the Layer Schedule

    you are working with. The Action button will open the Dimension Style Editor allowing you
    to create a new or edit and existing Dimension Style.
2. Horizontal Line Offset - This setting controls how far away from the object being Auto-
    Dimensioned the first Horizontal Dimension line should be located.
3. Horizontal Line Increment - This setting controls how far away any subsequent Horizontal
    Dimension lines should be located away from the preceding Dimension Line.
4. Vertical Line Offset - This setting controls how far away from the object being Auto-
    Dimensioned the first Vertical Dimension line should be located.
5. Vertical Line Increment - This setting controls how far away any subsequent Vertical
    Dimension lines should be located away from the preceding Dimension Line.
6. Tail Dimensions - This option allows you to display your Dimensions with Tails.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

   New Room/Sheet
Use this option to add a new Room to your Job from Plan View, or a New Drawing Sheet to your
Job in the Drawings View.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
  / Lock/Unlock Assembly Numbers

Normal Assembly numbering begins with Assembly #1. Which, is the first Assembly to appear in
the Job. However, if an Assembly is added to the Room and it is added to a Wall with a lower
number, it will renumber the Assemblies within the Job. Typically, Base Assemblies are numbered
before Upper Assemblies. Lower numbers are on the left of a Wall, and the Upper Assemblies
continue the numbering sequence that the last Base Assembly was using. If Wall #1 had 5
Assemblies, then Wall #2 would start with Assembly #6, and running left to right, Base then Upper
Assemblies, assign numbers to those Assemblies. The next Room will start where the previous
Room left off. Deleting or adding Assemblies to an earlier Wall or Room results in renumbering of
all subsequent Assemblies, which can sometimes present problems. The lock Assembly Numbers
feature prevents this potential problem.

CABINET VISION allows locking Assembly numbers that are program generated, or user
selected, as well as assigning and locking a unique number to an Assembly.

Once locked, the numbers on the Assemblies will not change regardless of where other
Assemblies are added or deleted within the Room. If Assembly numbers are locked, and an
Assembly is added to that Room, it will receive the next higher number in sequence, assuming the
number is not used elsewhere, as in another Room. Assemblies with unlocked numbers all start
numbering from the lower left side of Wall #1 in Room #1 and proceed left to right, then left to right
for Upper Assemblies on the same Wall, and then to the next Wall following the same numbering
sequence. If an Assembly is added to the Base Assemblies on Wall #1, Room #1, ALL
Assemblies renumber in all subsequent Rooms. This is prevented if Assembly Numbers are
locked.

To lock a Job access the Utility/Lock Assembly Numbers as shown below. To unlock, access the
same utility, and select the Unlock feature.

                      Remember, this is a Job Level feature, therefore, all Rooms are locked.

Assigning a unique number to specific Assembly

An Assembly can have a unique number assigned to it and locked. The only requirement is that
the number is not previously used in the Job. An Assembly number can only exist one time in any
Job. To lock a number to a specific Assembly, right click on the Assembly, and select the
"Properties" option. The "General" tab allows assigning a number and locking that number by
clicking on the box next to the number. If you wish to assign a unique number, providing it is not
previously used, you can do so by replacing the number in the box with the unique number then
checking the box. To unlock, remove the check mark. The graphic below shows this option.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

          Rotate
To Rotate the view, click and hold the left mouse button in the window. Move the mouse up or
down, or left or right. In this mode the Rotation when moving the mouse left to right the object is
being rotated about the local Y Axis passing through the Object.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
If you press  while dragging left to right the object will rotate about the world Y axis

running vertically down the screen instead of through the object. This allows you to fin tune your

view a bit better giving views that are difficult to do with local Y Axis rotation.

The axis for the up and down movement of the mouse is the Floor (0 Elevation). The axis of the
left to right movement is the center of the Room. If you notice, with the Grid option on in Floor Plan
view, there are 2 darker blue lines. One line that is horizontal and one that is vertical. Where these
lines cross is the center of the Room and the intersection of the 2 lines is the pivot point of the left
to right motion with the mouse.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
If your Room is not Centered you can have CABINET VISION center it automatically by using the
Room | Center Room option.

         Move
Rotating around the axes to get the view you want may move the view all the way or partially off
the screen. The Move View tool on the toolbar can be used to center the view on your screen.
This tool will allow you to maintain the current Room or Assembly orientation but will move the
view to where you want it on the screen. Following the same way to rotate the view, click and drag
the view to where you need to view it.

                Camera Move
The Camera Move option changes Panning to actually 'moving' the Camera rather than normal
Panning. It also changes Scroll Wheel Zooming to 'moving' the Camera in and out, allowing
you, with the combination of Panning and Zooming, to control the Camera's position and
perspective of the View.

Locking Cad Objects

You can use any of the standard CAD Tools available in your Templates. In addition to normal
CAD functionality you also, when in Template Mode, have the option to Lock CAD Objects to your
Paper. As mentioned previously, the primary feature of a Template is to automatically adjust to the
real paper size/orientation.
In order to control this behavior, every Cad Object in a template can be Locked in different ways.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Simply click on the little button associated to a CAD Object property to sequentially change its
locking flags:

  - The position will be kept at the same distance from the left edge of the Paper.
  - The position will be kept at the same distance from the right edge of the Paper.
   - The position will be kept at the same distance from the center (Horizontally) of the Paper.
  - The position will be kept at the same distance from the top edge of the Paper.
  - The position will be kept at the same distance from the bottom edge of the Paper.
  - The position will be kept at the same distance from the center (Vertically) of the Paper.
NONE - The position will adjust proportionally to the Paper Size.

              Every object is auto-locked when editing a Title Block created in a previous version of
       Solid for the first time.
The Auto-Lock Mode is applied to every new Cad Object added to a template, and can be
deactivated/reactivated with the right-click menu.

              The Auto Lock feature chooses the locking edge by dividing the paper size by 3 and
       checking where the Cad Object's position falls.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
               Container

When creating an Assembly Sheet, Part Sheet, and/or a Wall Elevation template, you need to
place an Container object on the Paper to control the image(s) position and appearance during
the printing process.

              Only one Image Container Object can be placed on a Template.
You place an Image Container Object the same way you place a Rectangle or Table Object.
When setting up Assembly Sheet templates, the following window pops-up after you finish placing
a new Image Container Object, and/or selecting Edit from the right-click menu.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The Standard Tab refers to Standard Assemblies, the Shaped Tab to Shaped Assemblies. A
check mark means the selected view is active, a question mark means it's optional, nothing
means it won't be printed.

              Optional means that it will not Print out if Printing it causes another piece of Paper to be
       used.

              Annotated Parts refer to any Part of that Assembly that has had CAD added to it at the
       Part Level.

3D DXF Rules for Import

CABINET VISION imports AutoCAD Release 12 and 13 DXF's. Most other CAD and modeling
programs should work just fine as long as they generate polygon based DXF models. Any non-
polygon information within the file (lines, arcs, text, blocks, etc...) is ignored. While there haven't
been any reported problems so far, AutoCAD R14 does have the option to export Release 12 and
13 DXF's.

Object Types

The main compatibility problem with importing DXF's into CABINET VISION is that the DXF file
specification has several ways to describe polygon-based models.

Polyface Mesh

This object type defines a group of polygons as a single object. This kind of polygon model can
be easily imported to CABINET VISION.

3D Face

This defines each polygon as a separate object. These import into CABINET VISION as well.

3D Mesh

Similar, but internally very different, to Polyface Meshes, this type of polygon object can't be
directly imported into CABINET VISION. Fortunately, most DXF models exported out of other
modeling programs usually produce either Polyface Mesh or 3D Face models. The one huge
exception to this is AutoCAD itself: most of their polygons modeling tools create 3D Mesh objects.
In AutoCAD, it is possible to convert 3D Mesh objects to 3D Face by using the "Explode"
command.

Materials

The other major compatibility issue is how the DXF file specification indicates what materials go
on each object. There are three basic ways: by object, by layer, and by color. Models that can be
imported into Solid must have unique materials distinguished BY LAYER. In the CABINET VISION
import dialog, what you are seeing is not individual objects but a list of all the layers within the
model. Multiple objects that use the same material are on the same layer. The majority of existing
models distinguish materials by layer, but some use the other methods. In fact, it is not uncommon
for models to use combinations. For instance, a model may have multiple objects on a single

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
layer, each with a different color. CABINET VISION would import such a model with all objects
being the same material: the color information is ignored.
The 3DS conversion technique described below can be used to convert these to layer based
models. In step 2, instead of deriving 3DS objects BY LAYER, select BY OBJECT, or BY COLOR,
as appropriate. It may require some trial and error to find what works best. If all else fails,
AutoCAD provides many tools for manually editing objects, colors, and layers.
Solids
Another common way to create models in AutoCAD and other programs is as "solids". While
similar appearing, solid models are very different from polygon models. Solid cannot import
AutoCAD or other types of solids directly. Your program must be able to convert the solid models
into polygon models. In AutoCAD this can be done by using the 3DS conversion technique
described below. The 3DS filter automatically converts solids into polygons.

3DS Conversion Technique:

Load a DXF or DWG model into AutoCAD.
Export the model as a 3D Studio (3ds) model. When AutoCAD prompts for it, check the box to
derive 3DS objects BY LAYER, all other settings default.
Clear out the current model and re-import the 3DS model back into AutoCAD. When prompted,
set "Available Materials" to ADD ALL, "Save to Layer" should be set to BY OBJECT, other settings
should be default. The imported model will imported as a Polyface Mesh.
Now export it as a DXF.

Walls/Room

The below cover manual movement of the S910.
                      Before capturing any measurements in a room without Wall Cladding (Drywall) it

       is important to enter the Wall Cladding thickness so it will be compensated for in the Room
       Layout.

The CV Leica DISTO Utility requires the capture of the Room (or at least the Floor, Ceiling, and 1
Wall) before you can do any other measuring. Follow the button prompts. As prompted, point the
device anywhere on the floor and click the "Measure a floor point" button.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
                      While the Leica Disto Utility is open you can switch Views in CV. This can be very
               handy if you want to see what you are capturing. The 3D View is especially helpful
               when capturing.
Next, point the device anywhere on the ceiling and click the "Measure a ceiling point" button.

Next, point the device anywhere on the first wall and click the "Measure the first wall - Point 1"
button.

                      In case you need to move the device during the capture of measurements or
               possibly Resume your session later knowing exactly where this first point is and being
               able to shoot it accurately is very important. It is recommended to use a piece of tape
               with an 'X' on it or some other accurate point of reference for Wall #1 - Point #1.

                      Walls are being drawn as you measure so just like when drawing Walls manually
               it is best to measure around the Room clock-wise.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Next, click the "Measure Point 2 of Wall 1" button.

At this point you can either stop measuring Walls by clicking the Finish Walls button or you can
click the "Measure next wall - Point 1" button to continue measuring the Room

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
If you choose to continue measuring the Room simply follow the prompts until you have measured
all the Walls in the Room. You can then click the Finish Room button.

Once the Room is Finished you can then start measuring other Objects or simply Free Capture
Points in the Room.

File Property Area

There are ten general options available to configure your output:

File Name - This field will allow you to specify a specific or partial file name. You may choose to
use {JobName} as a variable. Any use of {JobName} will be replaced by the current job.

       Example settings:
               {JobName}.txt  Smith.txt
               MyOutput.csv  MyOutput.csv
               Out-{JobName}.lst  Out-Smith.lst

Header - The header is optional. If specified it will be placed once at the top of the file. It can be
left blank to omit. Any use of \n will be replaced with a carriage return.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Example Setting: ;This is a heading\nThis is the second line\nThis is
       the 3rd line.

               ;This is a heading
               This is the second line
               This is the 3rd line.
Fixed Width - This will determine if each field will use a specific number of characters in the
output. If the actual data has fewer characters then that specified the remaining characters will be
padded with space. If the actual data exceeds the character limit then the value will be truncated.
              String Length includes the Text Qualifier. If the Field Length is set to 4 and the String is
       "ABCDEFG" the output will be "AB". If there is no text qualifier the output would be ABCD.
To set the length of the output field first select the field on the right then enter the Fixed Length at
the bottom of the list.

              If Fixed Width is false then the Text Length indicates the maximum length of any field.
       This by default can be left at zero, but can be set to a number it you wish to limit the output
       length. Unlike Fixed Width, the max length does not include the text qualifier. A max length
       of 4 with the string ABCDEF would result "ABCD"
Delimiter - This is an optional single character to separate each field. It is commonly a comma (,).
Text Qualifier - This is an optional single character that will surround and text or memo output.
Typical values are (") and (`).

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
              When the output type is not fixed width if the text qualifier character is found in a text or
       memo field it will be replaced with either " or ` (whichever is NOT the text qualifier character).
       The example below uses a double quote (") as the text qualifier.

       A "sample" string with "double" and `single' quotes: "A `sample' string with `double' and
       `single' quotes."

Units - The unit can either be metric or imperial. As an option the unit may also be multiplied by a
factor of 10.

Unit Precision - This option specifies the unit precision. Value will be rounded to the nearest
selection. The unit precision applies to measurements as well as singles and doubles.

Boolean Format - This option allow for multiple Boolean formats.

              A string value such as Yes, No, True, False, Y, N, T, F will NOT be surrounded by the
       Text Qualifier.

Date Format - A string value using (M)onth, (D)ay & (Y)ear as variables. Example settings:

M/D/YY                 10/4/10
DD-MM-YYYY             04-10-2010
DDD DD-MM-YYYY         Mon 04-10-2010
DDD, MMM DD/YY         Mon, Oct 04/10
DDDD, MMMM DD of YYYY  Monday, October 04 of 2010

Currency Precision - Similar to unit precision, the value will be rounded to the specified
precision.

       Export ORDX

This option allows you to export the current Assembly list to an ORDX XML file for import into a
3rd party application. See the ORDX Format topic for file format information.

ORDX Format

In general the ORDX format follows the formatting of Properties throughout a Job. Unlike an ORD
file which is restricted to one Room the ORDX can have multiple Rooms. The ORDX can also
define both Face and Interior Sectioning per Assembly which also can not be achieved via the
ORD file.
We have included a sample ORDX file, which touches most areas of a Job, in the install. It is
located in the \Support\Sample ORDX\ Folder.
As the format matures we'll be adding more documentation to this topic.

Working with Parts

There is a PartOverrides section in the ORDX. It uses the part path from the Object Tree to
identify the part e.g. Cab.interior.AS@2. The standard 9 parameters are written out as well as
other modified parameters which will be in a Parameter section.

       <PartOverrides>
             <PartOverride>
                  <Name>Cab.Case.LF</Name>
                  <DZ>50</DZ>
             </PartOverride>
             <PartOverride>
                  <Name>Cab.Case.TO</Name>
                  <Y>760</Y>
                  <DZ>20</DZ>

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
                  <AX>-65</AX>
                  <Parameter>

                       <Name>GOAT</Name>
                       <Type>M</Type>
                       <Value>0.925</Value>
                  </Parameter>
             </PartOverride>
             <PartOverride>
                  <Name>Cab.Interior.AS@2</Name>
                  <DZ>35</DZ>
             </PartOverride>
       </PartOverrides>
There is also a Shape item in the PartOverrides section. In addition we also added Shape to the
AdditionalParts section for shapes on manually added parts
       <PartOverrides>
             <PartOverride>
                  <Name>Cab.Interior.AS@2</Name>
                  <Shape>
                       <Axis>XY</Axis>
                       <Template>

                             ***
                       </Template>
                  </Shape>
             </PartOverride>

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       </PartOverrides>
The xml describes the shape as a series of entities (either lines or arcs). For a line you will have:

<Begin>

       <x></x>

       <y></y>

</Begin>

<End>

       <x></x>

       <y></y>

</End>

Everything is assumed to be Zero. So, if we were describing a line that started at (0,0) and went to
(2,0) the only information that would be needed is:

       <entity id="1" type="line2d">

       <End>

                 <x>2</x>

       </End>

       <entity>

Here would be a simple triangle going from (0,0), (2,0), (1,1)

       <Shape>

       <Axis>XY</Axis> XY is the default. Other options would be XZ

or YZ

                 <template firstid="1" unit="mm">

                 <entity id="1" type="line2d">

                           © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
                                           <End>
                                                  <x>2</x>

                                           </End>
                                    </entity>
                                    <entity id="2" type="line2d">

                                           <Begin>
                                                  <x>2</x>

                                           </ Begin >
                                           <End>

                                                  <x>1</x>
                                                  <y>1</y>
                                           </End>
                                    </entity>
                                    <entity id="2" type="line2d">
                                           < Begin >
                                                  <x>1</x>
                                                  <y>1</y>
                                           </ Begin >
                                    </entity>
                           </template>
         </Shape>
Note: There are also Arc entities. It is probably best to output some cabinets / parts with various
shapes to get a handle on the output.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Also any entity can have parameters. The format for an entity with parameters is:
         <entity id="2" type="line2d">
                <Begin>
                       <x>2</x>
                </ Begin >
                <End>
                       <x>1</x>
                       <y>1</y>
                </End>
                <parameters>
                       <parameter name="ABC">
                              <value type="4">1</value>
                       </parameter>
                       <parameter name="Test">
                              <value type="4">1</value>
                       </parameter>
                </parameters>
         </entity>

ORD File Format

Order Entry (ORD) Version 4 File Format

Standard, Extended, and Jobsite Companion

The Order Entry (ORD) file format is an ASCII format used for transferring CABINET VISION
Cabinet data in a version and configuration independent form. The ORD file may contain Cabinets
from multiple Catalogs with multiple door styles and options.

The ORD file has a hierarchical structure consisting of a [Header] section followed by [Catalog]
and [Cabinet] section pairs. The [Header] section is used to set the CABINET VISION Job defaults
while the [Catalog] and corresponding [Cabinet] section are used to set the Door Styles and options
for a list of Cabinets. Multiple Catalogs, Door Styles and options are specified by including multiple
[Catalog] and [Cabinet] section pairs in the ORD file.

For example, if all the Cabinets in a CABINET VISION Job had the same Catalog and options, the
ORD file would only have one [Catalog] section followed by one [Cabinet] section. If there were
some Cabinets from a different Catalog, there would be secondary [Catalog] and [Cabinet]
sections. This scheme may be repeated as many times as necessary to list all the Cabinets in a
CABINET VISION Job with differing Catalogs, door styles and options.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
              Certain characters in Comment fields can cause problems and should be avoided. This
       includes but is not limited to the following: # ? = | ;

              Items in red represent the Extended ORD File Format

An Extended Format allows for the creation of Walls, Floors and the placing of Moldings and
Cabinets on the Walls. The created objects are visible in the Job as if they had been placed in
Layout whereas in the Standard ORD format, the Cabinets are added to an Order Entry List and
are not visible in the Layout views. The Walls section should precede the Moldings and Cabinets
sections as the items in these sections are attached to a Wall which needs to be defined first.

[Header]
Version=4
...
[Link]
...
[Walls]
...
[Windows]
...
[Doors]
...
[Appliances]
...
[Floors]
...
[Moldings]
...
[Lights]
...
[Catalog]
Name="Catalog 1"
...
[Cabinets]
1,...
3,...
...
[Catalog]
Name="Catalog 2"
...
[Cabinets]
2,...
...

The order of the entries in the [Header] and [Catalog] sections is not important. All string values
should be enclosed by quotes (" "). Numbers representing dimensions should be entered matching

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
the Unit value specified in the [Header] area.

CABINET VISION Layout screen. They are mostly optional but can be used to set up the defaults
for the CABINET VISION Job into which the ORD file is imported. The Materials, Door Styles and
Construction set here do not affect any of the Cabinets listed in the ORD file as they take all their
configurations from their corresponding [Catalog] sections. The [Header] section should at least
contain the Version number for future compatibility.

Walls Section (Extended Format)

The entries in this section are used to define Walls. The parameters reflect the Wall's location and
direction as well as its Length, Height and Thickness. If the start or end point of a Wall is the same
as an existing Wall, the Walls will be joined at that point.
If this section is present, all Cabinets will be added to a Wall instead of being added to the Order

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Entry list and will thus be visible in the Layout view (Floor Plan, Elevation and Perspective). The
optional positional parameters for the Cabinets should be filled out to place the Cabinets correctly
on the Wall.

To maintain a consistent Wall numbering sequence, the Walls should be defined in a clockwise
direction. This will ensure that the Walls are numbered in the order in which they are defined.

The Wall definitions should consist of 14 comma separated fields.

[Walls]

Po                Value
siti Type
on                Wall X Position
                  Wall Z Position
1        Float    Wall Direction
                  Wall Length
2        Float    Wall Height
                  Wall Thickness
3        Float    Wall Number (1 based) Empty = Line Count
                  Wall Type
4        Float    Left Wall Number (0 or Empty => No Wall Attached)
                  Wall Radius
5        Float    Rotation of the Radius Wall (0 = CW, 1 = CCW)
                  Arc Angle for the Radius Wall
6        Float    Wall ID
                  Modify Code
7        Integer

8        Integer

9        String

10 Float

11 Integer

12 Float

13 Integer

14 String

The "Wall Type" field must be represented by one of the following values.
1 = Exterior Wall
2 = Interior Wall ('T' Wall or extra Wall)
3 = Peninsula or Island Wall
4 = Radius Wall
The format for the "Left Wall Number" field is #-x where x:
can be empty, or E to indicate the Wall is continued from Wall #, e,g., 3 or 3-E
F to indicate the Wall is attached to the front of the Wall #, e.g., 3-F
B to indicate the Wall is attached to the back of the Wall #, e.g., 3-B

Moldings Section (Extended Format)

The entries in this section are used to define moldings attached to a wall. The Molding type may
be one of the following predefined types, "Crown", "LightRail", "Scribe", "BaseBoard", "ChairRail"
or "Casing". The moldings can be created in the XZ (as done in the Plan view in Solid) or XY (as
done in the Wall elevation view in Solid). There needs to be a minimum of two coordinate pairs to
define a molding shape.

The Molding definitions should consist of 8 comma separated fields followed by a comma
separated list of additional coordinate pairs as follows:

[Moldings]

1  Integer  Wall molding should be applied to
            Molding Type
2  String   Molding Axis
            Molding Elevation/Outset
3  String   1st X position
            1st Y/Z position
4  Float    2nd X position
            2nd Y/Z position
5  Float

6  Float

7  Float

8  Float

Optional fields for additional coordinate pairs.

The Molding axis can be either "XZ" to specify Molding laid out in Plan view or "XY" to specify
Molding applied to the face of a Wall.

            © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
If the axis is specified as "XZ", the 4th field specifies the Elevation of the Molding. If the axis is
specified as "XY", the 4th field specifies the offset of the Molding from the Wall Face.

Catalog Section

The entries in this section reflect the Door and Option Property Pages for the Catalogs and
Cabinets in Solid. They are used to define the Catalog, Door Styles and options for the following
[Cabinet] section. This section should always contain the Catalog Name, Base and Wall Door
Styles and a list of the options to apply to the Cabinets in the following [Cabinets] section. The
Cabinets listed in the following [Cabinets] section will be extracted from the specified Catalog by
their nomenclature and have the listed Door Styles and Options applied to them. If the Catalog,
Door Style or any of the options are different for a Cabinet then a new [Catalog] section should be
created for the Cabinet and the Cabinet should be placed in a following [Cabinets] section.

Parameters Section

The Parameters section reflects cabinet "Note" and "Attribute" parameters. The parameters will
only be applied to the cabinet specified by the following cabinet record. Once a cabinet has been
processed the Parameters list will be cleared. The Parameters section may be inserted in a list of
cabinets. For example, to insert parameters on cabinet 2 in the following list...

       [Cabinets]
       1,"2 Door",30.00000,34.50000,24.00000,"P","R",1,""
       2,"2 Door",30.00000,34.50000,24.00000,"P","R",1,""
       3,"2 Door",30.00000,34.50000,24.00000,"P","R",1,""

The list becomes...

       [Cabinets]
       1,"2 Door",30.00000,34.50000,24.00000,"P","R",1,""
       [Parameters]
       Attribute="My Dimension","MYDIM","meas",26.75
       [Cabinets]
       2,"2 Door",30.00000,34.50000,24.00000,"P","R",1,""
       3,"2 Door",30.00000,34.50000,24.00000,"P","R",1,""

Parameters are defined in the format "Type=Description,Name,ValueType,Value"

Type         Attribute or Note (String)
Description  Parameter Description (String)
Parameter    Parameter Name (String)

Value Type   Valid Value Types                   Value Type Description
             meas                                Measurement
             deg                                 Degrees
             int                                 Integer
             bool                                Boolean

             © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
                     dec                             Decimal

                     text                            Text

Value                Parameter Value (String/Number)

You can also define Choice Lists. See the Parameters topic for more information.

Cabinets Section

The entries in this section list the Cabinets along with their sizes, hinging and end type
information. The Cabinet will be pulled from the Catalog defined in the preceding [Catalog] section
by matching it's nomenclature with a Cabinet in the Catalog. The Door Styles and options defined
in the preceding [Catalog] section will be applied to the Cabinet.

The Cabinet definitions should consist of 9 comma separated fields defined as follows (If the
Extended ORD Format file is being used and contains a Walls section then the Cabinet definitions
should contain an additional 9 positional fields as well):

[Cabinets]

Position    Type     Value

4           Float    Cabinet Height

7           String   Cabinet End Types

9           String   Cabinet Comment

12          Float    Distance from Floor
13          Float    Outset from Wall
14          Integer  Cabinet Type

The Order Entry Number is the Cabinet number as reflected in the "Order Entry" screen in Solid.

The Cabinet Nomenclature should reflect the nomenclature of a Cabinet available in the Catalog
defined in the preceding [Catalog] section.

Extended Format Sample

The following sample is an example of the extended ORD format that provides for the creation of
Walls, Floors and adding Cabinets to the Walls. The Cabinets are visible in layout as they are
added to the Walls and not to the order entry list which is the case in the standard ORD format.

The Header section reflects the current Job Door Style, Materials and Construction as well as the
Wall and Floor Textures. There is also a setting to set the initial Camera position for the 3D
perspective view. The [Walls] section creates three connected Walls while the [Floors] section
creates two floor shapes. The [Moldings] section creates some Crown Molding in plan view at an
elevation of 92 inches. It also creates some Chair Rail along the Wall in plan view followed by
some Chair Rail on the Wall face in elevation view. The [Lights] section sets up three lights, one of
each type allowed in Solid (it is good practice to always include an Ambient light). The [Catalog]
section describes the Catalog Name, Door Styles and Options for the two Cabinets pulled from
"Generic". The two Cabinets are listed in the corresponding [Cabinets] section.

Custom Order Import

When opening a .TXT or .CSV file you will be presented with the custom Data Field Configuration
Utility. This utility examines the text file that you are importing and helps you ensure that the data
is imported in the way that you want. You can use this Utility to define what each field in your Text
file represents so it is imported properly.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Toolbar

There are four options in the toolbar:

    Save
       Allows you to save the current configuration for re-use.
                                     Select Configuration
       Allows you to select which of your predefined configurations to use on the current Text file.

     Rename
       Allows you to rename the currently selected Configuration.

    Delete
       Allows you to delete the currently selected Configuration.

General Options

There are five general options available to configure your Text file:

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Fields - This option allows you to establish how the fields in the Text file are defined. If items in
the text file are separated by tabs, colons, semicolons, spaces, or other characters, select
Delimited; then select what the delimiter is (Tab, Comma, Semicolon, Space, Other). If all of the
items in each column are the same length, select Fixed width.
Catalog - Select the CABINET VISION Catalog to utilize.
Text Qualifier - Select the character that encloses values in your text file. When Solid encounters
the text qualifier character, all of the text that follows that character and precedes the next
occurrence of that character is imported as one value, even if the text contains a delimiter
character. For example, if the delimiter is a comma (,) and the text qualifier is a quotation mark ("),
"Tuscaloosa, Alabama" is imported into one field as Tuscaloosa, Alabama.
Dimensions - Select whether the file you are importing is Inches or Metric.
Start Import at Line - Type or select a line number to specify the first line of the data that you
want to import.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Import Preview Area

In this are you will see all of the columns that CABINET VISION has created for your Text file
based on the translation of the Text file. Click the column header of the column(s) that you do not
want Ignored and set its type. There are thirteen options:

Ignore - Will ignore this column when importing.
Catalog - The Catalog to pull the Object from. The name specified in the Text file must exactly

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
match the Catalog name in Cabinet Vision.

Comment - The Objects Comment.

Depth - The Objects Width.

Description - The Objects Description.

Height - The Objects Height.

Hinge - The Objects Hinge orientation.

       * = Undefined
       P = Cabinet has a pair of doors (Ignored*)
       L = Cabinet is left hinged (If assembly is saved with a single door L vs R will control hinge
       direction)
       R = Cabinet is right hinged (If assembly is saved with a single door L vs R will control hinge
       direction)
       T = Cabinet is top hinged (Ignored*)
       B = Cabinet is bottom hinged (Ignored*)
       Ignored* - Changing this value will not change the hinge type on the saved catalog object.

ID - The Objects line item number.

Finish - The Objects End Type.

       * = Undefined

Drawing Walls

Click your mouse at the point you desire the Wall to begin. Note that creating the Walls in a clock
wise direction around the perimeter of the Room will cause the dimension lines to appear on the
outside of the Walls. This would be the normal procedure for placing Assemblies on the inside of
the Room. After clicking the origin point for the Wall, release the left mouse button and pull the
Wall in the direction you want it to run.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Note the information in the sidebar will change to reflect the Length and angle as the Wall
changes. You are free to enter the value for the Wall length at any time by typing in a value. To do
this, simply type the value, you do not need to click anywhere or perform any other action prior to
entering the value, assuming that the data box for the Wall length is filled with a background color.

If you desire to enter values for the other data boxes, use  to move down, or

+  to navigate upward.

If you are creating the Wall with the mouse only using Chained Line, which is the default, to
complete the Wall, left click at the location for the end of the Wall, if you wish to stop drawing
Walls simply right click the mouse and select the Select option to complete. To create subsequent
Walls, simply drag the mouse to the end point of your next Wall.

Final adjustment to Wall dimensions can be made by left clicking on the Wall, and entering data in
the sidebar as described above.

Right click on a Wall for options regarding "Connect Left" or "Connect Right". These options will
cause the Walls to connect if they are close enough to one another and not connected to another
Wall at the same end. See the Right Click a Wall in Plan View topic for more information.

   © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Connecting A Wall to the Face of Another

When Drawing a Wall if you click on the Face of another Wall as the Start point the new Wall will
be connected to the face of that Wall and then allow you to slide the start point along the Wall.
When you are happy with the start point simply click then drag the Wall to Length.
If you click on the Face connected Wall you will be able to set the Walls position accurately along
the Wall using the Clearance options in the sidebar.

the Left window. Or you can, while dragging the Wall, press the function key F3 on the keyboard to
bring up the Angle Calculator. You can use the Angle Calculator to calculate inside angles only,
using the 3/4/5 method.

Creating Vaulted, Cathedral, or Peninsula Walls

Either before starting to draw your Wall or by selecting the Wall once drawn you can control the
Wall's Style by selecting an option from the Style option in the sidebar.

The Wall Style option provides for Standard (rectangular) Walls, Peninsula Walls, Cathedral Walls
(which slope to a high point mid length), and Vaulted Wall (right or left slope to high point). Below
is a graphic that explains the Cathedral and Vaulted options.
Note that all changes made in this window are for this wall only. If you desire to change more
than one Wall, you must select each Wall that is to be changed. Regardless of any choice you
make here, these changes will not be set as system default (except Hatch Type or Back Type),
and therefore, will have no effect on future Walls. Remember, the Soffit is not a physical object,
but represents the distance you desire to hold your Wall and Tall Cabinets down from the physical
ceiling.
Notice how the Cathedral Height and the Vaulted Height are represented by CABINET VISION.
The Wall height is set at 96 inches in this example, and the actual height is greater due to the

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
ceiling condition. The angle of the vault of Cathedral is related to the width of the Wall. The height
remains constant as the angle flattens with wider Walls. This angle is adjustable for Vaulted Walls.

Cathedral Walls are adjustable as well, and the vault location for the Cathedral may also be
adjusted.

Objects -

Remember that a Wall is required before Objects can be placed.
The Custom Cabinets Library will display 4 icons representing 4 Assembly classes, Base, Wall,
Tall and Vanity. Select the class icon representing the Assembly class you wish to place, and click
on it. The Class will open presenting the members of that Class, as shown in the right hand
graphic. Here the Standard Base Cabinet is highlighted. To place this Cabinet on a Wall click on
the icon representing the Cabinet, and drag the icon from the sidebar into the Room. Either Plan
View or Elevation View allow placement of Objects.

As you drag the icon beyond the right margin of the sidebar your cursor will change to a figure
resembling a Cabinet. As soon as your cursor crosses into the Room, release the mouse button
and your cursor will again change, this time to a dashed rectangular outline representing the
Object you are placing. Move your cursor to the area you would like the Object to occupy. To place
the Object, left click and the Object will snap to the Wall closest to your release point. If placing
multiple Objects, it is a good idea to overlap the new Object on its neighbor as Solid will
compensate for the Object dimensions and move your new Object so that it touches the Object it

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
overlapped, just as if you were installing the Objects side by side. This method prevents the
possibility of an error caused when placing Objects and trying to move one to the side of another,
as you may be off by 1/8 or 1/4 inch, and at the scale you are working with, this small dimension
may not be noticed.
Once placed, an Object may be moved in several ways. The favored way is to click on the Object,
and it will change to an outline with yellow and green dots. Grab the center yellow dot and drag
the Objects to it's new location. The center yellow dot is favored because it will not allow you to
place an Objects within a Wall, or another Object.

The dark green dot, on the other-hand, works the same as the center yellow dot, except it allows
placement of the Object anywhere you wish, within a Wall, overlapping another Cabinet, in the
middle of the Room, etc.

              Additionally, the same function of being able to place an Object where it otherwise
       would not go can be accomplished by dragging the Object from the library, and holding

                     when you click to place the Object. This is a method of placing an Object in the
       middle of a Room, as you might do for an island.
There is also a light green dot visible on the Object when you have clicked on it. This light green
dot allows for rotation of an Object. Typically, the Object follows the Wall, however, when the need
arises to have the Object rotated to a different orientation than the Walls, the green dot will allow
you to do so.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The Yellow dots that appear in the middle of the dashed lines allow for sizing an Object. Click the
dot, and drag the dot to a position representing the value you desire to obtain, and the Object will
stretch or shrink accordingly.

The below graphic shows an Objects that has been clicked on and is displaying the various
colored dots. If you look to the sidebar, in the lower half you will see data boxes representing the
dimensions, elevation, outset, and rotation of the Object. Instead of dragging a dot, the desired
dimension can be written to the data box and the Object will respond accordingly.

      These data boxes have a unique value in that you can add or subtract to the value
within them by clicking to the right of the last digit, and typing either the plus "+" or the minus
"-" sign, and then the value that you wish to add or subtract. Once you have entered the

value, and press  , the data box functions like a calculator, computing the new

value, and thereafter, modifying the Object to the new value.

Object positioning can be as precise as you need it to be. Any Object will display the information
shown in the below graphic when activated. This information represents the Objects position on
the Wall relative to other Objects on the Wall, as well as the Wall itself. Study the graphic and the
number superimposed to represent the values or call of the dimension. Centering the Object can
be as simple as entering one half the length of a Wall in the appropriate box, or how accurately
you can position the Object for other requirements using these values.

                  © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The grey square in the right corner is added to the graphic to represent an area that exists when
two Walls join. This area represents the depth of the Object type as set in Layout Properties and the
overlapping of the Objects as they reach the end of their Wall. Because of this condition you will
see that the clearance and the position differ in example 2 and 4 above. This represents the
difference between Clearance and End Position. Note that the difference is 24 inches (90 - 66 =
24), which happens to be the depth of the Objects on that Wall if it exists. If the above example
had an Upper Cabinet instead of a Base Cabinet, the area would be in the neighborhood of 12 x
12 or whatever value you set for the depth of your Uppers.

It is a good idea to keep a close eye on the clearance and position of the Objects you place as a
means of insuring that the Objects you are placing represent the sizes of the Objects your Job
requires. Also, adding clearances to items like Dishwashers or other appliances that require less
than 1 inch clearance is much easier when the appliance is dropped on its neighbor, (zero
clearance) and the clearance is added to the appropriate data box (right or left clearance). This
insures accurate and reliable dimensioning throughout the Job. Another tip that helps insure
accuracy is to spend a moment looking at the data in these boxes after placing, editing, or moving
an Object. Angle, Outset (distance from Wall) and Elevation (distance above floor) are provided in
the lower data boxes above. These data boxes only appear when an Object is activated.

Tops -

After selecting this feature, you will see your Room, with an outline around your Assemblies that
are Classified as Base or Vanity and a red dashed outline that appears to be a Counter Top on
one of the Walls. This red outline represents the Wall that is active. The active Wall is the Wall
that the Counter Top is attached to in the hierarchy of CABINET VISION. If you draw a Counter
Top with an active Wall other than the Wall the Counter Top is on, and later delete the Wall that
was active, you will loose that Counter Top even though it appeared to be attached to a Wall that
still exists. Always give thought to which Wall should be the active Wall when creating your
Counter Tops.

              Selecting the correct active Wall (the red outline) is VERY important. If you have a
       different Wall activated than the one you are drawing your Counter Top on you will not see
       your Counter Top in the proper Elevation view. Another VERY important point to note is
       when using the Bid Center and using the Bid Method Per Lineal Foot of Counter Top or Per Lineal
       Meter of Counter Top the calculation is based on the active Wall. Not having the correct active
       Wall selected can cause ERRORS IN YOUR BID.
To change the active Wall, simply click in front of the Wall that you would like to be active. This
works equally well on Wall faces and Wall backs.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Creating Counter Tops for your Job requires choosing whether you would like to use the AutoBuild
Tops sidebar button or build the Counter Tops using the New Top sidebar button. Simple plans,
are easily accomplished using the AutoBuild feature. Click the AutoBuild button, then choose
whether you wish the Counter Tops built for the entire Room, or just a single Wall. If you choose
the single Wall option, be sure that you have selected the correct Wall as the active Wall.
If you choose to use the New Top method, you will see the same outline with a reference to the
active Wall as shown above, however, you will be required to use the Counter Top Shape Editor that
will appear in the sidebar.
It is possible to use both methods in a Job, however, if you choose to do so, you must build using
the AutoBuild feature before building any Counter Tops by the New Top feature.

              The AutoBuild feature will delete any existing Counter Tops in the current Room.
The following graphic is an example of Counter Tops that would require being built using the New
Top feature. Note the unique shapes involved, and the different Elevations.

These Counter Tops were created, one at a time, using the New Top sidebar option. The image

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
below shows the lower Counter Top with the edge attributes defined below.
