Auto Fill -

The following options appear in the sidebar after the Auto Fill button is selected.

There are three sections in the Auto Fill sidebar:

Fill Options
      Mode - There are three Fill Mode options:

     Space - Will fill between two Objects, as is the case when there is less than a full Wall to fill.
       Space can also be used to fill a Wall.

     Wall - Will fill the entire Wall with Base or Wall (or both) Cabinets.
     Room - Will fill all Walls within the Room.
Source - There are two Fill Source options:
     Catalog - Pulls Objects from the selected Catalog. Will only use Objects specified as Auto

       Fill in Advanced Object Save Properties.
     Custom - Uses Standard non-Catalog Base and Upper objects to fill the Room.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Catalog - Select the Catalog to Auto Fill with from the drop down list.
       Ask Corner Type - This option is only enabled if you are using the Custom Source. This
       enables the Corner Options prompt covered later in this topic.

Cabinets

       Modular Increments will cause Objects to seek the same size while holding the differences
       to the increment shown. This might result in an Object that defaults to 30 inches wide (as
       saved to your Catalog) and increments to 27 or 33 inches when placed. All Objects will be
       equal width on the same Elevation.
       Shrink becomes an option if you choose a modular Catalog for your fill style. Choosing Yes
       allows those modular Cabinets to be re-sized to fill the space.
       Base Corners - Allows you to choose the corner Cabinet type for Auto Fill.
       Upper Corners - Allows you to choose the corner cabinet type for Auto Fill.

Room

       Molding and Counter Tops become active options if you choose Room as the Fill Mode.
       Selecting Yes will cause CABINET VISION to include Counter Tops and Molding to the
       automatic Room.
Using Auto Fill
The Auto Fill feature provides a quick way to place multiple Cabinets on a Wall or Walls within a
Room. This is most useful when you have long Elevations with many similar Cabinets. CABINET
VISION does not treat Cabinets placed by the Auto Fill feature any differently than Cabinets
placed individually, they are edited, stretched, etc. in the same manner as manually placed
Objects.
The area shown below is available in the Layout level, by clicking File | Preferences | Layout Tab. You
will notice the Clearance area below, these clearances will be followed by the Auto Fill feature,
when used. The more important ones are the Floor to Upper clearances as well as the Refer Side
Clearance. If the Refrigerator is placed prior to the Auto Fill feature being used, the clearances will
be followed.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
To use the Auto Fill feature you must first select a Cabinet as the default Base and Wall Cabinet.
You are free to do this in each library, but, without so selecting, the Cabinet will not Auto Fill.
Typically, a standard Base and standard Wall Cabinet are selected. Right Click one of these
Cabinets from the Objects sidebar and select Edit Item.
The following "Save Object" window will appear. Click the "Advanced" button on this window.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The following "Save Object Advanced Properties" window will appear.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
In the bottom right corner of this window is a small box with the word "Auto-fill" beside it. If you
want this Cabinet to be your default Auto Fill Cabinet, place a check mark here. Be sure you have
not made any other changes to the menu and click OK. Click OK on the window behind the above
window to return to the Room Level of CABINET VISION. Do the same with your Wall Cabinet. If
you have more than one Catalog, you may select Cabinets in each Catalog to Auto Fill with, and,
when using the feature, select the Catalog of your choice.

Grain Match -

There are some Job Properties to set Automatic Grain Matching we should look at first. These
options control how Assemblies are Automatically Grain Matched by CABINET VISION. There are
three options:
If you do not select the Grain Match option on the Doors Tab for the Job/Room then CABINET
VISION will not Grain Match any Assemblies at all. This will allow you full Manual control over
which items are Grain Matched and how.
No Grain Match

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

CAD Layers are used in CAD and within Drawings Scenes when you edit a Drawing Scene in
CAD mode. This list may be different depending on what objects are in the active Scene.
The following are the possible default Layers when bringing a Scene into CAD.

       Walls - The Walls CAD Layer contains all of the Walls in the selected Scene.
       Dimensions - The Dimensions CAD Layer contains all of the Dimensions in the selected
       Scene.
       Annotations - The Annotations CAD Layer contains all of the Annotations in the selected
       Scene.
When using CAD in "non-Scene" areas you can create your own Custom Layers by clicking New...

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
in the Layer Selector. Whichever Layer is selected in the drop down menu is the current Layer and
any CAD entities drawn will be on that Layer.

Hiding the CAD Layers

Each of these Layers can be set to hidden by toggling the Light Bulb to grey. When a Layer is
hidden; the elements particular to that Layer will not be visible until that Layer is toggled back to
visible. In addition, if you add additional CAD details such as dimensions, lines, etc. to a scene
then set that Layer to invisible; all of the added CAD details will be hidden as well.
This can be highly useful when you have a great deal of detail in one area. This can help prevent
accidentally editing/deleting the wrong CAD Object as well as making the view clearer for you to
work in it. All Drawings sent to the Drawings page as a scene will have a set of Default Layers,
which Layers are contained in the Scene is dependent upon the source View of the Scene and/or
what is actually contained in the Scene.

Locking the CAD Layers

Each of the CAD Layers include a Lock/Unlock icon. If you click on the Lock icon while it is in the
Unlocked position - it will change to Locked and the reverse steps will unlock it. While a CAD
Layer is Locked - items in that scene (particular to that Layer) cannot be deleted or modified. Also,
items added to that scene (such as Lines, Dimensions, etc) cannot be deleted either. The Lock
feature enables you to protect those portions of the scene which you don't want to change.
You can also add your own CAD Layer(s) when you click on the drop down arrow and click on
New. This new CAD Layer will of course be blank until you add new CAD elements or symbols to
it.

Editing Tables

To edit the look and feel of your table simply click anywhere in the Table using the CAD Select
          Tool. With the Table active you will see the available Editing options in the CAD sidebar.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
© 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
    To edit the Groups or line items in an existing table simply Right Click Edit the Table or

    Double Click on it with the CAD Select    Tool.

There are 40 possible Table Editing options:

 Color - Allows you to change the color of the lines making up the Table.

 Layer - Allows you to change the CAD Layer the Table is on.

 Line Type - Allows you to change the Line Type of the Lines making up the Table.

 Line Width - Allows you to change the Line Width of the Lines making up the Table.

 Dash Scale - The scale for dashed lines.

 Left - Allows you to change the Left position of the Table. Referenced from Grid Center.

 Right - Allows you to change the Right position of the Table. Referenced from Grid Center.

 Top - Allows you to change the Top position of the Table. Referenced from Grid Center.

 Bottom - Allows you to change the Bottom position of the Table. Referenced from Grid Center.

 Center X - Allows you to change the Center X position of the Table. Referenced from Grid
   Center.

 Center Y - Allows you to change the Center Y position of the Table. Referenced from Grid
   Center.

 Width - Allows you to change the Width of the Table.

 Height - Allows you to change the Height of the Table.

 Frame - Allows you to turn the Frame of the Table On or Off.

On

    © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Off

 Grid - Allows you to turn the Grid of the Table On or Off.
On

Off

 Allow Duplicates - Set to Yes will consolidate like Parts on a single line item with the total
   Quantity reflected.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
There are three main areas of each table.
Group

 Group Font - Allows you to select the Font for the Group area of the Table.
 Group Bold - Allows you to select the Font weight for the text in the Group area of the Table.
 Group Height - Allows you to change the Font Height for the Group area of the Table.
 Group HAlign - Allows you to select the Horizontal Alignment of the Text in the group area of

   the Table.
 Group Padding - Allows you to set the Spacing between one Group and the next, when the

   Table consists of multiple Groups.
 Group Show Text - Allows you to display or to suppress the display of the Group Title.
 Group Show Empty - Allows you to display or to suppress the display of a Group if it contains

   no data.
Header

 Header Font - Allows you to select the Font for the Header area of the Table.
 Header Bold - Allows you to select the Font weight for the text in the Header area of the Table.
 Header Height - Allows you to change the Font Height for the Header area of the Table.
 Header HAlign - Allows you to select the Horizontal Alignment of the Text in the Header area of

   the Table.
 Header Padding - Allows you to set the Header Spacing.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 Header Show Text - Allows you to display or to suppress the display of the Header Title.
 Header Show Empty - Allows you to display or to suppress the display of a Header if it

   contains no data.
Data

 Data Font - Allows you to select the Font for the Data area of the Table.
 Data Height - Allows you to change the Font Height for the Data area of the Table.
Selected
Group Selected

     Caption - Allows you to Name/Rename the Headers Caption.
       Header Selected

     Caption - Allows you to rename the Column Header Caption.
     Width - Allows you to set the Column Width.
     Sort - Allows you to set the Sorting of the Column.

       Data Selected
     Width - Allows you to set the Data Column Width.
     Sort - Allows you to set the Sorting of the Data.
     Bold - Allows you to select the Font weight for the Data.
     HAlign - Allows you to select how the Data Column is aligned horizontally.
     Negative Numbers - Allows you to select how Negative Numbers are displayed.
Whenever you add text through CAD to any area of CABINET VISION, you not only have the
ability to type your desired Text but also have the ability of selecting from Text Variables of
information already within your Job. The auto text appears inside the brackets { } and is

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
sometimes accompanied by additional static text. The text outside of the brackets may be deleted
leaving only that which is inside the brackets to be automatically filled in. Automatic text is not
limited to but is especially useful in Title Blocks.
Clicking the Action button will bring up the list of available Text Variables. The list of Text
Variables will be different depending on what Level of CABINET VISION you are in.

Below is a list of the Text Variables and where the values in the variables are being pulled from.
              The list below represents the text variables listed in the menu system. This list does not

       include "ALL" that are available. In addition to the text variables in the list you can also call
       out any Parameter in CABINET VISION whether it is a System Parameter or a User
       Parameter by following the format below and replacing the variable name with the
       Parameter you want to call.
       Examples
       To call out the AX Rotation of a Cabinet you would simply type {cab.ax}.
       OR

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       To call our a User Parameter named CabNote1 you would simply type {cab.cabnote1}.

Text Format Options

There are three formatting options available specifically to Automatic Text:
       u: - Sets first character to upper case.
       l: - Sets first character to lower case.
       n: - Displays negative numbers within parentheses
       Example
       {u:cab.cabnote1}
              If a variable is not populated with data it will show the Variable name in CAD mode.
       However, in Normal View modes it will be invisible. This is a very handy feature that allows
       you to have Notes on Assemblies that maybe populated by a UCS only in certain conditions.
       This allows you to control the display of the note conditionally.

General

{dim} - Displays the formatted Dimension for the Object. See the CAD Dimensioning topic for more
information.
{value} - Displays the content of the Text Objects Value field formatted as specified. If you select
or type {value} as your Text you will get additional options in the sidebar for the Text object. Please
note you can use {value} in the Text field along with other Text and or Parameters.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Value - The actual value for the {value} parameter to display.
       Type - The Type of value to display. There are six possible Types:
    Measurement
    Degrees
    Integer
    Boolean
    Decimal
    Currency

There are several options when selecting CAD Objects you can initiate by simply clicking points
on screen around the selected CAD Object(s).

Scale

Once a Group of CAD Objects is selected simply left click one of the corner points to Scale the
selected Objects. You either eye-ball the Scale or you can use the Tab key to change the values in
the sidebar for the selected objects.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Stretch

Once a Group of CAD Objects is selected simply left click one of the mid-points to Stretch the
selected Objects. You can either eye-ball the Stretch or you can use the Tab key to change the
values in the sidebar for the selected objects.

              You can also Stretch to a Snap point. For example you can pick a single line and grab
       and end-point and stretch/extend that line to any other Snap point.

Move

Once a Group of CAD Objects is selected simply left click any point within the object to use that as
the Move point, this will allow you to Move an Object or Group of Objects from one known (snap
point) position to another (snap point position). You can also Move the selected Group of Objects
by using the Tab key to change values in the sidebar.

              Since Scale and Stretch are also available by clicking the corners of selected CAD
       make sure the proper cursor prompt is used.

                  Scale/Stretch
                     Move from End Point

              When using Copy and Paste on CAD Objects, upon Pasting the Objects, they remain
       selected to allow you to use the three (Scale, Stretch and/or Move) options described above.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Splash -

Splashes can not only be added when creating Counter Tops in Plan view but can also be added
to your Designs from the Elevation View. From Elevation View simply click the Splash button in the
sidebar. Adding a New splash uses the Shape Editor. You can also modify the Shape of Splashes
placed via the Counter Top tool from Elevation view simply by right clicking on them in Splash
mode and selecting Edit Shape.
To access the options for changing the Splashes Thickness and other properties, right click on the
Splash as soon as you enter the Editing window. The following menu will appear if you have
performed this correctly.

              If the Splash you are attempting to Edit was placed using the Tops tool, you will need to
       Edit the Splash in this area before having access to Splash Properties.
Selecting Delete will delete the selected Splash.
Selecting Delete All will delete all the Splashes on the current Wall.
Selecting Edit will take the Splash to the Assembly Level. There is very limited access to modify
Splashes at the Assembly Level.
Selecting the Edit Shape right click option will open The Shape Editor options in the ribbonbar
allowing you to Edit the Shape of the Splash.
After Clicking Properties the following menu appears:

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
This area allows setting the Thickness of the selected Splash. Note that the Material and Texture
can also be adjusted here.

Camera -

The Camera button, available in the sidebar, will open the Camera Editor giving you the ability to
set a view position to show a perspective view of your design. The closer the Camera position is
to what you are viewing the more intense the perspective.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Simply drag the Camera around to where you want to view from, you can also drag the view point
end and move, lengthen, or shorten it. Following are the options available in the Camera Editor
sidebar:
 Position - Height - The Height of the Camera from the Floor.
 Position - Target Height - The Height of the view point's end.
 Lens - Angle - The Angle width of the Camera Lens.
The Preview button will allow you to Preview the results in the View without having to Close the
Camera Editor.

Lights -

The Lights button, available in the sidebar, will give you an overhead view of the current design
with the light showing (red/blue/light blue/orange) in relationship to where it is currently placed.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Simply select the Light in the view to set it's Properties. The best thing to do with lighting is to
experiment with it to see what works best for you.

The Automatic lighting should be setup to place at least the following two Lights in every Room:
 The Sun Light, which is a directional light placed in the southwest corner of the scene.
 The Center Light, which is a Point Light placed in the Center of the Scene..
There are other Lights that can be placed in the Room automatically, if they are enabled, as your
design changes.
 Corner Light, a Directional Light in the southeast corner of the Scene.
 Door and/or Window Spotlight added directly behind a Wall that has one or more Windows or

   Doors in it.
 Wall Corner Light added where two walls meet and there are Assemblies present.
 Wall Spotlight added 12" below the Height of the Wall at the middle of a Wall that is up to 300"

   long, two lights evenly spaced to anything longer. Wall Ends are ignored.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 Wall Spotlight added 30" above a Peninsula Wall at the middle of the Peninsula Wall that is up
   to 300" long, two lights evenly spaced to anything longer. Wall Ends are ignored.

You can modify the settings for any of these Automatic Lights and your changes will be preserved.
If you would like to have your own Light Schedule for the Job you can click the New or Copy
button in the toolbar.

To adjust a light, select it by clicking on it. It will be highlighted with a dashed outline when it is
selected. Now you can move it anywhere in the view port or change any of the Light, Beam, or
Direction specifications available to that particular type of Light.

You also have the ability to add or delete lights with the Add/Delete  buttons and to save

different lighting setups to the Light Schedule. These lighting schedules are specific to the job you

are currently working in.

Light Properties

Enabled

A light can be temporarily shut off by setting Enabled to No.

Color

The Color list lets you tint the light to simulate different types of light sources, such as White Light
(whitish), Sky Light (bluish), Sun Light (yellowish), Fluorescent (greenish), or Incandescent
(orangish). You can just use White Light (the default setting for a new light), but if you want to give
your scene a little more color, try experimenting with the other color settings. The more lights you
set to a particular color, the more pronounced that color will be. There are also pure color lights
available (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow, Orange, Violet) if you want a color to be more pronounced.

Brightness

Brightness is your most important setting and controls the overall intensity of the light.

                           © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Beam Properties

The Beam Properties area will allow you to set up the type of light beam that you will need for the
effect you are looking for. These properties are not available for the Ambient or the Head lights.

Type

There are three Light types:
· Spot - Appears as a red circle and projects a cone-like beam of light.
· Directional - Appears as a blue circle and projects a wide parallel beam of light as if from a

   distant source.
· Point - Appears as a light blue circle and acts as a ball of light projecting light in all directions.

   This is the most versatile or all light types.

Height

This setting allows you to set the Height of a Spot or Point Light. Height is not an option for a
Directional Light.

Angle

If you have the light set as a spot light, you will be able to control the angle of the light-cone it
creates. The tighter the cone, the more intense the light will be and the stronger the shadows.

Cast Shadows

Unlike the real world, it is possible to set whether a light casts shadows or not. Sometimes if you
are just using a light to fill in a dark part of a scene, you may not want that light to cast a distinct
shadow. The fewer lights casting shadows, the faster your scene will render.

Softness

This setting affects the sharpness of the spotlight cone and the shadows that are cast.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
In Ray-Trace rendering, if you have the Beam Softness set to zero and you have the Ray-Trace
Sharp Shadows flag turned on, then you will generate a very sharp detailed shadow. In general,
you will get more natural looking lighting with the normal soft shadows.

Direction Properties

The Direction Properties are not available for Point Lights.

Vertical

This setting allows you to set the Vertical Angle of your Light. You can also click the action button
in the Vertical field to get the Angle window. By grabbing the "nose" of the light you can adjust its
vertical angle.

Once you get the light pointing in any direction, other than straight down, it will also have a handle
in the Light Editor which you can drag to control where it is pointing.
Horizontal
This setting allows you to set the Horizontal Angle of your Light. Your Light has to have a Vertical
Angle set to anything other than -90 for the Horizontal field to be available.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Geometry Properties

The Geometry Properties allow you to indicate if the Light Source is actual physically visible. For
Spot and Point Lights you establish the Radius and for Directional Lights you establish its Width
and Length.

Advanced Lighting

Lighting is the main thing you will need to spend time with in order to use xRender to its full
potential. Before you continue into this section, make sure you are familiar with the previous
section on how to select, move, and adjust light settings.
Planning your Lighting
Good lighting requires a little common sense plus a bit of creativity. Before you start adding lights
to your scene, ask yourself the following questions:
Primary Light Sources
What is the primary sources of light in your design? Lights, windows etc...
 Is the sun shining through a window?
 Are there light fixtures within your scene?
 What "time of day" is it?
Secondary Sources
Are there any logical sources of light beyond the bounds of you room?
Are there sources of ambient or reflected light?
For each Light Source
 Is it near or far away?
 Is it hard and directional or soft and diffuse?

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 Does it cast any noticeable shadow?

 Is it direct light or light reflected off walls and floor.

Sources of Inspiration

Look at magazines and pictures of rooms. You may even want to create a collection of rooms with
different types of lighting situations. Try to figure out the light sources in those pictures and
practice copying those effects in xRender. With a little bit of practice you'll be amazed at how
much your renderings will improve.

Types of Lights

Following are the types of lights you can use in your scene.

Spot Lights

Spot Lights (red circle) cast a strong cone of light. The narrower the beam angle, the more intense
the light and the more intense the shadow it casts. The angle of the beam ranges from 0 to 180
degrees. A setting of below 90 degrees casts a strong shadow while a setting of 180 casts
virtually no shadow. The Beam Softness setting affects the softness of the shadows a spot light
casts, as well as the fuzziness of the spot light cone. Spot lights are most useful to shine light
through windows or to simulate Can Lights or Lights flush to the Ceiling.

Directional Lights

Directional lights (blue circle) simulate light coming from a long distance away. It projects a wide
parallel beam of light and, at high brightness settings, casts a strong shadow. Though directional
lights do not project a cone of light, the Beam Softness setting does affect the softness of the
shadows it casts. Use directional lights to fill large areas.

              It does not matter where a directional light is placed in the scene; only the direction it is
       pointing. Even if the directional light is in the Room, it will cast shadows as if it is far outside
       the Room. It also can't shine through walls.

Point Lights

Point Lights (light blue circle) are the most common form of artificial Lighting in the real world. It
most accurately simulates a light bulb as it casts light in all directions from its placement.

Lighting Setup

The following topics cover some basic lighting setups.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The "Top" Light

At the beginning of a xRender project, you will start with a single point light centered above your
scene. If the light is too close to any wall, move it out further so the light can better angle in toward
the fronts of your cabinets. A light in this position is referred to as a "Center" light.

The "Key" Light

To give your rendering more contrast, it is a good idea to add another light, in addition to the
"Center" light, coming in from the side. This light is referred to as the "Key" light, or primary light
source in the scene. The idea is to make one of your walls brighter than the other. Usually the wall
adjacent or opposite the window is the brightest wall. The "Key" light is usually a spot light
positioned at ceiling height, angled slightly, and pointing primarily toward one wall.

The "Fill" Light

Sometimes a third light is added to the scene. The "Fill" light is usually positioned to fill in the
areas of the scene not covered by the "Key" light. A directional light can serve well as a "Fill" light.
The "Fill" light is usually set to a much lower brightness than the "Key" light.

The "Fill" light is usually placed at about half room height, pointing sideways. Usually the higher
the height of the "Key" light, the lower the height of the "Fill" light.

Since much of the light in a kitchen is reflected light from walls and floors, try to use the "Fill" light
to simulate this effect. For instance, you might tilt the "Fill" light slightly upward to simulate light
being reflected upward from the floor. This can lessen the severity of shadows under upper
cabinets. Good use of a "Fill" light can add a subtle glow to cabinet faces and lessen the flatness
of the lighting in darker parts of the scene.

Window Light

A common addition to a kitchen lighting setup is a light shining through a window. A window light
is usually a point light set to cast shadows. For direct sunlight, the Beam Softness should be set
very sharp, for indirect sunlight set it softer. You may want to set the color of the window light to
either sunlight or skylight.

The "Key" light inside the room is usually turned so that it is the pointing in the same general
direction as the window light. The window light is used to cast bright light through the window
frame, but the "Key" light is still the primary light source inside the room.

Order Entry -

The Order Entry screen shows a list of everything that appears in the Job and some of the general
properties of each item. On the sidebar you will also see that the Catalogs are accessible so that
items may be added to the Job directly through the Order Entry screen. To add an item (such as a
Cabinet, Appliance, etc.) simply find that item in the correct Catalog and then drag it out and drop
it onto an empty area of the Order Entry list. Adding items in this manner includes those items in
all aspects of the Job except the drawings. In other words, if you add items through the Order
Entry screen, those items will appear in the Reports and the Bid but will not appear in Floor Plan,
Elevation, or 3D views.
Order entry allows spreadsheet style Object management. This tool is useful for viewing your
Objects and their configuration for an entire Room, on a single sheet.

At first the Order Entry screen appears the same as the Cabinet List Report Screen. There are
several differences though. The areas highlighted in RED above contain data regarding the
Objects in the current Room. That data can be changed at this level. This tool would be useful
when furnishing a specific amount of Cabinets, some with Finished Ends Left, Some Right, etc.
The advantage is that you do not have to draw Walls, and place Objects, yet, all other features are

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
available, such as cut list, material summaries, section editing, bidding, etc. The Cabinet List at
the Report area does not allow near the data modification available here.

What are Rate Tables?

First let's get some of the terminology down so we don't get too confused during the rest of this
topic. Rate Tables are basically a store house for a group of Bid Methods. You can create an
unlimited number of Rate Tables and utilize them together in any way you want.

Selecting/Creating/Editing Rate Tables

To select/activate a Rate Table simply click on the check box next to it. You can use as many Rate
Tables in as many combinations as you want. In the Rate Tables and What If's topic some techniques
using multiple Rate Tables to create "What If" Bid Scenarios is covered.

To create or edit Rate Tables click on the Rate Table  option in the Bid Center ribbonbar. This
will open the Select Rate Tables area.

             © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

       jobs without previsouly selected Rate Tables simply click the "Set As Default Rate Table"
       button here.
To edit an existing Rate Table simply highlight it and click the Setup Button. To create a new Rate
Table just click the Setup Button. Once you have clicked on the Setup button the Setup Rate
Tables area will open.

% of Material Cost

This Bid Method takes the value you enter (Whole Number representing the Percentage) and
multiplies it by the Total Cost of Materials used in the Job. Material Cost is returned and calculated
from the highlighted settings below in the Material Manager.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Let's break these highlighted areas down.
First let's start with the Default Markup and Default Tax Rate. The Default Tax Rate comes from
the Tax Rate either entered here by you for the Material or is brought over by the Vendor selected
for the Material. The Default Markup is either entered by you or brought over by the Vendor
selected for the Material.
The Tax Rate percentage is only applied to individual Materials if the Sales Tax field is set to True
for that Material. Typically, you will only select Tax for those Materials that "you" pay tax on. There
is a separate area in the Bid Center to calculate the Tax your "customer" pays.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The Default Cost field in the Materials Properties area represents the selected Units Cost. So, in
the example above the Cost is per Sheet. This Cost is either entered by you or is brought over by
the Vendor selected for the Material.
The example below represents one Sheet of the Material we have been looking at. In this case the
price will come through to the Bid Center for one Sheet as:
 1.00 Sheets x $17.00 = $17.00
 2% Default Markup = $.34
 0% Tax = $0.00 (Because Sales Tax is False)
 Total = $17.34
The final Material Property that will affect % of Material Cost is the Waste field. The Waste
Percentage entered for the Material in the Material Manager will be added, in this case, to the
number of Sheets represented in the Job.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Per Hour of Assembly Labor

This Bid Method takes the value you enter and multiplies it by the total Labor Hours calculated by
CABINET VISION. Labor Values for Assembly come from the Object's Labor Property.

Per Hour of Drawer Labor

This Bid Method takes the value you enter and multiplies it by the total Labor Hours calculated by
CABINET VISION. Labor Values for Drawer Boxes come from the Drawer/Roll-Out Construction's
Labor Per Box value used for the Drawer.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Per Hour of Parts Labor

This Bid Method takes the value you enter and multiplies it by the total Labor Hours calculated by
CABINET VISION. Labor Values for Parts come from the Part Manager. Each Part contained in the
Part Catalog has two Labor Settings. The first setting is Labor Setup, this value represents a one
time Labor Cost in minutes for this Part per Job. The next setting is Labor Each, this value
represents an incremental value based on each of these Parts within the Job.

Per Hour of Roll Out Labor

This Bid Method takes the value you enter and multiplies it by the total Labor Hours calculated by
CABINET VISION. Labor Values for Roll-Outs come from the Drawer - Roll-Out Construction's
Labor Per Box value used for the Roll-Out.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Per Hour of Total Labor

This Bid Method takes the value you enter and multiplies it by the total Labor Hours calculated by
CABINET VISION. Labor Values for Total Labor come from a Total of all the above Labor Bid
Methods.

Use Assembly Catalog Pricing

This Bid Method can be used to set an Up-charge or Discount to Assembly Pricing that is brought
over to the Bid Center. By Default any Assembly that has a Value for Price in its Properties will

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
come over and be added to the Bid by default. This Bid Method, if used with no values, would
actually double the Price values applied to the Assemblies. The best way to explain this Bid
Method is by example. The image below represents what you would see with no active Rate Table
and you bring in a Std Base with a Price of $100.00.

Without utilizing this Bid Method in your Rate Table there is no way to either Up-charge or
Discount this price. The graphic below demonstrates how to use this Bid Method using the Markup
field to give a 20% (-120 Markup) discount on the Assembly demonstrated above.

And here is the result:

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
You could do a 20% Up-Charge utilizing the same Method. You would set the Markup to 80%
instead.

Use Door Catalog Pricing

This Bid Method does not use the Value field. It takes the Prices you enter for Doors, Drawer
Fronts, False Fronts, and Panels and their sub-components and totals them for the Job.
There are several places where this data is retrieved.
Door Catalog
The first area where Door Catalog Pricing is retrieved is from the Door Styles Price fields. You can
add a price either "Per Door" or "Per SqUnit" or even a combination of both. The highlighted
portion of the image below shows these fields.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Door/Drawer Front Material Schedules
The next area where Door Catalog Pricing is retrieved is from the Material Schedule(s) assigned
to the Door Style. You can add a price either Per Door (Cost/Door) or Per Square Foot or Meter
(Cost/SqFt/SqM) or even a combination of both. These fields can be used to add Door Pricing Up-
charges based on the Material(s) utilized by the Door Style. The highlighted portion of the image
below shows these fields.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Door Profiles

The next area where Door Catalog Pricing is retrieved is from the Profile(s) assigned to the Door
Style. You can add a price either "Per Door" or "Per SqFt" or even a combination of both. These
fields can be used to add Door Pricing Up-charges based on the Profile(s) utilized by the Door
Style. The highlighted portion of the image below shows these fields.

              The Per SqFt Price entered here represents the Square Footage of the Door that the
       Profile is assigned to.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Use Drawer Catalog Pricing

This Bid Method does not use the Value field. It takes the Price you enter for Drawer Box(es) in
the Drawer/Roll Out Construction and totals them for the Job. The highlighted portion of the image
below shows the entry field.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Use Molding Catalog Pricing

Similar to % of Material Cost this Bid Method pulls pricing from Molding Materials (Molding you
Buy) in the Material Manager. See the Use Profile Catalog Bid Method for Molding you make from
the Molding Manager.

Use Part Catalog Pricing

This Bid Method does not use the Value field. It takes the Price and or Formula you enter for
Part(s) in the Part Manager and totals them for the Job. When you are in Internal Mode the Part Pricing
will be broken out at the main level of the Bid Center. Parts will be sorted in the list alphabetically
by the Part name.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Parts are also broken out for each Cabinet in the Catalog Level of the Bid Center.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Use Profile Catalog Pricing

This Bid Method does not use the Value field. It takes the Price you enter for Molding(s) in the
Molding Manager and totals them for the Job. The Cost Per Job field would be a one time Cost when
the selected Molding is used in a Job. Cost Per Strip would represent each Piece of Molding. Cost
Per FT/Meter would represent the Price you charge for each Foot/Meter of Molding. The
highlighted portion of the image below shows the entry fields.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Use Roll Out Catalog Pricing

This Bid Method does not use the Value field. It takes the Price you enter for Roll-Out(s) in the
Drawer/Roll Out Construction and totals them for the Job. The highlighted portion of the image
below shows the entry field.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
This option opens an area that allows you to select Bid Methods as add-ons for a specific Job. This
area is not used in lieu of Rate Tables but only for specific add-ons in addition to the current Rate
Tables. Unless you click the "Set as System Defaults" button these Add-Ons will be temporary to the
current Job only.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Following are the Tabs in the Bid Center Options Area:

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Totals Tab

There are eight options on the Totals Tab:
 Default Deposit % - Allows you to set the Default Deposit % you require your Customers to

   pay for the Job.
 Default Markup % - Allows you to set the Default Markup % for your Jobs.
 Include Drawer Fronts in Door Count - If you treat your Drawer Fronts as Doors when

   Bidding by Door select this option. This would come into play when using the Per Door Bid Method.
 Include False Fronts in Door Count - If you treat your False Fronts as Doors when Bidding

   by Door select this option. This would come into play when using the Per Door Bid Method.
 Price Fillers As Cabinets - If you consider your Fillers Cabinets enable this option. Enabling

   this will include Fillers in Lineal Foot/Meter and Per Cabinet type Bid Methods.
 Price Detached Toe Kicks As Cabinets - If you consider your Detached Toes Cabinets

   enable this option. Enabling this will include Fillers in Lineal Foot and Per Cabinet type Bid Methods.
 Lineal Total For Corner Cabinets is Width + Depth - If you calculate your Lineal totals for

   Corner Cabinets by both width and depth select this option. See the two figures below for
   examples:

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
With this option Disabled the Cabinet below would calculate as 3 Lineal Feet.
With this option Enabled the Cabinet below would calculate as 6 Lineal Feet.

 Include Doors, Drawers & Hardware in Part Count - If you include Doors, Drawers and
   Hardware in your Part Count calculations Enable this option. This would come into play when
   using the Per Part Bid Method.

 Estimate Sheets of Material - With this option enabled the Bid Center will use the results of a
   generic panel Optimization to estimate Sheet Goods usage rather than simple area estimations.
   This functionality uses a generic Optimizer with the following limitations:
   · It will not use your Optimization settings even if you have the Optimizer, it uses predefined
      settings.
   · If there is an error during optimization for any reason (ie. part that won't fit the sheet) you will
      get a Warning in the status bar about that Material and it will end Optimization on that
      Material and use the waste factor from the Material Catalog.
   · Buy out parts are never included in a sheet estimate
   · Any material that has a valid Sheet Size are estimated regardless of their "CNC" or
      "Optimize" Settings.
   · The grain property of the sheet is honored.
   · The Sheet estimate uses a 1/4" trim, 1/8" kerf, Block Nesting with no restrictions on phases.
      As a result the actual Optimization results may be better or worse depending on TrueShape
      versus Block and Yield versus Labor.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Rounding Tab

There are two main options on the Rounding Tab:
 Line Item Rounding - There are three options for Line Item Rounding:

   · Round To The Nearest Penny - Selecting this option will Round all the Line Items in your
      Bid to the nearest Penny using standard Rounding rules.

   · Round To The Nearest Dollar - Selecting this option will Round all the Line Items in your
      Bid to the nearest Dollar using standard Rounding rules.

   · Round Up To The Nearest Dollar - Selecting this option will Round Up all the Line Items in
      your Bid to the nearest Dollar.

 Totals Rounding - There are two options for Totals Rounding:
   · Show Cost Of Actual Total - Selecting this option will display the actual Total vs. a Rounded
      Total.
   · Round Cost To Display Total - Selecting this option will display the Rounded Total based
      on the selected Line Item Rounding option.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Show / Hide Tab

There are four options on the Rounding Tab:
 Show Price Lines That Are $0.00 - Selecting this option instructs the Bid Center to display all

   Line Items in your Bid including those that have a value of 0. This is especially helpful when
   setting up your Rate Tables for the first time.
 Show Hidden Lines In Internal Mode - This option is used for Stock Pricing.
 Show Stock Cabinet Options At Opening Screen - This option is used for Stock Pricing.
 Show Legacy Line Items & Variables - Selecting this option will allow or suppress the display
   of Legacy Bid Methods.

Modular Catalog Word Forms

In addition, all available Microsoft Word Form Templates for the selected Catalog will appear at
the top of the Catalog Information Screen in the Report drop down.

These Microsoft Word Form Templates are used to merge Catalog information from Solid Design

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
into printable Microsoft Word documents. These Forms will list all the units in the Room, the Door
Styles, and Catalog options used, and the associated prices in a format designed for reporting and
ordering purposes.
To activate the Form, click the drop-down arrow next to the Form drop down menu and select the
desired Form from the list. Then, click on the "Order Form" option to the right of the drop-down list.
When you activate your first Form you will, more than likely, be prompted to browse to the
Microsoft Word (WinWord.exe) application. By default Microsoft Word is installed at C:\Program
Files\Microsoft Office\root\Officenn\. nn representing the Version of Office you have installed.
Microsoft Word will open and a security prompt will appear; select "Enable Macros" or "Enable
Content" (depending on the Version of Word you are using) on this prompt to proceed.

In versions of Word prior to Word 2007 simply selecting Enable Macros will enable all Word
Forms. In Word 2007 and higher the Enable Content option is only per instance. You will need to
add the location of the Forms to the Trusted Locations area of the Word Trust Center. To do this
follow these steps:
In Word 2007 click the Office button and select Word Options.
In Word 2010 and higher click the File Tab and select Options (highlighted below).

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
In the Word Options area select Trust Center from the sidebar then click the Trust Center
Settings... button.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
In the Trust Center select the Trusted Locations option in the sidebar and click the Add New
Location.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Click the Browse button.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Browse to the location of the Forms. This is typically C:\ProgramData\Hexagon\CABINET VISION\
CV 2025\Database and click "OK".

Close Word and re-open the Form from Cabinet Vision.
Next, an Order Options window will appear prompting the entry of User-defined fields or to pull the
requested information from Cabinet Vision (information is pulled from the Job Properties fields).
Once this information is satisfactorily entered, click the "OK" button to merge the current Job's
Modular Catalog information to the Microsoft Word Form Template.

The Advanced Reports area is used to select, print, and organize your Reports into "Report
Groups" that you create and maintain. A Report Group is a collection of Reports organized under
one heading or name. Using Report Groups makes it easy to print multiple Reports; you just
select a "Report Group" to print, and then click on the "Print Reports In Group" button and all the
Reports contained in that "Report Group" will print.
While it is true that you can start printing Bid information about your Job as soon as you have
something laid out, as Solid comes preset up with sample Report Groups. It is also true that those
Report Groups might not contain the Bid Reports you would like them too. Therefore you will have
some preliminary setup work to do to customize the Advanced Reports area to your way of doing
things.
Once you have the Advanced Reports area setup to your satisfaction printing is just a matter of
clicking on the "Advanced Reports" button. You then select the "Report Group" to print and then
click on the "Print Reports In Group" button.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The following options are available in the primary Advanced Reports area
Click on the sidebar options below for more information

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
              It is important to note that the Advanced Reports area will remember the last Printer
       you printed an individual Report too. This is a handy feature when printing a Report Group

Report Center -

When your Job is complete, the Report Center allows you to print information about your Job.
The Report Center is also used to select, and organize your Reports into "Report Groups" that you
create and maintain. A Report Group is a collection of Reports organized under one heading or
name. Using Report Groups makes it easy to print multiple Reports; you just select a "Report
Group" to print, and then click on the "Print Reports In Group" button and all the Reports
contained in that "Report Group" will print.
While it is true that you can start printing information about your Job as soon as you have
something laid out, as CABINET VISION comes preset up with sample Report Groups. It is also true
that those Report Groups might not contain the Reports you would like them too. Therefore you
will have some preliminary setup work to do to customize the Report Center to your way of doing
things.
Once you have the Report Center setup to your satisfaction printing is just a matter of clicking on
the "Reports" button then clicking on the "Report Center" button. You then select the "Report
Group" to print and then click on the "Print Reports In Group" button.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Click the options below for more information

The Export option allows you to Export the currently active Report to another application or file for
further modification. Finished reports can be exported to a number of popular formats, such as
spreadsheet, word processor, HTML, XML, and other common data interchange formats. This
makes the distribution of information easier. For example, you may want to use the report data to
project trends in a spreadsheet package or to enhance the presentation of data in a desktop
publishing package.
The exporting process requires you to specify a format via the Direct to... option.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Export Direct To... Types

The export formats supported by the Report Center can be broadly categorized in two groups:
page-based formats and record-based formats. Page-based formats tend to produce a more exact
output. The emphasis of these formats is layout representation and formatting. Formatting refers
to attributes such as font style, text color, text alignment, background color, and so on. Layout
refers to object position, object size, and the relationship between these attributes and other
objects. Depending on the format of the Report, it may not be possible for the program to preserve
all layout and formatting perfectly, but page-based formats, in general, preserve these properties
as closely as possible.

With record-based formats, the emphasis is on data rather than the layout and formatting.
However, in some formats--such as Microsoft Excel - Data only--you will notice that some
formatting is exported.

Please consider:

 Due to the format, the layout cannot always be taken over 1:1 because there are specific
   restrictions when converting to these formats.

 The Microsoft® Word export format creates DOCX files that are compatible with Microsoft®
   Office 2007 and higher. Tables will be exported on continuous pages to support later editing.

Many formats have various possibilities for configuration. You can make use of these by clicking
the "Options" button.

 With Excel formats, you can reduce the number of columns and rows to the minimum required
   by means of the "Only data from table object(s)" option. Also all pages can be exported into one
   sheet and the output formats 'xls' as well as 'xlsx' are available.

 The picture export to JPEG, TIFF and PNG supports optional automatic cropping of the results
   to the content. An exported barcode is therefore only exactly as large as required to display the
   complete content.

Following are the supported Outputs:

 Adobe PDF Format

 Microsoft Excel Format

 Microsoft Word Format

 Rich Text Format (RTF)

 XHTML/CSS Format

 Multi-Mime HTML Format

 Text (CSV) Format
 Text (Layout) Format
 XML Format

 PNG Picture

 TIFF Picture

Toolbar

Following are the Advanced Property toolbar tools.

    Import/Link Data For Report

This tool allows you to import data that is found in databases outside of report.mdb. This can
include, but is not limited to, data found in the following databases:
 Door.ddb
 BidData.mdb
You can also import data from a database that is not provided by CABINET VISION.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Type - Import

       The Import options are as follows:
     Name - This is the name of the table that will be created, in the report.mdb
     Source - This is the path to the database that will be used.
     Table - Once a source is selected, this will list out all of the available tables inside the

       database to choose from.
     Fields - This checklist contains the various fields that the selected table has available for

       import.
       Name
       As stated above, the name of the import is the name of the table that will be created in the
       report.mdb file when the report is generated.

                      Make sure that you follow these simple rules:
       1. Do not use a reserved name. An instance of this would be Parts. There is already a

            Parts table in the report.mdb and using this as a name will cause the program to not
            create the table.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       2. Do not use illegal characters. Basically, the safest bet is to only use letters and the
            underscore (_) character. Anything else may cause problems.

       Source
       The source is the path to the database. Click on the ellipsis button (...) to open a dialog that
       will allow you to select a database. Once the database is entered, this field will update to
       have the proper pathing.
       Table
       This is a list of tables that are available, in the selected database. Since the import can only
       create one table at a time, just select the table you want to use here.
       Fields
       This is a list of the fields that are contained in the database, in the table that was selected.
       The fields are in alphabetical order, and will be in this order when the table is imported into
       the report.mdb. Just place a check in the fields that you want imported.
Type - Link

       Linking is similar to an import, but rather than creating a new table from a different database,
       it creates a new 'view' from the report.mdb.
       The Link options are as follows:

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
     Name - The name of the link as it will appear in the designer.
     SQL - The SQL statement that will be used to generate the view.

       Name
       As stated above, the name is what the name of the view will be once it is generated inside of
       the report.mdb.

                      Make sure that you follow these simple rules:
       1. Do not use a reserved name. An instance of this would be Parts. There is already a

            Parts table in the report.mdb and using this as a name will cause the program to not
            create the table.
       2. Do not use illegal characters. Basically, the safest bet is to only use letters and the
            underscore (_) character. Anything else may cause problems.
       SQL
       This is the SQL statement that you can use to generate your view. It must be a valid SQL
       Select statement.

    Create Table Wizard

The Create Table Wizard is a list of the tables, as they will appear in the report for use. The tables
can come from multiple datasources, not just the ones provided by Cabinet Vision.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
There are nine tabs in the Create Table Wizard:
Source
The Source tab is used to define the data source that this table is drawn from:

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
    This tab has the following options:
 Name - This is the name of the table, as it will appear in the report.
 Source - This is the path to the database that will be used.
 Specify Provider - This allows you the option to define a data source provider [Advanced].

    Name
    As stated above, this is the name of the table, as it will appear in the report. If you leave this
    blank the proper table name (from within the database) will be used.
    Source
    The source of the database, is its location on your hard drive or network. This field is not
    directly editable, rather, you click on the select source button next to it to browse to your data
    source.
    Specify Provider
    There are times when you would like to connect to a non-access database, this allows you
    to define the provider that will be used to access the data source. Once you have specified

                                                                © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
the provider, make sure to click the 'Test Data Source' button to make sure it is valid.
              The vast majority of reports will never need to have the provider specified, this is

       for very advanced users that have a multitude of data sources that they want to report
       from.
Select
The Select tab is used to create a select statement that will pull the appropriate data from
the database.

First, you would select the table you want to use, from the drop down list.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Once you have selected the table (or view), you need to add the table. You do that by
clicking on the add button.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
To know what table(s) (or view(s)) have been added, you can just look back at the tables
drop down list and see that a 'plus' symbol has been added to the table name.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
              When you add multiple tables to a query, you have to specify the join type (or how
       the data mates together). Look at the Joins section below to see what happens when
       you add a second table.

Now you will be able to select the fields that you want to pull from. To do this, all you need to
do is take a look at the list of columns (if they are greyed out, that means you haven't added

the table). You can use  + Click or                                  + Click to select multiple fields.

                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Simply select the column(s) you want, then click on the add columns button.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
This will place all of the selected columns into the 'selected columns' list.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Removing a column is as easy as clicking on the column you want to remove (on the right
list), and then clicking the remove column button.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

                                              © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

 Criteria - this is the SQL approved filter criteria that can be used.

                 This is a VERY important tab and will have a huge result on the order in which

   With this tab selected, you have the following options available to you:
 Simple Sort - This allows you to just specify what columns should be sorted, in an

1 (2), 2, 3 (2)
This is reminiscent of the cabinet (qty) list found on the old Part_List.rpt file.

   Group Cabinet (Qty) - This allows you to select the list type.

   The default value is n/a which means that no list is generated. You can also use one of the
   following options:
 Parts
 Doors

 Custom
   Each one of these options requires a special setup in the Select tab. Essentially, you need to

   change the tab to look like this:

   With this you now have the following options:
 CabinetID Field - This is the field that holds the cabinet's ID number.
 Quantity Field (Count) - This is the field that will be counted.
 Grouping Criteria - This is a list of the fields that you will group on.

   'Group', then it should remain unchecked.
   Once you are done with all of the options, Cabinet Vision will use the given criteria to create
   a the Cabinet (Qty) field and attach it to the appropriate record.

                                                              © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Comment List
       This is a drop down list that allows you to select one of the built in comment lists that can be
       created by Cabinet Vision for reporting.
       To get one of the automatic items, you must have grouped the fields together properly. They
       require the following information:
     ID field
     Comment Field
       If you don't get an automatic one, because Cabinet Vision might not recognize your query as
       one for automatic selection, you can still select the Custom option to create your own.
Optional Comment List Format

               This allows you to format the comments that are created. You can use variables to
               setup the list. The variables MUST match a column name that has been selected.
               The default value is:
               Cab# {Cabinet} - {Comment}
               Let's break this down:
               Anything that is contained in curly braces is a variable (i.e. {Cabinet}). Anything not
               contained in curly braces is a string literal (i.e. Cab#). All string literals are displayed, in
               the report, as they are shown here. All variables will pull the data from the given
               column name. In this instance, we have the following columns being used:
         Cabinet
         Comment
               If the columns don't have the same name as here, they you may get a error when you
               run the report.

Custom List
This tab allows you to define the values for a list of concatenated values.
To learn more about what concatenation is, please visit this website:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concatenation

              This feature was specifically designed to allow a concatenated string to be placed
       on label reports in the S2M Center, but can be used for anything that you can think of
       in both Cabinet Vision and the S2M Center.

This tab has the following options:

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 Create Custom List - This enables this tab to create a custom list.

 Primary Field - This is the primary field that represents the unique ID of the data from this
   table.

 Foreign Table - This allows you to select the table/view, from the given datasource, that
   contains the records you wish to concat.

 Foreign Field - This is the reference to the id of the unique data from this table.

 Display Field - This is the field that holds the information to concat.

 Optional Display Format - This allows you to customize the display format for your custom
   lists.

   Create Custom List

   Enabling this option allows you to let Cabinet Vision know that you want to create a custom
   concatenated list.

   Primary Field

   The primary field is the unique id field that is found in this field. In the example given here,
   this would be the Cabinet ID field.

   Foreign Table

   This is the table, or view, contained in your data source, that has the records that you want
   to concatenate. In the example given here, this would be the DoorLabels table.

   Foreign Field

   This is the field, in the selected Foreign Table that holds a reference to the 'ID' field in this
   table. This data should match the data type, and value, found in this tables Primary Field. In
   the example given here, this would be the Cabinet D field.

   Display Field

   This is the field that holds the strings to concatenate together. In the example given here, this
   would be the DoorLabel field.

   Optional Display Format

   This allows you to specify a special format for your list. You can use variables and string
   literals.

   A string literal will be displayed exactly as it is typed here.

                                                              © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       A variable will use what's in the curly braces ({}).
       You can use one variable as of right now. That's {field}, which will use the 'Display' field that
       is given. The string literal '\r' is the literal for 'carriage return'. This will create a new line after
       the string is created.

    Relationships

A relationship is a connection, between two tables, that have related data.
For a better understanding of relationships, you can learn about how relational databases (such
as Microsoft Access and Microsoft SQL Server) work:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relational_database

              Do not use a relationship in your report unless absolutely necessary (for sub table
       creation) as these can cause severe slow down of the report generation.
When you create a new relationship, the following dialog appears:

       This dialog has the following options:
     Primary Table Name - This is a list of the primary tables that have been created for this

       report.
     Primary Field Name - This is the list of fields, in the primary table, that hold the 'parent'

       data.
     Foreign Table Name - This is a list of the foreign tables that have been created for this

       report.
     Foreign Field Name - This is a list of the fields, in the foreign table, that hold the 'child' data.
Primary Table Name

       This is the name of the primary table. A primary table holds all of the parent data that will be

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
   used. An example would be the Cabinets table in the report.mdb. It has the following fields:
 Cabinet ID
 Cabinet Name
 Width String
 Height String
 Depth String
 Etc.

   The Cabinet ID is a primary field as it defines the cabinet record uniquely.

                 Only tables that have been created, using the Tables interface, will show up in
          this list.
   Primary Field Name
   This is the name of the field, found in the primary table, that holds the primary key. As in our
   previous example (in Primary Table Name) we can see that the Cabinets.Cabinet ID is a
   unique identifier, so this would be the example that we would use here.

                 The primary field data MUST have a relational link to the foreign field data.
   Foreign Table Name
   This is the name of the foreign table. A foreign table holds a reference to a primary table's
   data. An example would be the Parts table in the report.mdb. It has the following fields:
 Cabinet ID
 Door ID
 Rollout ID
 Top ID
 Part ID
 Etc.
   These are all examples of references to other tables' records.

                                                              © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
                      Only tables that have been created, using the Tables interface, will show up in
               this list.
       Foreign Field Name
       This is the name of the field, found in the foreign table, that holds the foreign key. As in our
       previous example (in Foreign Table Name) we can see that the Parts.Cabinet ID is a
       reference to the Cabinets.Cabinet ID field.

                      The foreign field data MUST have a relation link to the primary field data.

    Add Variable

A variable is an optional place holder to store data that can be used in the report. The variable is
not linked to any table and can be used anywhere in the report.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Variables are dynamic bits of data that can be used to drive formulas in a report. This allows a
user to alter the function, style, or other items, of a report, without editing the report itself.

              There are default variables that are created by Cabinet Vision whenever you create a
       report. These variables do not need to be defined by you, the user, they will appear in the
       report regardless of any intervention on your part.
When you create a new variable, no dialog is displayed. Rather, the variable is added to the list
and you can alter it in the property panel on the right of the dialog.
       The properties of a variable are as follows:
     Name - This is the name of the variable, as it will appear in the report designer.
     Value - This is the value of the variable, as it will appear in the report designer.
     Type - This is the data type of the variable, this will affect how the report treats the variable.
       Name
       This is the name of the variable, as it appears in the report. It's how the variable will be
       referenced in equations and used to display information to the end user.
       Value
       This is the value that the variable has. You can use this value in equations, or just display it
       in the report directly.
       Type
       You can specify one of may types when creating a variable, the list is very large and includes
       (but is not limited to) the following types:
     Barcode
     Text
     Numeric
     Boolean
     Date
     Drawing
     RTF (Rich Text Format)

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Default Variables
       The following variables are created in the report without you creating them:
     KeyName - This provides the name of the key that is entered into your system. This is a
       'Text' variable.
     RunCounter - This provides you with the S2M Centers run counter, useful when you are
       creating S2M Center Reports. This is a 'Numeric' variable.

                      There are also 'Report Variables' that are created for the list and label designer.
               These are outlined in the designers help file. These are contained in the Variables -->
               LL folder.

Will delete the selected object.

When an Object is selected in the sidebar its Properties are available for editing in this area.

Sidebar

This area stores the Objects for your Report. Simply select the Object to Edit/View it's Properties
in the Property Pane.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
There are six primary Objects in the sidebar:

Properties

Set the basic properties for the report. Following are the Report Property options:
 Name - The Short Name of the Report.
 Description - The Description of the Report.
 Label Report - Establishes if the Report is a Label Report.
 Catalog - Establishes if the Report is a Catalog Editor Report.
 Estimate Materials - Establishes if Sheetgood Materials should be run through the basic

   optimizer (True) or if a general Sheetgood Estimate (False) should be performed.
 Part Graphics - Establishes if the report requires a Part Graphic.
 Pixel Width - The Width in Pixels of the Part Graphic.
 Pixel Length - The Length in Pixels of the Part Graphic.

Imports

Imports data from another data source into the report database. This is only required if you are
setting up a table of information that is linking data from an outside source. If no link is required
then there is no need to import, the data can be reported directly from an external source.

Tables

This a gathering of data from multiple locations that all have a 1:1 relation to each other. Multiple
tables can be setup in a report to show different types of data.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Relationships

A relationship is required when you have a 1:E between two tables. Relationships are slow and
should be avoided if possible. By establishing a relationship you can list multiple records from the
foreign table for each record in the primary table.

Variables

A variable is an optional place holder to store data that can be used in the report. The variable is
not linked to any table and can be used anywhere in the report.

Script

Allows the implementation of VBScript into your Reports. VBScript (Visual Basic Scripting Edition)
is an Active Scripting language developed by Microsoft that is modeled on Visual Basic. It is
designed as a "lightweight" language with a fast interpreter for use in a wide variety of Microsoft
environments.

You can use the built-in text editor for writing your script, but it is highly recommended that you
use some kind of Interactive Development Environment (IDE) to allow for Syntax Highlighting,
execution of the script and debugging. The scripts written for the stock reports were created using
Notepad++ (http://www.notepad-plus-plus.org), but there are a plethora of IDE applications that you
can use.

For information on learning VBScript, please refer to the following Microsoft website:
https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/t0aew7h6%28v=vs.84%29.aspx

Report Name Contents of Each Report Grouped by category

Review the list noting which Reports potentially meet your requirements. Use the Preview tool in
the Report window to view the presentation of each Report and further narrow your selection.

Use this as a reference in setting up the Report options that fit your needs. Each heading will be in
bold text, and followed by Report options for that heading. Look through the entire list before
beginning, as some Reports for some items are in different places.
