Pages & Directory
This area, when on the Pages tab, displays a thumbnail view of each page of the active Report.
Simply select a thumbnail to quickly go to that page.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
When on the Directory tab it will show any Groups within the active Report. Simply clicking on a
Group name will quickly send you to the page in the active Report that contains that Group.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Plan & Elevation Sheet -

Plan and Elevation Sheets are special reports designed for your Installers. They will have a
picture of a Wall Elevation, with a list of all the Assemblies that go on that Wall across the bottom
of the printout, as well as other Job/Room/Wall information. See the Plan & Elevation Sheet Layout topic
for more information.
You also have the ability to create your own Plan & Elevation Sheets which are stored as Templates
in the Drawing Library and can be retrieved by clicking the Change... button in this area.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
You can Print or send "To Drawing" either Plan or Elevation or both by simply enabling or disabling
their respective options at the top of this window. When both are selected you will see the the Plan
then the Elevation(s) for each Room printed in order before the next Room is printed.
To Print or send "To Drawing" a Plan and/or Wall Elevation sheet for one Wall in a Room, select
the Plan or Wall to print, and then click on Print or To Drawing.
To Print or send "To Drawing" multiple Plan and/or Wall Elevation sheets for only some of the
Walls in a Room; select the Walls to print with your mouse while holding down the "Ctrl" key, and
then click on Print or To Drawing.
To Print or send "To Drawing" Plan and/or Elevation sheets for all Walls in the Job, select the
"Entire Job" option and then click on Print or To Drawing.
To Print or send "To Drawing" Plan and/or Wall Elevation sheets for all Walls in a Room, select the
"Current Room" option and then click on Print or To Drawing.

                      By default CABINET VISION will place only Walls that have Objects placed on
               them in the list of Walls to Print. If you would like the ability to Print all Walls including
               Empty Walls select the "Include Empty Walls" option.

Transmit to Factory -
XTernal Link

This option allows passing of data to 3rd party or custom applications. You can have up to 5
unique Transmit to Factory Links:

 LinkCommand LinkCommand2 LinkCommand3 LinkCommand4 LinkCommand5

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
LinkLabel  LinkLabel2  LinkLabel3  LinkLabel4  LinkLabel5
LinkImage  LinkImage2  LinkImage3  LinkIcon4   LinkImage5

                      This topic contains information about modifying the WindowsTM Registry. Before
               you modify the Registry, make sure to back it up and make sure that you understand
               how to restore the Registry if a problem occurs. For information about how to back up,
               restore, and edit the Registry, click the following article number to view the article in the
               MicrosoftTM Knowledge Base:

               256986 Description of the Microsoft Windows Registry

An additional user defined button can be added to the sidebar in the Reports area. This button can
be customized to open and populate Report.mdf, open and populate ORD Files, or to Open 3rd
Party and/or Custom Applications. The feature can be activated by adding a LinkCommand string
value to the registry that is a statement to be executed when the button is pressed. The
LinkCommand string value should be added to the following Registry location:

HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Hexagon\CABINET VISION\CV 2025\Settings

It can contain one of the following variables: jobordfile, ordfile, ordxfile, user, reportdb, biddb. The
variables must be within {} as normal CABINET VISION variables. If the ordfile or ordxfile
variables are used, you will be prompted to save an ord/ordx file.

The button text can be set with a LinkLabel registry setting.

The image for the button can be set with a LinkImage registry setting. The image should be a
50px wide and 40px high .PNG file with a transparent background for the best results.

An example LinkCommand might be:

LinkCommand=notepad.exe "{jobordfile}"

This button, when clicked, would prompt you to save the Job File if it has not been and Saves an
ORD file with the same name and location as the Job file and then open Notepad with the saved
file...

notepad.exe "{ordfile}"

Another example might be:

LinkCommand=YourCustom.exe "{reportdb}"

This POPULATES report.mdf backs it up as report.sql then opens your requested EXE so you can

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
access the updated data. Report.sql is an SQL backup which can be restored and accessed.
Report.mdf can not be accessed directly as it is in use by CABINET VISION.

Another example might be:

LinkCommand=notepad.exe "{user}"

This opens Windows Notepad with the Login User Name for CABINET VISION.

Another example might be:
LinkCommand=YourCustom.exe "{biddb}"
This POPULATES BidData.accdb backs it up as BidData.sql then opens your requested EXE so you
can access the updated data.
There is another related Registry setting which can be entered here which will force CABINET
VISION to populate Report.mdf upon entry into the S2M CENTER.
CNCPOPULATEREPORT
A value of 1 turns this feature on.
A similar function also exists for the S2M CENTER adding the button in the output area.
HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Hexagon\CABINET VISION\CV 2025\Settings
OR
HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Hexagon\CABINET VISION\S2M 2025\

NCLinkComman  NCLinkComman  NCLinkComman  NCLinkComman    NCLinkComman
d             d2            d3            d4              d5

NCLinkLabel   NCLinkLabel2  NCLinkLabel3  NCLinkLabel4    NCLinkLabel5

NCLinkImage   NCLinkImage2  NCLinkImage3  NCLinkIcon4     NCLinkImage5

From the S2M CENTER you can run {psncdb} and {reportdb}.

Running {psncdb} will make a backup copy of the current PSNC-xx.mdf file as PSNC-xx.sql. You
can restore and attach to this SQL using SQL Management Studio.

An example might be:

NCLinkCommand=YourCustom.exe "{psncdb}"

              © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
This POPULATES psnc-xx.mdf backs it up as psnc-xx.sql then opens your requested EXE so you
can access the updated data.
You can also accomplish multiple tasks in a single line. For instance if I wanted to populate both
reports and cnc simultaneously I could do the following:
NCLinkCommand=YourCustom.exe "{psncdb} {reportdb}"

Available Scenes -

This section displays any views that have been sent "To Drawing" using the right click "To
Drawing" or "To Live Drawing" option. The list will also indicate the status of each scene. An

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
asterisk next to the scene means something has changed since in the view the Scene was shot
from. A check mark next to the scene means that the scene is placed on a Drawing Sheet. Two
recirculating arrows next to a Scene means that the Scene is a "Live" Drawing Scene.
Simply drag a Scene from the list to the Drawings area just like you place an Object on a Wall
from the Objects area.
You have two options to size a Scene which has been placed on a Drawing Sheet.
 Scale - See the Right Click on Scene-Page topic for more information.
 Grip Sizing - When selecting a Scene on the Drawing Sheet you will get handles at the corners

   and mid points which you can use to re-size the Scene. Utilizing this method will not produce a
   standard Scaled scene. However, once you get it around the size you want you can go to Scale
   and tweak the User Scale that is applied using this method.

              Once a Scene is placed in the Drawings Area you can double click the Scene to take it
       to the CAD area for notation.
There is also a Preview option in this area. There are three choices here:

None - Turns off the Scene Preview when selecting a Scenes from the Available Scenes list.
All - Displays a Preview for All (Live and Static) selected Scenes.
Only Statics - Displays a Preview for only Static Scenes.

Statusbar Menu

The statusbar menu gives you quick access to control the status of certain Drawing aids. There
are six possible options here:

Unit Selection or

Allows you to toggle between Inches (Imperial) and Metric Units on the screen. The Unit displayed
on the button represents the Unit of Measure that is currently active. You can turn this button On/
Off via the Preferences | Units tab.

Unit Precision

Allows you to select the Unit of Precision for the selected Unit. The Precision of the Unit selected
will be dictated by the Unit of precision last Set As System Default for that Unit and View in Units
Properties.

Reset Ruler

This option allows you to quickly remove any Snap Marks you have placed on your Drawing.

Snap to Marks

This feature allows snapping to a Snap Point set by use of the Ruler Tool. If this button is highlighted
in blue it means it is active simply click it again to disable it.

Snap Grid

This option turns the Grid display on. You will see a grid pattern in the window where you layout

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Jobs, edit Assemblies, or CAD that you can Snap to. If this button is highlighted in blue it means it
is active simply click it again to disable it. Go to Right Click Properties to set the Grid Spacing.

Snap to Points

This is perhaps the most useful tool when using the measure option of the Ruler Tool. Using this
snap feature allows precise snapping of dimension lines in CAD, and other precise placement
options. This option turns on the Dynamic Snapping functionality in Solid The snap to points appear
as small dark dots in the corner of the objects and all parts within the object. These are the snap
to points. If these points are present and not desired, reset the snapping mode to OFF or another
mode to eliminate them. If this button is highlighted in blue it means it is active simply click it again
to disable it.

      Snap Tips

     Use Ruler Points to place complex Peninsula Wall layouts
     Use Ruler Points for placing Assemblies, Parts, etc.
     Use Ruler Points to create Architectural Symbols for saving into your Symbol Library
     Use Ruler Points to draw construction details.
     Use Ruler Points to edit complex Assembly shapes.
     All of the CAD Functions in CAD can Snap to Points, Grid or Ruler Points.
     Use Grid Points to place items on the Grid.
     Use Points to measure distance on Assemblies, Parts, Walls, etc.
     Use the Points on an object to place Ruler Points

      CV Render Tab

                             The options here only impact the CV Render (Red Cube) Renders.
       Following are the options on the CV Render Tab:

               General - Outline Filled - With this option enabled CABINET VISION draws a black
               outline around all part edges.
Outline Filled = On

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Outline Filled = Off

            Enhance - Watch Enhancements - The Watch Enhancements option
            updates the screen as the rendering enhancements are performed
            using the Enhance option. If this option is not set, the screen will only
            update after the render enhancements are complete.

               Enhance - Enhanced Lighting - The Enhanced Lighting option will add lighting
               calculations for actual beam width, position, and intensity when using the Enhance
               option. The lighting settings may be set at the Lights option in the sidebar in a 3D View.
               Enhance - Dithering - The Dithering option adds a significant amount of processing
               time and is only helpful for close up rendering of Textures when using the Enhance option.
               This option simply applies some randomization noise to avoid the appearance of
               banding in Textures.
               Enhance - Anti Alias - This options allows you to smooth the jagged lines typically
               associated with Rendering when using the Enhance option. The farther right the slider
               the "smoother" the edges of the Renderings will be.
               Ambient Light - Brightness - Use this option to control the Brightness of the Ambient
               Light. The farther right the slider the "Brighter" the Ambient Light will be. The Ambient
               Light serves to set the base level of light of the scene. It evenly illuminates all surfaces
               in the scene, including the insides of cabinets. However, it will never cast shadows.
               Increasing its brightness will increase the overall illumination of the scene, as well as
               decrease the overall contrast. Setting the Ambient Light too high will make your image
               look flat.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Head Light - Brightness - Use this option to control the Brightness of the Head Light.
       The farther right the slider the "Brighter" the Head Light will be. The Head Light is a
       Light which always shines from your Viewing perspective (all other Lights move with
       the view's rotation.). Basically, imagine this as a Light shining from your computer
       screen onto the scene as this is what it simulates.

xRender Tab -

                      The options here only impact the xRender (Blue Cube) Renders.
Following are the options on the xRender Tab:

General - Auto Refresh - Automatically re-render if Properties have changed.
General - Light Geometry - A global switch to turn on/off light geometry, for light geometry
to show, it must be "on" both here and "on" in the light itself. See the Lights topic for more

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
information.

Render - Anti Alias - This setting defines the quality of sharp edges.
Render - Light Sampling - Reduces noise in direct light areas. The default value should be
sufficient in most cases. Increasing this value will significantly increase Rendering time and
may have no real impact on the Render.
Render - Reflection Detail - This setting determines the number of bounces a reflection
makes. A lower setting will only reflect off maybe one surface, with a higher value the
reflection will bounce onto more surfaces. The default value should be sufficient in most
cases. Increasing this value will significantly increase Rendering time and may have no real
impact on the Render.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Post Process - Image Editing - Enables the manipulation of the Post Process Properties
defined below in the sidebar after the Render is complete. This gives you a lot of control
over the final Render and is highly recommended when high quality renders are desired.

Post Process - Tone Mapping - There are four Tonemapping options:

· Clamp - No Tonemapping.
· Photographic - A Tonemapping setting derived from photographers' best practices.
· Neutral - A Neutral Tonemapping setting which does not change any input intensities.
· Exposure - A Tonemapping setting which multiplies the input intensities by the Exposure

   value.
· Exponential - Exponential tonemapping operator based on the average luminance in an

   image.

Post Process - Exposure - The exposure is a multiplicative term applied to the colors of
processed image during tone mapping. Increase the exposure to light up your tone mapped
image, or decrease it if you want to make it darker.

Post Process - Gamma - A non-linear operation used to encode and decode luminance or
tristimulus values in an image.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Post Process - Temperature Adjust - Enables/Disables White Balance.
Post Process - White Balance - White balance changes the overall mixture of colors in an
image and is used for color correction. HSL is an alternative color space to RGB. It is a
cylindrical-coordinate representation of color points.

Post Process - Brightness - This option allows you to increase (Brightness > 0) or
decrease (Brightness < 0) the image brightness.
Post Process - Contrast - This option allows you to increase (Contrast > 0) or decrease
(Contrast < 0) the image contrast.
Post Process - Burn - In a tone-mapped image, pixel luminances have been transformed to
the unit interval [0, 1] making feasible to best display it on any device. The pixels having the
biggest luminance (Lmax) in the source image are mapped to pixels having luminance = 1 in
the tone mapped image. However, sometimes it is desirable to reproduce some kind of
burning into the tone-mapped image. It's a way to reflect how some sensors can saturate
(e.g the eye) under too bright light. This is the purpose of the burn factor which expresses
how much of the range between [0, Lmax] will burn into the tone-mapped image.
Post Process - Sharpen - The Sharpen option is used for enhancing the definition of edges
in the image. The sharpen filter kernel size is 3x3 pixels.
Post Process - Glow - The Glow option is used for increasing the white areas intensity in
the image. The glow filter kernel size is 11x11 pixels.
Post Process - Blur - The Blur option applies a gaussian blur filter on the final image. The
blur filter kernel size varies from 1x1 pixels to 11x11 pixels depending on the slider position.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
   Background - Style - Select the Background Style from the following options:
 Plain- Renders the background color behind your scene.
 Graduated- Renders a gradient running vertically from background to foreground color.
 Image- Allows you to use a Bitmap image as the background.

   Background - Back - Select the Background color here.
   Background - Fore - Select the Foreground color here.
   Background - Image -Select the Background Image, if the Style is set to Image, here.

                                                              © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Image - Size - This option sets what pixel resolution the images will be rendered out at when
you use the Photovision to File options. You can use the pre-set image sizes, or set your
own by using Custom. The higher the resolution, the longer it will take to render the image.
Image - Width - If Custom is selected for Image Size then set the Custom Image Width
here.
Image - Height - If Custom is selected for Image Size then set the Custom Image Height
here.

     Save

The reference to an Object in Solid includes Cabinets, and other items that you save to your
library. Appliances, Cabinets, Closet Objects, Furniture, etc., are all objects. After creating a
special Assembly or other object decide whether this will be a desirable item to have available in
future Jobs. If this is a one time only creation, it is not necessary to save it as it will be saved when
the Job is saved. However, it will only be available in the Job it is saved with. If it is possible that
the item will be required for other Jobs it must be saved back into your library.
Save versus Save As

       Right clicking on the Assembly at either the Plan or the Elevation view at the Layout or
       Assembly Level, will provide a menu option similar to the one shown above. Note that there
       are two options under the "save" feature. It is important to understand the difference
       between the two options. In the simplest terms, Save keeps the new item in its new form at
       the expense of loosing the prior item (the pre-edit form). Save As allows for the creation of a
       new item. In effect, Save As allows for two items when finished, whereas, Save allows for
       only one. Save overwrites the original item, whereas Save As creates a new item in addition
       to the original one. Use the Save feature when you want a permanent change to an existing
       item or Assembly, and the Save As feature when you want the new item in addition to the
       existing one. Save As will allow you to rename the new item and place it in other libraries
       you may have made.
Features Common to Save and Save As

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The first option allows choosing of a Library by clicking on the Library Symbols in the left
window as shown on the above screen capture. Thereafter, if desired, the icon can be
changed by typing the selected name in the "Name" box at the top. The Description can be
changed to represent your Assembly. An Icon should be chosen from the list at the right that
represents the Assembly you are saving. This is done by clicking on the one of your choice.

Preserve Finish

This feature will save the item you are saving to your Library with any Finish overrides you
have applied to the Object or its Parts.

Preserve Height

This feature will save the item you are saving to your library at the Height you have edited it
to, instead of the default Assembly Height. If you have created an object that is of a different
Height than a default Assembly, it is advisable to select this option. You will still be able to
stretch or re-size it's Height after you bring it into a new Job regardless of whether you select
this option or not.

Preserve Depth

This feature will save the item you are saving to your library at the Depth you have edited it
to, instead of the default Assembly Depth. If you have created an object that is of a different

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Depth than a default Assembly, it is advisable to select this option. You will still be able to
       stretch or re-size it's Depth after you bring it into a new Job regardless of whether you select
       this option or not.
       Preserve Attributes
       This feature will Save any Attributes you have added to your Assembly either via UCS or
       Manually with your Object in the Catalog.
       Preserve Notes
       This feature will Save any Notes you have added to your Assembly either via UCS or
       Manually with your Object in the Catalog.
       Preserve CAD
       This feature will Save any CAD you have added to your Assembly in the Assembly Ortho
       Views and/or any CAD you have added to you Assemblies Parts in the Part Level Ortho
       Views with your Object in the Catalog.

The Closets Tab -
               This Tab allows you to specify Placement options for Objects with the Closet Class.
               This options will be activated/deactivated based on the Type of Closet Object selected.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       There are five main options.

       Snap Height to 32mm Increment - Used for Sizing Closet Classed Object heights in
       32mm increments. This option actually serves two purposes.
1. Enabling it denotes that you want the Objects Height to size in 32mm increments.
2. The Height Offset value determines any extra dimension to add to the parts size outside
    of the 32mm increment Height rule.

                      Example 1: If you enabled this option with a value of 20 and placed the
                      Object and gave it a Height of 1408mm you would get a 1428mm Height
                      Panel: 1408 + 20 = 1428
                      Example 2: You can also enter Heights that are not on a 32mm increment.
                      This option will evaluate the nearest 32mm increment so if you entered
                      1400mm you would also get a 1428mm Height Panel: 1400 = 1408 + 20 =
                      1428
       This option controls and sets a Parameter on the Object named SNAPH32.
       Snap Elevation to Increment - Primarily used to snap elevations of Horizontal Types
       to 32mm centers. This option actually serves two purposes.
1. Enabling it denotes that you want the Objects Elevation to snap on either 32mm or User
    Specified increments.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
2. Its value determines the bottom reference of the Object.
       Using this Option changes the Reference point of the Shelf to the Center of the Shelf.
       Thickness/2.
                      Example 1: If you were using 19mm Melamine for your Shelves Thickness
                      and you set Bottom Reference to 9.5; when placing the shelf you would see
                      this:

                      Example 2: If you set the Bottom Reference to 0 when placing the shelf you
                      would see this:

       This option controls and sets the Parameter on the Object named SNAPSHY32. If a User
       Specified increment is set it uses the Object Parameters SNAPTOOSET and
       SNAPTOINC instead.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
               Snap Door Heights to 32mm Increment - This option is used to snap elevations of
               Doors on 32mm centers. Snaps to the top of the lower shelf's position. This Option
               actually serves two purposes.
       1. Enabling it denotes that you want the Objects Elevation to snap on 32mm increments.
       2. Its value determines bottom reference of the Object in relation to the shelf below it.
               This option controls and sets a Parameter on the Object named SNAPDOY32.
               Snap Door Elevation to 32mm Increment - This option is used to snap Door and
               Drawer Heights to 32mm centers.
               This option controls and sets a Parameter on the Object named SNAPOP32.
               Stretch to Fit Doors and Drawers in Opening - This option is used to force Solid to
               Stretch-fit Doors and Drawers in openings. It can be set to Stretch in Width only, Height
               only, or both.
               This option controls and sets a Parameter on the Object named STRETCHFIT. Value is
               either 1(Stretch-Fit Width Only), 2 (Stretch-Fit Height Only), 3(Stretch-Fit Both Width
               and Height).

Selecting a Point on a Counter Top

When selecting a Point on a Counter Top you are presented with the following sidebar options:

 Start X - Sets the Start X for the selected Point.
 Start Y - Sets the Start Y for the selected Point.
 Build Up Joint Type - Will allow you to select the Joint Type (Build-Up Joint) for the selected

   Node/Point. There are six options here:

        Default - The Default Joint type as defined by the Counter Top Construction Method.
        Push - Configures a Push Build-Up as demonstrated by its image.
        Pull - Configures a Pull Build-Up as demonstrated by its image.
        Miter - Configures a Miter Build-Up as demonstrated by its image.
        Common - Configures a Common (one Piece) Build-Up as demonstrated by its image.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
        None - Configures a no Build-Up Joint.
 CNC Auto Radius - This function is very handy for creating your own Miter/Butt Joints. If the

   Point is set to Auto Radius as an Outside Corner the corner will be radiused to match the
   diameter of the Outline Tool. This will allow an Outside Corner to fit into an Inside Corner.

Selecting a Line or Arc on a Counter Top

       When selecting a Line or Arc on a Counter Top you are presented with the following sidebar
       option specific to Counter Tops:

     Edge - Type - Specifies the Edges Type. Following are the options here:

                      · Automatic
                      · Unfinished - This option allows you to specify an Edge on a Counter Top to be

                         Unfinished.
                      · Finished - This option allows you to specify an Edge on a Counter Top to be

                         Finished.
                      · Profile - This option allows you to specify an Edge on a Counter Top to

                         incorporate your selected Counter Top Edge Profile.
                      · Splash - This option allows you to specify an Edge on a Counter Top to have a

                         Splash.
                      · Butt - This option allows you to specify an Edge on a Counter Top to have

                         your specified Counter Top Joinery.

  Delete - This option will Delete the selected CAD object(s).

  Break - This option will allow you to Break a selected CAD object into multiple objects.

  There are three Break Modes:

                                                           © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
  Break into equal segments - Simply enter the Number of segments you need.

  Break into pieces with length - This option will break the Object into segments of a
  Length specified; with an Object at the end equal to the remainder.

  Break at location with length - This option will Break the Object from the Start Point
  at the Length Specified.

  Transform - There are four possible Transform options:

  © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

              Mirror - Will Mirror the selected CAD Object.
             Reverse - Will Reverse the selected CAD Object.

  Object.

               These options will not be available if the selected CAD Object is Connected. See
         Remove Connections below.

  Select All - The Select All menu option will select all CAD Drawn objects in the current

  the current View.

                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

     Render

If Render is checked, the Live Drawing Scene will display and print in the view's Render Mode when
it was taken (i.e. if it was taken in textured mode, it will display and print in textured mode). If the
view was in line drawing it will display and print in a non-concealed line drawing. If you are in
Filled or Texture Render Mode when you create the Live Drawing Scene, Render is automatically
checked. Otherwise it is not and Preview is checked.

     Preview

Preview mode allows quick display of your Live Drawing Scenes. Live Drawing Scenes have two
options "Preview" and "Render". Because of the nature of Drawing Scenes and how they are
presented a Render Scene can be very slow to process.

        a name.

   5. If you want to create a new Category, click the New Category button and the following
        interface will appear:

   6. Name the new Category and click OK to continue.

        the OK button to complete the addition of the new Symbol.

     Title Block

Allows you to select a Title Block from the Drawings Library and places it on the Page.

Title blocks may be edited or created, within the Drawings Library, so that your drawings page will be
bordered neatly and include important information about the Job and your Company. There are
several Title Block Templates that come with your installation of Solid. These Title Block Templates
may need to be customized with your information before using them. You may also create your
own Title Blocks using the Drawing Library.

              By default each new Drawing Sheet you add will automatically add the Title Block you
       have Set As System Defaults. To clear this out so your new Drawing Sheets are blank
       simply select the None option here and click OK.
If you change the Title Block, the drawing page will be updated with the new Title Block. This has
been made possible by putting the Title Block on its own Layer. Any CAD on the Title Block layer
will be removed and replaced by the newly selected Title Block.

                      Doors/Drawers

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Allows the selection of the Door Style and Material for Doors, Drawer Fronts, and End Panels
(Panelized Ends and Applied Doors) for the active Cabinet/Closet, based on it's Class (Upper/
Base/Closet).
The Door selection interface is designed to allow you to have complete control over the Door
Styles for your Cabinet with the fewest selections possible. The most important area in this
configuration screen is the All branch. With this you can specify the General Door Style, Material,
and Profile the majority of your Doors will be.

For instance, let's say I wanted to have a Cathedral Arch Door for my Upper Cabinets I would
simply expand the Upper Branch and select that Door Style and would need to make no other
changes. If you will notice in the image below I have selected the Cathedral Arch Raised Panel
Door Style for my Upper Cabinets. Also notice that instead of normal text the text is italicized, this
is way for you to quickly see that you have selected something that differs from the "All" selection.

Another example would be my Drawer Fronts. I would not do a Square Raised Panel for those but
a Solid Wood Drawer Front instead.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
You are also not limited to Style differences from the "All" selection as you can see in the Drawer
Front example above my Inside Edge Detail and Raised Panel Detail also differ from the "All"
selection. I could also choose an alternate Material for my Drawer Fronts as well.

              By selecting a Door Style for Base EP (End Panel), Upper EP, and Tall EP you are not
       necessarily, depending on Finished End type in the Construction Method, changing or modifying
       your Cabinets Ends, instead, you are selecting the style of Door that will be used only if you
       do select to have these ends on the Cabinet.

The Case Tab at Cabinet/Closet Properties has three main options:
 Top - Allows you to change the Properties for the Top of the active Assembly. You have five

   options:
    No Top
    Full Top
    Stretchers - Make sure you have a valid width dimension for Stretchers in your Construction

      Method. You do not have to have them as your default but they should have valid
      dimensions.
    Web Frame - Make sure you have a valid width dimension for Web Frame members in your
      Construction Method. You do not have to have them as your default but they should have
      valid dimensions.
    Gussets - Make sure you have Gussets configured in your Construction Method. You do not

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

 Bottom - Allows you to change the Properties for the Bottom of the active Assembly. You have

   two options:
    No Bottom - Removes the Deck/Bottom from the Assembly.
    Standard - Follows the Construction Method for your Deck/Bottom.
 Scribes - Allows you to change the Properties for Scribes of the active Assembly. You have
   seven possible options:
    Top - Sets the value for the Top scribe of the active Assembly.

                    Default Assembly

A default Assembly is an Assembly that has been reconstructed by CABINET VISION at the
Assembly Level, following the information you have entered in the Assembly Manager and Assembly
Parts Material Schedule for the Assembly in question. Additionally, the Assembly is absent features
such as Face configuration and Interior options. It is, in short, a box built exactly as you specified
when you setup the Construction Method that is effective for the Assembly. Another advantage is
that the Default Assembly sheds any unintentional overrides that may have accidentally become
part of the Assembly. In practice, it is probably a good idea to begin the process of sectioning an
Assembly into a unique configuration by first defaulting the Assembly.
Also note there are two options when Defaulting an Assembly. By default the Default Assembly
option will not Remove an Assemblies Shape or any user Added or user Modified Parameters. If
you would like them removed as well simply enable these options.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
After defaulting the Assembly, it will appear similarly to the Base Cabinet below.

As an example of how this may be used, assume a Wall Cabinet above the refrigerator needs to
have ends that extend to the floor. There are several methods to create this Cabinet, however,
using the Parts Adjustment menu allows an easy method to create the new feature. Because the
Cabinet is 69 inches off the floor, I need the ends to increase in length 69 inches. By placing that
value in the box marked "Height" for each End, Right and Left, I have increased the length of the
ends to 84 inches (69 plus the original 15). The result entering the value in the Height box for both
Ends is shown on the graphic below.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
              Hide Parts

Parts that are added to an Assembly by CABINET VISION that are a part of the Assembly
Construction Method are referred to as system Parts. Typically, system Parts lack a "delete"
feature for removal. The Hide Parts option allows hiding Parts by placing a check in the box next
to the Part to be hidden. To restore a hidden Part, re-access this option and remove the check
mark. Notice that the Parts are grouped. Check marks in the group will hide all Parts within the
group. If you want to hide only Front Toes, you would not benefit from clicking the Toe Parts group
as all Toe Parts would be hidden, instead, select "Front Toe" from the Toe Parts Group and limit
the hide to the specific Part you need to hide.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
              Please note that the keyword here is "Hide" the Assembly still reacts and is
       constructed as if the Part were still visible.

Side Selector Section View  -  Section Face

This Side Selector interface allows you to select the Side of the Assembly you would like to modify
in the Section Editor. In the image below the Assembly was edited in an Ortho View so that the
Top and Front of the Assembly were setup to have Faces. When Faces are defined on two
different planes it activates the plane selection drop down at the Top. In the View below we have
the End View selected so we can define the Top (Priority 1), the Front (Priority 2), the Back, and
the Bottom of the Assembly.

Face Priority Explanation

The face priority is the order in which the interior of the Assembly will be sectioned. It is done in
the order 1, 2, 3, etc. If you put in a Partition on Face priority 1 it will cut all the way through the
Assembly. If you then put a Partition on Face priority 2, the Partition will stop where it meets
Partition 1. If you change the priorities around so 2 becomes 1, then the old 2 will now go all the
way through the Assembly and the old 1 will stop where it meets the other Partition.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

Edit Shape -

After clicking the Edit Shape button the Shape Editor options will appear in the ribbonbar.
Click the options below for more information

When an Assembly is brought from a Catalog and placed on a Wall in a Room, it exists as a

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
standard Assembly or a shaped Assembly. Typically, the corner Cabinets, 45's and 90's are
already shaped Assemblies. The remainder of the Assemblies are standard Assemblies.
Understanding the advantages of both types of Assemblies allows for greater editing capabilities.
There are a few points to understand when defining the Assembly types, the more important of
which are:
 A shaped Assembly need not be "shaped" differently than a standard Assembly, although it may

   be.
 Every Assembly, shaped or otherwise, must have a minimum of one Face.

Shaping an Assembly (creating a shaped Assembly)

You must shape an Assembly if the Assembly requires an irregular shape. This shaping can be
done in any of the three orthographic views or it can be done at the Plan or Elevation view of the
Room level. The view that you choose to edit the shape from MUST be the view that represents
the unique shape. In other words, if you want to edit the shape of a the Assembly so as to appear
as a roll top desk, you would have to choose the orthographic view allowing access to the
Assembly from the side. There are a few tips and tricks that make the process easier to
accomplish.

              Always edit an object AFTER you have correctly sized it to it's final size. In many
       cases, resizing an object will trigger a refresh which can rebuild your Assembly to a default
       configuration. This is avoided by sizing the object to the correct size first. A matter of an inch
       or two will generally not have that effect on a shaped object, however, whenever possible,
       get the dimensions close.
There are several options specific to editing the Shape of an Assembly which should be noted.

Selecting a Point on an Assembly's Shape

When selecting a Point on an Assembly's shape you are presented with the following sidebar
options:

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

Constraints" on the Point. See the Constraints topic for more information.

Right Click Part -

Following are the options when right clicking on a Part in the Face, Plan, and End views:

     Copy

This option will copy the selected Part and allow you to place the copied Part somewhere else
within the Assembly.

     Delete

This option will delete the selected Part.
              This option will only Delete user added parts. You have two options for Deleting System

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Parts.
       1. (Preferred) Go to the Section Editor, and use the "Hide Parts" option. This adds

            parameters to the Assembly that keeps CABINET VISION from ever creating the Part in
            the first place on a rebuild.
       2. Add the parameter QTY with a value of 0 to the Part in the Object Tree. Doing this,
            CABINET VISION will create the Part on every rebuild, then apply QTY = 0 to it making it
            no longer display or go to CNC/cut-list.

     Replace

There are two options in the Replace fly-out:

  Import DXF Part - The only difference between using a DXF to replace a Part rather than

  simply importing a DXF is the selected DXF will conform to the dimensions and Materials of the

  Part it is replacing. See the Import topic for more information.

  Library Part - The only difference between using a Library Part to replace a Part rather

  than simply bringing in a Library Part is the selected Library Part will conform to the dimensions

  and Materials of the Part it is replacing. See the Library Part topic for more information.

  Save To Library

The Save To Library option allows you to Save the selected Part to a Part Library for retrieval later.
Select the Library from the list on the left where you want to save the selected Part.

                   © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Following are the options here:
 Preserve Finish - This option will Preserve the current Finishes assigned to the Part.
 Preserve Size - This option will Preserve the current Size of the Part into the Library. Without

   this option enabled when you use Replace with Library Part the Library Part would take on the
   sizing characteristics of the Part being Replaced.
 Preserve Material - This option will Preserve the current Material of the Part into the Library.
   Without this option enabled when you use Replace with Library Part the Library Part would take
   on the Material characteristics of the Part being Replaced.
 Preserve Attributes - This option will Preserve any Attributes you have added to the Part.
 Preserve Notes - This option will Preserve any Notes you have added to the Part.
 Preserve CAD - This option will Preserve any CAD you have added to the Part.
 Output to CNC - This option if selected will send this Library Part to the S2M CENTER when
   the rest of your Job is sent. If this option is disabled the Library Part will not be transferred to the
   S2M CENTER.

     Relate To Part

The Relate to Part option will allow you to add intelligence to a new or existing Part and relate the
selected Parts properties to an existing Part within your Assembly. In the following Exercise we
will add Intelligence to a Board relating it to the Top Front Stretcher. This Part could be used as a
Sink Skirt.
1. Select Top Stretcher to be the "Relate To" Part then select Part Length + 0.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
2. Select the X Position to be Part X Position + 0, the Y Position to be Part Y Position + 0, and the
    Z Position to be Part Z Position + 3.25.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
3. Select the X Axis Rotation to a Value of 0, the Y Axis Rotation to a Value of 0, and the Z Axis
    Rotation to a Value of -90.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The added Part is now Intelligent and as long as the Top Stretcher it is referenced to exists it will
as well.

    Edge Connection

The Edge Connection option allows you define which edge of a Part gets a Connection. Once the
Edge Connection option is selected you will be placed in Connection mode with the following 5
options in the ribbonbar.

·  Select - When entering Connection mode this tool is selected by default. Simply click on

   the edge you would like to apply the Connection to and then select the Connection to use in the

   sidebar.

             © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
   You can use Windows                         + Click to select multiple edges.

·  Select All - To quickly change all edges to a specific Connection select this option

   then select the Connection in the sidebar.

·  Remove Connections - Will remove Connections from the selected edge(s).

·  Set Connection - Will expose the Connection selector in the sidebar without

   having to select an edge first.

·  Reset Connections - This will remove any Edge Connection Overrides and

   revert the Part Edges to the current Construction Methods specifications for the selected Part.

Once you are through defining the Edge Connections simply click the Return        option to save
the new Edge Connection Properties.

    Edge Banding

The Edge Banding option allows you define which edge of a Part gets edge banded with which
edge band type. Once the Edge Connection option is selected you will be placed in Edgeband
mode with the following 4 options in the ribbonbar.

   Select - When entering Edgeband mode this tool is selected by default. Simply click on

                                    © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
  the edge you would like to apply the Edgeband to and then select its type in the sidebar.

  You can use Windows                + Click to select multiple edges.

  Select All - To quickly change all edges to a specific edgeband select this option then

  select their type in the sidebar.

  Remove Banding - Will remove Edgebanding from the selected edge(s).

  Set Banding - Will expose the Edgeband type selector in the sidebar without

  having to select an edge first.

It is important to note that the default values in the sidebar options are NOT representative of the
current Edge Banding on the selected Part. To use this function simply select which Edgebanding
type you would like and whether to Trim the Part for the edgebanding or not. It is also important to
note that ALL system edgeband is applied with Trim Part set to yes. So, it would probably be
desirable in most cases to set this option to yes.

Once the Banding and Construction options are chosen simply select any of the Part Edges you
would like these Edgeband properties assigned to. In the image below the Front Edge of the End
has been selected.

                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Note that the front edge is now Red which indicates an Exterior Edgeband has been applied.

Once you are through defining the Edges simply click the Return                                                  option to save the new
Edge Properties.

New Operation -

Adding an operation to the Part: To add a manual Operation to a Part, begin by clicking the New
Operation Button.
After clicking the New Operation button, you will see the new Operation wizard which will guide
you through the process of adding the new Operation. In the Face area, you need to select which
Face that you want the Operation to appear on. Generally, if you want the Operation to be on the
primary Face so that it gets cut out on the nest, you would choose the Back face. See the Work
Planes topic for more information.

In the Operation area, you will need to select the type of Operation that you want to add.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Following are the Operation types to select from:

 Dado - Allows the addition of a Dado to your Part.

 FastenLink - Allows the addition of a FastenLink Operation.

 Hole - Allows the addition of a Hole to your Part. A Hole is round and it's shape can not be
   altered.

 Intelli-Joint - Allows the addition of an Intelli-Joint to your Part.

 Line Bore - Allows the addition of a Line Bore or Line Bore series to your Part.

 Primary Blind Dado - Allows the addition of a Primary Blind Dado to your Part. A Primary Blind
   Dado is applied to the Primary Part and the Machining for it actually gets applied to the
   Secondary Part. This is very similar to an Intelli-Joint utilizing a Secondary Dado.

 Primary Clamex - Allows the addition of a Primary Clamex Operation on your Part. A
   Primary Clamex is applied to the Primary Part and the Machining for it gets applied to both the
   Primary and Secondary Part.

 Primary Dado - Allows the addition of a Primary Dado to your Part. A Primary Dado is applied
   to the Primary Part and the Machining for it actually gets applied to the Secondary Part. This is
   very similar to an Intelli-Joint utilizing a Secondary Dado.

 Primary Dove Tail - Allows the addition of a Primary Dove Tail (Male) to your Part. A
   Primary Dove Tail is applied to the Primary Part and the Machining for it actually gets applied to
   both the Primary (Male) and the Secondary (Female) Part.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
 Primary FastenLink - Allows the addition of a Primary FastenLink Operation.
 Primary Hole - Allows the addition of a Primary Hole to your Part. A Primary Hole is applied to

   the Primary Part and the Machining for it actually gets applied to the Secondary Part. This is
   very similar to an Intelli-Joint utilizing a Secondary Bore.
 Primary Line Bore - Allows the addition of a Primary Line Bore to your Part. A Primary Line
   Bore is applied to the Primary Part and the Machining for it actually gets applied to the
   Secondary Part. This is very similar to an Intelli-Joint utilizing a Secondary Bore.
 Route - Allows the addition of a Route to your Part. A Route can be shaped after being added
   in the Part Shape Editor.
 ALPHACAM Drawing - This Operation type will allow you to select an ALPHACAM Drawing
   that has been saved into the S2M CENTER Part Library to add to your Part. See the S2M
   CENTER Part Library Help topic for more information.

The Drawings Area

The Drawings View is a convenient feature for placing and scaling drawings for printing. In this
view, scenes that have been sent to drawings are shown on the list at the top of the sidebar.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
These scenes are dragged to the drawing page and positioned. The scenes may be scaled by
right clicking on them and then selecting the Scale option.

The above graphic is annotated to show the areas and processes in the Drawing View. Notice that
the Scenes on the current sheet in the lower portion of the sidebar shows "Paper" as a scene on
the current sheet. This references one of the two "spaces" that are in drawings. The concept of
"spaces" simply refers to what you are working in. If you are working in the paper space, as you

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
would when making symbols, etc. you are working in real, 1" = 1" scale. When you change to
drawing space you are in that drawing's private space. Any CAD you perform at that level is
relative to the properties of that drawing. As an example, you use the dimension tool to dimension
between two walls. In drawing space, the dimension would be the real world dimension based on
the scale the drawing was in. If the scale were such that the walls were 48 inches apart, the
dimension tool would provide 48 inches as the dimension. If you measured the same dimension in
paper space, it would provide the dimension as if you had measured the same thing using a ruler
on the paper.

Sending a View to Drawing

Most Views within CABINET VISION may be sent to the Drawings View for arranging and printing.
To send a view To Drawings, simply maneuver to the perspective that you want (i.e. zoom, pan,
etc, until the picture looks like you want it to look) and then right-click on the screen and click To
Drawing or To Live-Drawing in the menu that appears.

After following the steps above, when you go to the Drawings View, the view that you just sent will
appear in the Available Scenes area. Simply drag the scene out of the available scenes window
and arrange it on the paper as desired. To drop the scene when you are ready, simply click the
mouse. You may move the scene on the page after it has been placed simply by clicking the
scene to select it and then grabbing the bottom left corner to move it around.

Overrides

Overrides are simply changes made to an Assembly or a Part that require some value to differ
from the Material Schedule or Construction Method that originally defined it. Schedules or Methods can
have Overrides too. Overrides are beneficial when used properly, and dangerous when improperly
used. Overrides are limited in reach to the level at which they are created, therefore an Assembly
with a Part that has an override in Room 1, will have no effect on other Assemblies in the same
Room, or other Rooms. The problems come, if at all, when the Override is accidentally saved
back to your Catalog. If this is done, the Override remains as part of the Assembly, and this may
result in a Part or Parts not responding to future changes. There is a simple way to avoid this
problem, and that is to never Save an Assembly to your Catalog with an Override unless you
understand where and why you have created the Override and desire it remain.

Understanding an Override

You have spent time setting up Schedules and Methods that define how you choose to build
Assemblies. As CABINET VISION rebuilds your Assembly (as it does at certain times when you
make certain modifications), it looks to those Schedules and Methods to determine values for the
Assembly components. If it expects to find a value, for instance, 4 inches for the height of a Toe
Kick as you have set it in the Construction Method, and it finds a value that differs, it assumes that
you have made a change that you desire to keep. Therefore, the Toe Kick will never again re-size
to the 4 inches unless you remove the Override. If you had saved this Assembly back to your Catalog
you would discover that each time you pulled it from your Catalog, it would have a Toe Kick that
reflected the size you had changed it to, and not the 4 inches you have set in the Construction
Method. The real danger with Overrides is when they become part of an Assembly by saving it to
a Library, as they are useful as a method of changing a single Part of a single Assembly for use in
a Job.

Removing Overrides

There are two methods of removing overrides. The simplest is from the Assembly Level, Section
View. Select the option Modifications | Default Assembly answer the prompt affirmatively regarding
your intention to Rebuild the Assembly as a Default Assembly. A Default Assembly is a box, it

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
lacks Doors, Drawers, Shelves, and any other interior members it had. You will need to add these
Parts back to it, and re-save it to your Library overwriting the existing defective Assembly. The
second method is to select the Part that has the Override on it by right clicking on it from an
Orthographic view. Select Properties and then go to the Overrides Tab. You will see the Override if
it exists, in the window. Click on the Override you choose to remove, and click the Remove button.
The Part should return to pre-override behavior.

Creating Rate Tables

Step 1

Begin this process by identifying each area that you will want to include in your Bid. One area
might be for Cabinets based on Construction as was demonstrated previously. Then identify the
various Bid Methods available within each area that represent different pricing standards for your
shop. Each of these areas can cover items that may not always be present. An example is the Bid
above has no price for Molding because CABINET VISION did not find any molding in the Job.
You may want to add an item that costs more to make therefore, they need to be included in a Bid
when present in the Job.

Step 2

After identifying the items to be priced, have a clear idea as to the Rate Table for which they will
be priced and the amount that will be changed. Consider any surcharge that may apply as well.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Step 3

Review your plan. Does it cover the work you do, and allow for the different ways it may be done?
Time spent planning at this stage will greatly increase the usefulness of the Bid Center.

Step 4

Define your sub Rate Tables. Remember, when defining each sub Rate Table, the name you
assign it will appear on the "Rate Table Window" you will select it from, therefore, name it in such
a way that you clearly recognize what the Rate Table represents.

From the Bid Center, click the Rate Tables  option to get the Select Rate Tables area. Select

the "Setup" button to access the "Setup Rate Tables" area. There are two ways to create a new

Rate Table. If you are making a new Rate Table, as you would when making the first one for a new

group you are creating, use the "Create New Rate Table" button. If you are making a
subsequent Rate Table that is essentially like a previous one, consider copying the previous one
and renaming it, as well as changing the values of the pricing.

Work Planes

Work planes, will allow you to easily add operations to faces or edges of a Part without having to
think about positions and rotations. The front and back face of a Part can be considered face
work-planes and each edge of the Part will be considered an edge work plane. Face work planes
are numbered 1 for the front face and 2 for the back face. Edge work planes are enumerated in a
counter clock-wise direction from the shape origin on a shaped part or the bottom left corner of a
rectangular part. This functionality will not work on radiused edges.

The edge work planes are oriented by following the Part edges from the origin moving in a counter
clock-wise direction. The Y axis will be along the front face of the Part toward the next shape node
and the X axis will be from the front face toward the back of the Part as shown on the following
sketch.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
To position an operation on a work plane, create the operation as if it were in a normal Cartesian
(XY) coordinate system. The Z position and AX, AY and AZ rotations will typically be 0. The
operation can then be applied to an edge by specifying the edge work plane with an _EDGWP
parameter. The value will specify which edge to place the work plane on, eg: _EDGWP=3 will
position the operation on the 3rd edge. The operation can also be applied to a face with a
_FACEWP parameter, eg: _FACEWP=2 will put the operation on the back face.

There are also additional lower level parameters that can be used to get information about an
edge. The values returned are for the edges orientation and position in Parts space. One set of
parameters assumes the edge orientation as described for the work planes. The parameters are
as follows (# is the edge number):

_edg#x
returns the x origin of the edge
_edg#y
returns the y origin of the edge
_edg#z
returns the z origin of the edge
_edg#dy
returns the length of the edge
_edg#ax
returns the x rotation of an operation (work plane) placed on the edge
_edg#ay
returns the y rotation of an operation (work plane) placed on the edge
_edg#az
returns the z rotation of an operation (work plane) placed on the edge
_edg#miter
returns the miter angle of the edge
_shpedgcnt
Returns the number of edges a shaped Part has. It will return 0 if the part is not shaped. A bend
line or radius node count as 1 edge.

                      Arcs and Curves are ignored in the Work Plane counts and can not be
               referenced.

Understanding Intelli-Joints

Introduction

The use of Intelli-Joints creates a greater flexibility for construction methods designed for
CNC. However, with flexibility comes complexity. This is an advanced concept that will extend your
ability to use CABINET VISION to its fullest extent.

The Concept

 What is an Intelli-Joint? An Intelli-Joint gives a set of rules and functions to separate Parts that

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
   come together. The best way to define an Intelli-Joint is to give an example like this. When the
   two Parts come together in the specified manner (the Parts must either touch or be at an exact
   specified distance from or into each other in order to trigger the Intelli-Joint to be applied), you
   may have the Intelli-Joint place operations on either of the two Parts or both of them.

Primary and Secondary

 A union between two Parts creates a secondary and a primary. The primary dictates to the
   secondary the required Operations. The primary is the key Part that sets into or demands a
   place on the secondary. The secondary operations only exist because of the primary.

 When two Parts intersect; the primary is typically the Part that "butts into" the other Part. The
   primary's edge touches the secondary's face.

 For example a left End (secondary) and an Adjustable Shelf (primary) have joined together. The
   left End is the secondary because it contains the boring holes for the Shelf to rest upon. Without
   the Shelf the left End would not need holes, therefore it is dependent on the Shelf for its
   characteristic, making it the secondary.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
2-D Views for Intelli-Joints

 When you place a "New Part" in an Assembly it looks fine in one view but in another view it may
   not be positioned correctly. This is a crucial point to understanding Intelli-Joints. Don't take for
   granted that an Intelli-Joint looks like it is in the correct place in one view that it will be correct in
   all views. It is best to view the Intelli-Joint in 3-D or in 2 separate 2-D views to verify its proper
   location. This will be discussed further later.

X, Y, Z of Intelli-Joints

 Remember "Parts are Parts". Nothing has changed for Intelli-Joints. We will be describing
   Operations on the Intelli-Joint. The X, Y, Z positions of the Operations will be in reference to the
   Intelli-Joint.

 Picture a piece of two-sided tape. It has a rectangular building orientation. On that rectangular
   shape are objects.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Using Intelli-Joints

 Step #1 - Understand the joint requirements.
 Step #2 - Designing an Intelli-Joint.
 Step #3 - Placing an Intelli-Joint on a sample Part to verify it is working correctly.
 Step #4 - Placing an Intelli-Joint via a User Created Standard.

Example Intelli-Joint

 Looking at this KD (Knock-Down) Fastener notice that it has 2 separate holes. This piece of
   hardware serves as a perfect example of the need for an Intelli-Joint for CABINET VISION.

 The first suggestion for creating an Intelli-Joint is to draw it on a piece of paper. Draw all
   aspects of it. The hardware, the Part that it will be going into and where in the finished product it
   will be. Having the views drawn will allow you to visualize the Intelli-Joint much easier.

Design

   1. Access Intelli-Joints from the System Level and in the Part level. From the System
        Level select Intelli-Joint on the Main ribbonbar.

   2. Select the New option in the ribbonbar and name the Intelli-Joint KD Fitting.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
   3. Click the New Operation button in the toolbar.
   4. Name the operation Front 5mm Hole.
   5. Set it to Primary.
   6. Set it's Type to Bore.
   7. Set it's Face to Left.
   8. Set it's X Position to 1.5.
   9. Set it's Y Position to 1.25
 10. Set it's Depth to 1/4".
  11. Set it's Width/Diam to 5mm.

                       Since you cannot enter pure Metric values in the Intelli-Joints screen you must
                qualify a metric value with mm so it is properly converted.
 12. Set it's Rept. to 1.

   1. Change it's name to Front 15mm Hole.
   2. Change it's X Position to .125.
   3. Change it's Depth to .5.
   4. Change its Width/Diam to 15mm.
 Notice that the Operation is highlighted to help identify what you are working on and whether it
   is a Primary or Secondary Operation.
    Primary = Yellow
    Secondary = Blue
    Selected Item = Red

 Select the New Operation button.
   1. Name the operation Front Peg.

 Now you have completely described the Intelli-Joint.
 Go in and change the sample joints' width and height to see the changes. Be sure that as you
   modify the Intelli-Joint size that the operations are moving correctly.
 Before leaving the design section jot down what the ID of the Intelli-Joint is. This will be needed
   later when you create the User Created Standard to place the Intelli-Joint.

                                                                    © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Thickness of an Intelli-Joint

 A piece of tape has a thickness of "0" this would be an example of a butt joint.
 The Intelli-Joint has to span the gap between the two Parts exactly or the Intelli-Joint does

   nothing. If the gap = 1/8 inch then the Intelli-Joint thickness must = 1/8 inch.
 When designing an Intelli-Joint for a dado the Intelli-Joint would have a negative thickness

   equal to the dado depth.

The Shape Editor (In General)

The Shape Editor consists of several tools designed to allow editing of the shapes of Assemblies,
Parts, and Operations. All tools within each Shape Editor work the same, yet not all Shape Editors
contain all the tools shown. The Shape Editor will not appear until you are in the "shape edit
mode" for the object you are working on. Typically, a right click on the item produces a menu with
the "Edit Shape" option. Selecting this option will cause the Shape Editor to display.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The tools defined below are from different Shape Editors, and may not appear in all Shape
Editors.

                   Layer Selector

There are two options in the Edit Shape Layer selector:
       Shape - The default Layer and the one all Shapes must be drawn on.
       Construction - This Layer allows you to draw Construction/Reference Lines to assist in
       creating your shape.
                      Depending on which Layer is active some options in the Modify section of the
               ribbonbar may or may not be available.

        Select

This will change the cursor to an arrowhead and allow selection of lines, arcs, etc. After selecting
the item, you will be able to change properties by selecting the desired property off the list in the
side bar and selecting the item to apply it to. Lines can be moved, re-sized, etc. Text can be
placed, edited, as well as changing the font and font size.

                      When selecting an entity there are some Simple Constraint options in the sidebar
               for the entity. See the Constraints topic for more information.

      Select A Split - Part

       When selecting a Part Split the sidebar will allow modification of two Properties for it
       depending on whether it is a Horizontal or Vertical Split:
     Y - Allows you to modify the Y Position of a Horizontal Split.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
     X - Allows you to modify the X Position of a Vertical Split.

      Select A Split - Counter Top

       When selecting a Counter Top Split the sidebar will allow modification of one Property for it:
     X - Allows you to modify the X Position of the Counter Top Split.

           Select All

The Select All menu option will select all objects in the Shape Editor.

           Measure

This option allows you to Measure Objects without leaving a dimension on the drawing.

         Delete

This option will allow you to Delete the selected CAD Object(s).

             Delete Split

This Tool allows you to delete a Top Split or Part Split you have added.

           Delete All

This Tool allows you to delete all Splits on a Part.

             Transform

                      The Transform tools will only be available (not disabled) when selecting objects

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       which are not Constrained.

        Flip

This option will Flip the selected object. First select all of the CAD Objects you would like to
Flip using the CAD Selection Options.

Then click the Transform | Flip option in the ribbonbar.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
          Mirror

This option will Mirror the selected object. First select all of the CAD Objects you would like
to Mirror using the CAD Selection Options.

Then click the Transform | Mirror option in the ribbonbar.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
                 Rotate...

       This option will Rotate the selected object. You will see the following dialog box when you
       select this option to choose how you want to rotate the object.

         Offset

This option allows you to Offset a copy of the selected Object a specific Dimension. Simply click
the Offset option in the ribbonbar then select (Left Click) the CAD Object you would like to Offset.
You can enter the Offset Dimension in the sidebar...

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
...or drag your cursor the amount (distance) you would like to Offset.
In the following example, the chamfer line has been offset by ¾" and is being offset again be 2 ½"
as noted in the Offset field on the left. The dashed line parallel to the chamfer is where the offset
will land when the left mouse button is clicked.

       Crop

There are four Crop options in the sidebar once the Crop Tool is selected:

       Start X - The X Start point for the Crop.
       Start Y - The Y Start point for the Crop.
       Crop Type - You have three Crop Types available; Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon that
       determine the shape of the area being cropped.

       Crop Area - The Inside option will get rid of what is Outside the Boundary and keep what is
       Inside. The Outside option specifies that you want to keep what is outside the Crop

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Boundary and get rid of the objects inside the Boundary.

      The Inside option can be a bit aggressive as it will remove all Objects in the
current view if it is not inside the boundary. To keep this option from being so
aggressive you can limit the Objects that are affected by a Crop by selecting the
Objects first.

      Remember you can select multiple Objects by holding the        key on the
keyboard down as you click the Objects.

Bend

This option allows you to select a Line and turn it into an Arc by dragging it to Bend it.

Scale

This option is made available in the Molding Manager and Profile Manager when Importing a Bitmap.
This tool allows you to scale the Bitmap to fit the overall Thickness/Height of your Profile.

Align Image

This option is made available in the Molding Manager and Profile Manager when Importing a Bitmap.
This tool allows you to align the Bitmap to the Origin of your Profile.

       Horizontal Split

This option adds a Horizontal Split to your Part. This is very handy, because CABINET VISION will
not determine if the Part's length is too large to manufacture in a single piece, this will allow you to
instruct CABINET VISION where to split the Part for manufacture.

Vertical Split

This option adds a Vertical Split to your Part. This is very handy, because CABINET VISION will
not determine if the Part's width is too large to manufacture in a single piece, this will allow you to
instruct CABINET VISION where to split the Part for manufacture.

                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       Line

This option allows the creation of Lines to define the shape of your Assembly or Part. After
selecting and placing a line, the line properties window will display in the sidebar. Clicking on the
items listed in this window will allow modification of that item.

              Chained Line

This tool allows the continuous creation of connected Lines. Similar to the Polyline option in CAD.
            Line Box

This tool allows the creation of a Rectangle. Similar to the Rectangle option in CAD.

          Polygon

This tool allows the creation of a fully enclosed Polygon.

        Arcs

                  Arc By Radius
       This option allows definition of a point where a radius begins, the radius, and the degrees of
       radius. The first mouse click marks the center of the radius, pull the radius that you want
       and click again.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
A circle will appear with a radius line within it. Move the cursor and the circle opening
becomes an arc as you do so.

When you reach the correct position, a third click will set the arc at the selected point.

         3 Points Arc
This option lets you place two points to define the opening of the arc, and the third point
pulls the arc increasing the radius. A 3 Points Arc is very handy when you have three known
points to Snap to.
In the example below I want to create the Arc shown in red.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
       To begin I select the Arcs | 3 Points Arc option from the ribbonbar then Left Click the End
       Point (With Snap To Points on) of the first line.

       Next I Left Click the Mid Point of the second line.

       And the last and third point I Left Click the End point of the third line.

       And now I have the Arc.

Constraints

When editing the shape of an Assembly, Part or Route Operation, you have the option to apply 2D
constraints to the Lines and Arcs making up the shape that must meet critical design
specifications or exhibit different kinds of parametric behavior. Solid maintains these constraints
when you edit these objects. You can apply the following types of constraints:

Simple Constraints - These constraints are applied in the sidebar when selecting either a Point
or a CAD entity that defines a shape.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The other two types, if available, are in the ribbon when the Shape editor is active.

Logical Constraints - Let you maintain logical geometric relationships between lines and arcs.
You can apply these relationships between lines and arcs that belong to the same shape.
Dimension Constraints - Let you apply fixed dimension distances or angles between lines and
arcs within the shape to meet critical design specifications. You can control these dimensions via
Object Tree Parameters as well as UCS's.

              Dimension Constraints are not intended for detailing and dimensioning drawing layouts.
       See CAD Dimensioning for more information on adding detail dimensions.
Basic constraints are applied automatically by Solid as you shape your object.
Right clicking on the screen while in Edit Shape gives you a few options:

  Paste

  Select All

              © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
  Reverse Selection

  Auto-Constraints - Will apply all the Auto-Constraints you have setup.

  Remove Constraints - Will remove all Constraints from the Object.

 Properties
You can add your own Constraints by using the following tools:

Simple Constraints

Simple Constraints are available when selecting a Point or CAD entity.

Simply click on the little button associated to a selected entity to sequentially change its Simple
Constraints:

  - The position will be kept at the same distance from the left edge of the Object.
  - The position will be kept at the same distance from the right edge of the Object.
   - The position will be kept at the same distance from the center (Horizontally) of the Object.
  - The position will be kept at the same distance from the top edge of the Object.
  - The position will be kept at the same distance from the bottom edge of the Object.
  - The position will be kept at the same distance from the center (Vertically) of the Object.
NONE - The position will adjust proportionally to the Object Size.
There are two types of Constraints available in the ribbonbar Constraints Group.
