JavaScript UCS

General Usage

JavaScript Macros (UCS:JS) are a powerful alternative to the existing traditional UCS Macros
(UCS:M). This will give you much more power in coding a macro and even allow debugging with a
tool like Microsoft VS Code. UCS:M and UCS:JS can run side by side. There are some slight
differences in the implementation of UCS:M vs UCS:JS outlined below.

Already a UCS:M guru and want to learn UCS:JS?

The quickest way to learn UCS:JS is to start with the basics. When running the UCS Wizard you
can have it write it to UCS:JS.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
                There are many learning and reference resources on the web for JavaScript. One we
         recommend is JavaScript | MDN (mozilla.org)

For Each

In a UCS:M, the condition used to apply the UCS to an assembly/part is defined in the UCS code
using a "For Each" statement. The condition is evaluated during the UCS execution, if the
condition is met the UCS:M continues execution else execution is terminated.

          ;UCS:M
               For Each AS|FS Part

For a UCS:JS, the For Each statement is not defined in code but is a property of the UCS. This allows
CABINET VISION to process the conditions prior to executing the UCS:JS, if the condition is met
the UCS:JS is primed and executed else execution is bypassed.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Objects

In a UCS:M, the macro is executed on the current CV object as defined in the "for each"
statement. As CV is executing the UCS:M, it is able to relate the code directly to CV objects.
There is therefore no requirement to identify an object in the UCS:M as it is implicitly implied. The
UCS:M macros have a special Cab object to identify the current assembly.

;UCS:M

DX = 5                 ; Implicitly apply a value to the current object

If Cab.DX > 30 Then ; Use of the assembly object

For a UCS:JS, a JavaScript runtime engine executes the script. The runtime engine has no direct
knowledge of CV objects so in order for scripts to operate on CV objects, the runtime must be
primed with a CV object. The runtime is primed with 2 CV objects, the current assembly (_cab)
and current "for each" object (_this).

//UCS:JS

_this.DX = 5;          // Apply value to the current object

if (_cab.DX > 30) // Use of the assembly object

Public Variables

In a UCS:M, public variables are defined in code. These are automatically extracted and displayed
in the UCS Manager UI where the values may be edited.

;UCS:M

Public PUB_VALUE=4 ;Public Value

DX = PUB_VALUE

For a UCS:JS, the public variables are defined in the UCS Manager UI and not in the JS code. For
code execution they are defined as a JS var variable (see Variables below).

//UCS:JS

_this.DX = PUB_VALUE;

Variables

In a UCS:M, all variables are applied as parameters on the current object being processed. This
means that they can be used in any equations that may be used to define values.

                       © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
;UCS:M

MY_VALUE = 5

DX = MY_VALUE * 2

For a UCS:JS, standard JS var values can be used during calculations, but it is important to note
they are not parameters on the current object being processed.

//UCS:JS

var MY_VALUE = 5;

_this.DX = MY_VALUE;     // Valid assignment

_this.DY = 'DX + MY_VALUE'; // Invalid use of var in an equation

Using a JS var can have a big performance advantage. For example, if the result of a parameter
or equation evaluation is stored in a var, it only need be evaluated once instead of potentially
multiple times.

In the UCS:M below, a parameter evaluation occurs two times.

if ( DY < 20 )           ; Evaluate parameter 1

      ShowMessage(1);

else if ( DY > 50 ) ; Evaluate parameter 2

      ShowMessage(3);

else

      ShowMessage(2);

In a UCS:JS the code can be written so there is a single parameter evaluation.

var length = _this.GetParameterValue('DY');                          // Evaluate parameter 1

if ( length < 20 )

      ShowMessage(1);

else if ( length > 50 )

      ShowMessage(3);

                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
else

      ShowMessage(2);

Parameters

In a UCS:M, as all variables are applied as parameters, there is no difference between a system
parameter such as DX and a user parameter such as MY_PARAM.

;UCS:M

DX = 5

MY_PARAM = 5

For a UCS:JS, the JavaScript runtime has no concept of parameters so object methods must be
used to set parameters explicitly. The most common parameters have been defined as object
properties which are a shorthand method of setting the parameter value.

//UCS:JS

_this.DX = 5;                 // Property to set DX parameter

_this.SetParameter('DX', 5);  // Method to set DX parameter

_this.SetParameter('MY_PARAM', 5); // Methods to set use parameter

The same applies to evaluating parameters in a UCS:JS.

//UCS:JS

var dx1 = _this.DX;

var dx2 = _this.GetParameterValue('DX');

var my_param = _this.GetParameterValue('MY_PARAM');

Case sensitivity

In a USC:M, all parameters and objects are case insensitive, in other words upper-case and
lower-case characters can be used interchangeably.

;UCS:M

DX = 5                        ; All upper case OK

Dx = 5                        ; Mixed case OK

                       © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
dx = 5                          ; All lower case OK

If Cab.DX > cab.DY THEN         ; Mixed case OK

JavaScript however is a case sensitive language so syntax and objects must use the correct case.

//UCS:JS

_this.DX = 5;                   // All upper case property OK

_this.Dx = 5;                   // Mixed case invalid

_this.dx = 5;                   // Lower case invalid

If (_Cab.DX > _cab.DY)          // Mixed case invalid

if (_cab.DX > _cab.DY)          // Correct case

Even in UCS:JS, using an object Evaluation method to evaluate a formula, mixed case is
permissible as the evaluation of expressions is relegated to CV which is case insensitive.

//UCS:JS

_this.DX = 'dy / 2';             // Assigns an equation to DX so mixed
case OK

_this.Evaluate('(DX+dy)/2');     // Using CV expresion evaluation so
mixed case OK

Functions

UCS:M do not have the concept of user defined functions. In UCS:JS standard JS function can be
used to isolate logic into neat components.

function CalculatePrice(length)

{

   if ( length < 20 )

          return length * 1.5;

   else if ( length < 30 )

          return length * 1.85;

   return length * 2.25;

                          © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
}
var price = CalculatePrice(_this.GetParameterValue('DY'));
_this.SetParameter('PRICE', price, VAL_CURRENCY);

Data Structure

As mentioned previously UCS:M do not have the concept of variables and data structures as all
data is considered an object parameter. In UCS:JS, all the standard JS data and data collections
are available.
const size = new Map([

   [1, 'short'],
   [2, 'medium'],
   [3, 'long']
]);
function ShowMessage(key)
{

       alert('A ' + size.get(key) + ' part in ' + _cab.NAME);
}
var length = _this.GetParameterValue('DY');
if ( length < 20 )

       ShowMessage(1);
else if ( length > 50 )

       ShowMessage(3);
else

       ShowMessage(2);

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Example

UCS:M to adjust an adjustable shelf part width under a number of conditions.
;UCS:M
;Adjust Adjustable/Fixed Shelf
For Each AS|FS Part
If Cab.ConstID = AsmConstID('Frameless') Then

 If Cab.DX >= 25 Then
   If Cab.Type = ASM_TYPE_STANDARD Then
     DY += 10;
   End If

 End If
End If
Equivalent UCS:JS.
//Adjust Adjustable/Fixed Shelf
if (_cab.GetParameterValue('CONSTID') ==
_this.QueryID(ID_ASSEMBLYCONSTRUCTION, 'Frameless')) {

 if (_cab.DX >= 25 ) {
   if (_cab.TYPE == ASM_TYPE_STANDARD) {
     _this.DY += 10;
   }

 }
}
See the JavaScript Object Model topic for more information.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
JavaScript Functions

The table below represents "global" functions that are exposed in the CV JS API. Additional
function will be added based on user requests.

 Methods
 alert(string message)

Displays a message box with the given message
example:
var name = `John Doe';
alert('Hello ' + name);

string message          Text to display

Imperial(double value)

Convert a value to imperial (value / 25.4)
example:
var result = Imperial(32);

double value            Value to convert to an imperial value
Metric(double value)

Convert a value to metric (value * 25.4)
example:
var result = Metric(1);

double value            Value to convert to a metric value

A _cvMath API is available for exposing CABINET VISION internal math functions. These are
currently limited to conditional checks that are an issue because of the way IEEE floating point
numbers work. Because of the quirks of IEEE numbers, safe conditional checks need to be
carried out with a tolerance. CABINET VISION Internally uses a conditional tolerance of 1.19e-04

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
for parameter evaluation.

 _cvMath API Methods
 isEQ(double value1, double value2)

Determines if the 2 values are equal within the Epsilon tolerance.
example:

  var isequal = _cvMath.isEQ(5.12, 5.12);

bool                                 Values are equal, true or false
isGT(double value1, double value2)

Determines if value1 is greater than value2 within an Epsilon tolerance.
example:

  var isgt = _cvMath.isGT(5.12, 5.15);

bool                                 Value 1 > value 2, true or false
isGTE(double value1, double vlaue2)

Determines if value1 is greater or equal to value2 within an Epsilon tolerance.
example:

  var isgte = _cvMath.isGTE(5.12, 5.13);

bool                                 Value 1 >= value 2, true or false
isLT(double vlaue1, double value2)

Determines if value1 is less than value2 within an Epsilon tolerance.
example:

  var islt = _cvMath.isLT(5.12, 5.15);

bool                                 Value 1 < value 2, true or false

      © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
isLTE(double vlaue1, double vlaue2)

Determines if value1 is less or equal to value2 within an Epsilon tolerance.
example:

  var islte = _cvMath.isLTE(5.12, 5.13);

bool                                 Value 1 <= value 2, true or false
isZero(double value)

Determines if value is equal to 0 within an Epsilon tolerance.
example:

  var zero = _cvMath.isZero(0.01);

bool                                 Value = 0. true or false

JavaScript Object Model

Currently, only a single CV object is exposed in the managed API. It is named CVAsmManaged.
CVAsmManaged exposes properties and methods. The properties are shorthand methods for
getting and setting common parameters, while methods are exposed for more complex
operations.

There are a number of predefined numeric constants used for parameter types and object
properties. The constants can be used in conditional checking and method calls. For example...

if ( _cab.Evaluate('ConstID') == _this.QueryID(ID_ASSEMBLYCONSTRUCTION,
'32mm') )

                            CVAsmManaged child objects

GetChildren(string filter)

                            © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Return a collection of object tree children of the current object using a filter. The filter can include
wild cards ? and *. There can also be multiple filters separated by the | symbol.

Array.

example:

var result = _this.GetChildren('face|?c*');

For a basic cabinet this will return [Case, Face]

                                       CVAsmManaged child objects

_BOTHPINS

This is a parameter on the primary work plane that indicates when both the A and B pin should be
used (for Lockdowel). This is only for small parts or short edges. When you have a small edge,
you only have one primary connection, but you have two support pins. We have fixed this value at
192mm. (Any operation on an edge less then 192mm will use both support pins). We set the value
at 192mm since the total span of the operation is 64mm, if you were to put two on one edge you
would want a 32mm gap between them and at least a 16mm gap from the start/end of the edges.
(64+64+32+16+16=192). However, you might want to have control over this value so you can
adjust the equation on this parameter.

Type:         System and/or User Definable

                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Valid Range:  Unlimited

Applies To:   Primary Work Plane

Values:       Numeric (Measurement)

Visibility:   Visible with user override

_BRT

Specifies a Lights Beam Brightness.

Type:         System and/or User Definable

Valid Range:  0~100

Applies To:   Light

Values:       0~100 Specifies Intensity 0 being Off ~ 100 being Brightest

Visibility:   Always

Valid Range:  0~3

              1 = Show Plan CAD

_DPTH

Used to modify the position of Connectors.

Type:         User Definable

Valid Range:  Unlimited

Applies To:   Material

Values:       Numeric (Measurement)

Visibility:   Never

                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The hardware is centralized in a bounding box (blue) as defined by the depth "d" of the
hardware.

The "centralize" calculations do not currently take the shape of the hardware model into
account. In this particular example it is possible that the hardware could be moved slightly
more to the SE because of the clipped area (green) but as CABINET VISION does not know
what the model shape and dimensions are in the general sense, it is not accounted for.

Typically the hardware origin is specified on one of the part edges. The actual model
components are offset with their own equations. This means that CABINET VISION in effect
needs to situate the hardware as if it were on a rotated piece of material (green). CABINET
VISION actually calculates the position of the black dot to get the hardware to position itself
correctly.

The _DPTH Parameter can be added to the Material to modify the depth "d". This can be
used to adjust the size of the bounding box (light blue line above). Making the value smaller
would make the box wider, while making the value bigger would make the box narrower. The
hardware would always be centralized within in the box, effectively moving it SE in the above
example.

                                                         © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

Extends the Parts Bottom Edge by the specified value. Similar to EDX/EDY with two very
important differences: 1) Grows the Part but only on the bottom edge 2) Does translate to CNC
Machines.

Type:         User Defined

Valid Range:  Unlimited

Applies To:   Part

Values:       Numeric (Measurement)

Visibility:   Visible with user override

_EDGDIR

This parameter will be set to either 1/-1 depending if the edge direction an Operations is on is
going towards the assemblies point of origin. This is required for Lockdowel because on one edge
of the part CV needs Hide Pin A and on the opposite end CV needs to Hide Pin B. See
_BOTHPINS, _LDEDGEGAP, and _LDPINGAP for information on other Lockdowel specific
Parameters. Obviously these could be used for other purposes as well.

                            © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Type:         System or User Defined

Valid Range:  1 or -1

Applies To:   Operation

Values:       1 or -1

Visibility:   Visible with user override

_EDGDY

Returns the parent edge length of an object using the _FACEWP or _EDGEWP parameter. Either
the _FACEWP or _EDGWP parameter must be on the object for the _EDGDY to work. For
example if a dado is on the top edge of a part, it should either have _FACEWP=5 or _EDGWP=3
parameter. You could then set the dado DY as an equation DY = _EDGDY and the dado will
assume the length of its parent part's edge "3".

Type:         User Defined

Valid Range:  Unlimited

Applies To:   Operation

Values:       Numeric (Measurement)

Visibility:   Visible with user override

                            © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
_EDGLEXT

_NORM

Specifies the projection search limit on an Operation. By default CABINET VISION will not
evaluate (place) an operation unless physical Part contact occurs. This Parameter establishes a
Dimensional limit to search if contact does not occur. See below for more information.

Type:         User Definable

Valid Range:  Unlimited

Applies To:   Operation

Values:       Numeric (Measurement)

                           © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Example:  ;Modifies Guide and Hinge Boring
          For Each _DGVBORE1|_DGVBORE2|_DGVBORE3|_HPVBORE
          Linebore

            _NORM = .5 ;This sets a search projection of 1/2"
                                   ;So if the Drawer Guide or Hinge Operation
                                   ;Does not touch the Part needing the boring
                                   ;CV will search 1/2" before giving up

In computer graphics a "NORMAL" is a vector that is perpendicular to a surface. It is a directional
ray with infinite length. To control which objects are found when we use a NORMAL vector to
intersect with surfaces we have the "_NORM" parameter which basically specifies a length for the
vector. Any intersection point beyond the length specified by _NORM is ignored.

When a primary operation determines if it needs to create a secondary operation, it typically takes
the mid-point of the operation and determines if that point is coincident with a neighboring face
using an "is point on plane" test.

          © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
The operation test point is coincident with right end back face.

In some cases, the parts do not touch so the match becomes a little more complicated. In this
case CV projects a normal to the operation and intersect the ray with a neighboring face using a
"ray to plane intersection". Any intersection beyond the _NORM value is ignored. Currently, the
system accepts the first face found, keeping this value low is recommended in order to keep
unintended faces from being found that are potentially farther away.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

GROUP

Specifies the group the Operation is associated with. When the S2M CENTER processes
operations they are sorted by Group, Operation Type, Priority. Group and Priority allow you to
override the operation sorting for an individual operation. Let's assume you want to add a pocket
on the edge of the part, then drill a hole in the pocket.

Standard S2M CENTER operations are by default assigned to group 0.

                           © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
You would have to assign the pocket a group of 1 or higher...This will make sure it happens after
all the standard operations including outline.

If you then have your operation order set to Routing, then Drilling, you could also assign the drill to
group 1 since drilling would naturally follow routing.

However, if you have the normal setup (Drill then Route) you would have to give the Drill operation
a group of 2 (anything higher than the 1st group) this will ensure the drill occurs after the routing.

Operation Types, of course, are the four listed on the Ordering Tab in the S2M CENTER. See the
S2M CENTER Help file for more information on the Ordering Tab.

ALPHACAM        User Defined
Drilling        Unlimited
Routing         Operation
Outline         Numeric (Integer)
                Visible with user override
  Type:

  Valid Range:

  Applies To:

  Values:

  Visibility:

                © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.

              parts and will tilt out with a DOPEN > 0. Any DWR_OPEN that has any

Fastenlink

_FLPLUNGEDEPTH - Depth of tool at initial plunge before the ramp down

Public Variables

Overview

You have the ability to declare a variable as Public in a User Created Standard. This will allow for
easy editing of the variables values without modifying the UCS Code.

Syntax

Each public variable must be declared on a single line of code. The syntax is as follows:
Public VariableName[ ] [:]= DefaultValue [;Variable Description]
Examples:

       Public BSpacing = imp(32) ;Bore spacing
       Public Oversized := DX > 40 ;When is the cabinet oversized?

                          © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Modifying a Public Variable

Note the public variable declaration at the top of this standard.

These variables are exposed in the public variables property list on the left when that UCS is
selected.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
You can modify a variables value in the code or directly at the property list.

              Once you have modified the variable from the property list the modified flag in the
       database will be set. From this point on the variable will always get its value from the
       property list. A workaround for this behavior is to modify the variable name in the Code
       editor.

UCS Evaluation Order

This topic is a look into the way that CABINET VISION generates Assemblies and the order that it
evaluates parameters. Following are the basic steps that CABINET VISION goes through to
generate an Assembly:

1. The Assembly is generated according to the Construction Method and creates the Connection
    specified between parts.

2. User Created Standards are processed for that Assembly, it's Parts, and the Connections. See
    below for details about the way that User Created Standards are processed for an Assembly.

3. The parts are generated.

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
4. Relocate the parts.
5. Connector creates Operations.

    1. User Created Standards are processed for connection generated objects.
    2. Build the connection generated objects
    3. Relocate the connection generated objects
In effect this is a 2 loop process, in the below example, first all the parts and connection (Red) and
secondly for the connection generated operations (Green):

UCS Evaluation For a Assembly

When User Created Standards are evaluated for an Assembly, they are evaluated in the order that
they (User Created Standards) occur in the list of User Created Standards. UCS #1 is evaluated
for the current Assembly, then UCS #2 is evaluated for the current Assembly, etc.
Each User Created Standard processes the Assembly in Object Tree order. Children of a higher
branch will have a higher priority than the parent of a lower branch. For example, consider the

                                                                     © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
following fictional Object Tree:

In the above example, the Assembly Parts will be evaluated in the following order:
Part A 1, Part B 1, Part A 2, Part B 2, Part C 1, Part A 3, Part B 3

Add Line and Arc Routes

It is possible to add Line and Arc Routes through a UCS. Below is an example of a UCS adding
the different types of Route Operations.

;Adds a Line Operation            True
For Each RF Part                  True

       ;Adds Line
       Dim LIN as New Line
       LIN._FACEWP = 1
       LIN.Visible<bool> =
       LIN.DX = 0
       LIN.DY = 10
       LIN.DZ = 0.25
       LIN.X = 5
       LIN.Y = 5
       LIN.Z = 0
       LIN.AX = 0
       LIN.AY = 0
       LIN.AZ = -45
       LIN._RCUT = 2
       LIN.TOOLID = 5
       ;Adds Circle
       Dim CIR as New Arc
       CIR._FACEWP = 1
       CIR.Visible<bool> =
       CIR.DX = 8
       CIR.DY = 8
       CIR.DZ = 0.25
       CIR.X = 15
       CIR.Y = 5
       CIR.Z = 0
       CIR.AX = 0
       CIR.AY = 0

                                  © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
CIR.AZ = 0                   (Default)
CIR._RCUT = 2
CIR.TOOLID = 5
;Adds Counter Clockwise Arc
Dim CCARC as New Arc
CCARC._FACEWP = 1
CCARC.Visible<bool> = False
CCARC.DX = 10
CCARC.DY = 10
CCARC.DZ = 0.25
CCARC.X = 5
CCARC.Y = 15
CCARC.Z = 0
CCARC.AX = 0
CCARC.AY = 0
CCARC.AZ = 0
CCARC._ANG1 = 315
CCARC._ANG2 = 45
CCARC._RCUT = 1
CCARC.TOOLID = 5
;Adds Clockwise Arc
Dim CWARC as New Arc
CWARC._FACEWP = 1
CWARC.Visible<bool> = False
CWARC.DX = 10
CWARC.DY = 10
CWARC.DZ = 0.25
CWARC.X = 15
CWARC.Y = 15
CWARC.Z = 0
CWARC.AX = 0
CWARC.AY = 0
CWARC.AZ = 0
CWARC._ANG1 = 45
CWARC._ANG2 = 315
CWARC._CWARC = 1
CWARC._RCUT = 1
CWARC.TOOLID = 5

Add Non-Graphic Accessory

It is possible to add a non-graphic accessory through a UCS. Below is an example of such a UCS
(in red type). Note that the parameters that are available for the non-graphic accessory are the
same ones that may be added to a non-graphic accessory that is saved into a catalog (see picture
below).

;Adds a Non-Graphic Accessory to a Cabinet
For Each CAB Assembly

                           © 2026 Hexagon AB and/or its subsidiaries.
Dim Addon as New NGAcsry   Accessory'
Addon.Visible = False
Addon.Name = 'Non-graphic
Addon.Name = Addon
Addon.PRICE = 5
Addon.Weight = 20
Addon.DX = 10
Addon.DY = 15
Addon.DZ = 6
Addon.Upchg = 5
Addon.Cubes = 900
Addon.Labor = 45

Above is a picture of the parameters of an identical non-graphic accessory that was saved to an
Object Catalog.
